sprintengine-studio

v0.2.0

SprintEngine Studio design system: neutral two-tier selection, one accent reserved for the primary action, a 2px-grid spacing scale, and progressive disclosure of row actions.

Foundations

sem colors

sem.syntax.foreground{sem.color.text.default}syntax

Code syntax foreground ink. foreground tokens inside source code.

sem.syntax.comment{sem.color.text.muted}syntax

Code syntax comment ink. comment tokens inside source code.

sem.syntax.keyword{sem.color.mark.violet}syntax

Code syntax keyword ink. keyword tokens inside source code.

sem.syntax.string{sem.color.mark.teal}syntax

Code syntax string ink. string tokens inside source code.

sem.syntax.number{sem.color.mark.orange}syntax

Code syntax number ink. number tokens inside source code.

sem.syntax.function{sem.color.mark.blue}syntax

Code syntax function ink. function tokens inside source code.

sem.syntax.type{sem.color.mark.cyan}syntax

Code syntax type ink. type tokens inside source code.

sem.color.bg.app{ref.color.mist-100}surface

Root/page background — the canvas every panel sits on. Root and page background, the base layer of every view. Do not: Cards or raised chrome — use bg.surface / bg.surface-raised so panels read as elevated.

sem.color.bg.surface{ref.color.white}surface

Panel, section, and default card surface — one step above the app canvas. Panels, sections, cards — the default working surface.

sem.color.bg.surface-raised{ref.color.white}surface

Raised chrome: tab strips, inputs, popovers, drawers. Inputs, popovers, drawers, and other chrome raised above the panel surface.

sem.color.bg.wellrgba(32, 36, 40, 0.05)surface

A content well set into a reading surface: a translucent tint of the ink over whatever surface is behind it, so it separates from the conversation canvas, a panel, and a card alike. Code blocks and other preformatted source shown inside prose — content the reader is meant to see as a separate object in the flow, not as chrome. Pair with a border.subtle hairline. Also the groove of a segmented control (owner ruling 2026-10-01): a track is set INTO the surface the same way, and a tint rather than a solid is what lets one strip sit on a panel, a card or a popover alike. Do not: A control's own face, rows, hover or selection (those are bg.hover / bg.selected), and chrome raised above the panel (bg.surface-raised). Never stack a well inside a well: the tints add.

sem.color.bg.hover{ref.color.mist-150}interaction

Hover fill on rows, buttons, and list items — the only hover treatment (no shadow, scale, or glow). Hover background on any interactive row, button, or list item.

sem.color.bg.active{ref.color.mist-200}interaction

Pressed / active background. Pressed state background on interactive surfaces.

sem.color.bg.selected{ref.color.mist-250}interaction

Selection in the pane that currently has focus. The selected row of the focused pane or list. Pair with text.primary. Do not: A second simultaneous strong selection elsewhere on screen — every other pane drops to bg.selected-resting.

sem.color.bg.selected-resting{ref.color.mist-225}interaction

Selection in a pane that does not have focus — it remembers, quietly. The selected row of every pane except the focused one, so a three-pane surface has exactly one strong selection. Do not: The focused pane — that is bg.selected.

sem.color.text.primary{ref.color.slate-900}text

Primary content ink: titles, selected-row foreground, headings. Panel titles, primary content, selected-row foreground.

sem.color.text.default{ref.color.slate-700}text

Body text and default row labels. Body copy, row labels, field labels.

sem.color.text.muted{ref.color.slate-500}text

Secondary and supporting copy, meta text. Secondary copy, counts, meta rows, ghost-button labels.

sem.color.text.subtle{ref.color.slate-450}text

Tertiary ink: identifiers, de-emphasized meta. Identifiers, placeholders, tertiary meta. Do not: Actionable copy on its own — pair with primary text or an affordance.

sem.color.text.disabled{ref.color.slate-400}text

Disabled controls and empty-state copy. Disabled control labels, empty-state hints. Do not: Body copy — this step is below the AA body-contrast floor by design.

sem.color.text.on-accent{ref.color.white}text

Label ink on the accent fill. Flips by mode: white on the deep light-mode green, near-black on the brighter dark-mode green. Text and icons sitting on accent.primary fills (primary buttons).

sem.color.border.subtlergba(32, 36, 40, 0.10)border

Default panel/section divider hairline. Section dividers and quiet card edges — borders carry the structure, not shadows.

sem.color.border.defaultrgba(32, 36, 40, 0.20)border

Raised-surface divider, popover and input edge. Input borders, popover edges, clear hairlines.

sem.color.border.strongrgba(32, 36, 40, 0.30)border

Hover emphasis and structural separators. Hover-emphasized edges, structural separators, ghost-button borders.

sem.color.border.focus{ref.color.green-700}border

Focus ring color on every focusable primitive (green family, tracks the accent). Opaque: at the 0.55/0.6 alphas it shipped with, the 2px ring composited to 2.31:1 on light and 2.58:1 on dark against bg.app — below the 3:1 non-text floor a focus indicator has to clear. The 2px focus-visible ring on every focusable primitive. Do not: Resting borders or dividers — focus only.

sem.color.accent.primary{ref.color.green-700}accent

The single product accent — signature green. Selection and primary action share it. Primary CTA fill, active selection chrome, active-tab underline. Do not: Decoration, category coding, or a second accent hue anywhere in a view.

sem.color.accent.hover{ref.color.green-800}accent

Accent hover step: deepens on light, brightens on dark. Hover state of accent.primary fills.

sem.color.accent.softrgba(47, 106, 74, 0.10)accent

Soft accent fill for selected rows. Selected-row fill, paired with a 2px left bar of accent.primary.

sem.color.accent.soft-strongrgba(47, 106, 74, 0.18)accent

Stronger soft accent fill for selected-card emphasis. Selected-card border fill where soft is too faint.

sem.color.status.neutral{ref.color.gray-500}status

Idle / neutral status mark. Idle or unknown status marks (the ring with a bar) and inline status copy. Do not: Button fills, chrome tints, or category coding — status only.

sem.color.status.good{ref.color.emerald-700}status

Done / ready / healthy. Kept apart from the forest accent by brightness and saturation. Completion and health marks: the done disc with its knocked-out check, in rows and status marks alike. Do not: Anything decorative; never retune toward the accent green.

sem.color.status.warn{ref.color.amber-800}status

Warning / needs-input. Needs-input and warning marks. Do not: Button fills or chrome tints — status only.

sem.color.status.danger{ref.color.red-600}status

Error / blocked / failed; destructive-action fill. Error marks, failed states, destructive-button fills, invalid-field borders.

sem.color.status.merged{ref.color.violet-500}status

Merged-and-complete purple, constant across modes so 'merged' stays recognisable (GitHub-family semantic). Completed-and-merged marks, distinct from the plain green done.

sem.color.status.neutral-softrgba(100, 108, 120, 0.14)status

Soft neutral fill for banners and chips. Neutral banner and chip fills in inspectors and drawers. Do not: Default panel chrome.

sem.color.status.good-softrgba(21, 127, 55, 0.20)status

Soft success fill for banners and chips. Success banner and chip fills in inspectors and drawers. Do not: Default panel chrome.

sem.color.status.warn-softrgba(204, 132, 0, 0.20)status

Soft warning fill for banners and chips. Warning banner and chip fills in inspectors and drawers. Do not: Default panel chrome.

sem.color.status.danger-softrgba(220, 40, 40, 0.16)status

Soft error fill for banners and chips. Error banner and chip fills in inspectors and drawers. Do not: Default panel chrome.

sem.color.status.good-faintrgba(21, 127, 55, 0.10)status

The quietest success fill: a wash for a whole row that has finished while the person was elsewhere. list-row --finished: the row-wide wash a finished row wears. One step under good-soft, because a finished row asks for a look, not an answer, and sits beside rows that must stay readable. Do not: Chips, banners, or anything smaller than a row — those take good-soft. Never as a hover or selection fill.

sem.color.diff.added{ref.color.emerald-700}diff

Added material in a diff — the same value as status.good, spent on a diff channel rather than on health (ruled 2026-09-09). The app has drawn added lines and added-file marks in this colour since before the system existed; the token is where that value now lives. The ink of an added line, an added-file mark, or the A status letter, and the hue a renderer derives its added-line wash from. One set of four so Monaco's theme, a gutter and any future unified renderer read the same values. Do not: Health or success (that is status.good), a button fill, or chrome. Added-ness is a property of a line, not a state of the app.

sem.color.diff.removed{ref.color.red-600}diff

Removed material in a diff — the same value as status.danger, spent on a diff channel rather than on failure (ruled 2026-09-09). A deletion is not an error, and the shared value is a legibility inheritance, not a claim that it is. The ink of a removed line, a deleted-file name, or the D status letter, and the hue a renderer derives its removed-line wash from. Do not: Errors or destructive actions (that is status.danger). A removed line is not a failure and must never be read as one.

sem.color.diff.changedrgba(43, 108, 212, 0.14)diff

The wash under a CHANGED line in a diff: identity blue at 14%. Neither added nor removed — the line exists on both sides and reads differently — so it takes the one neutral-of-the-two hue rather than borrowing green or red. The row wash on a changed line in a side-by-side or unified diff. Derived from mark.blue so the two modes track the same hue the file glyphs use. Do not: A changed WORD inside that line (that is diff.changed-strong), and never as a hover, selection or status fill — a wash that also means 'selected' makes both unreadable.

sem.color.diff.changed-strongrgba(43, 108, 212, 0.34)diff

The wash under the CHANGED WORDS inside a changed line: identity blue at 34%. One step of the same hue, so word-level detail reads inside the line wash without a second colour. The inline word-diff mark inside a line already wearing diff.changed. Do not: A whole line (that is diff.changed), and never on its own — the strong step only ever appears inside the soft one, or it reads as a selection.

sem.color.overlay.scrimrgba(20, 24, 28, 0.42)overlay

Modal/dialog backdrop above panel chrome. A plain translucent layer — never add backdrop-filter to a full-viewport scrim. The backdrop layer behind modals, dialogs, and drawers. Do not: Combining with backdrop-filter blur — full-viewport blur re-renders every frame and tanks pointer framerate.

sem.color.mark.blue{ref.color.blue-600}identity

Identity blue. The mark colour of TypeScript, Python and Markdown file glyphs (ruled 2026-09-06). Ink of a file-type glyph whose language wears blue, and of a machine's glyph when the machine wears blue (owner ruling 2026-10-04); nothing else. Do not: Status (that is status.*), the accent, selection, text, borders, or any background. Never a category code on a control, a row, or a section; never on a glyph that answers an action, lifecycle or status question.

sem.color.mark.yellow{ref.color.amber-800}identity

Identity yellow — the same value as status.warn, spent on identity rather than warning. JavaScript, JSON and lockfile glyphs. Ink of a file-type glyph whose kind wears yellow, and of a machine's glyph when the machine wears yellow (owner ruling 2026-10-04); nothing else. Do not: Status (that is status.*), the accent, selection, text, borders, or any background. Never a category code on a control, a row, or a section; never on a glyph that answers an action, lifecycle or status question.

sem.color.mark.orange{ref.color.orange-700}identity

Identity orange. HTML and Rust file glyphs. Ink of a file-type glyph whose kind wears orange, and of a machine's glyph when the machine wears orange (owner ruling 2026-10-04); nothing else. Do not: Status (that is status.*), the accent, selection, text, borders, or any background. Never a category code on a control, a row, or a section; never on a glyph that answers an action, lifecycle or status question.

sem.color.mark.red{ref.color.red-600}identity

Identity red — the same value as status.danger, spent on identity rather than danger. YAML and Java file glyphs. Ink of a file-type glyph whose kind wears red, and of a machine's glyph when the machine wears red (owner ruling 2026-10-04); nothing else. Do not: Status (that is status.*), the accent, selection, text, borders, or any background. Never a category code on a control, a row, or a section; never on a glyph that answers an action, lifecycle or status question.

sem.color.mark.teal{ref.color.teal-700}identity

Identity teal. Shell-script glyphs. A hue of its own so a coloured glyph never borrows the success emerald. Ink of a file-type glyph whose kind wears teal, and of a machine's glyph when the machine wears teal (owner ruling 2026-10-04); nothing else. Do not: Status (that is status.*), the accent, selection, text, borders, or any background. Never a category code on a control, a row, or a section; never on a glyph that answers an action, lifecycle or status question.

sem.color.mark.cyan{ref.color.cyan-700}identity

Identity cyan. React and Go file glyphs. Ink of a file-type glyph whose kind wears cyan, and of a machine's glyph when the machine wears cyan (owner ruling 2026-10-04); nothing else. Do not: Status (that is status.*), the accent, selection, text, borders, or any background. Never a category code on a control, a row, or a section; never on a glyph that answers an action, lifecycle or status question.

sem.color.mark.violet{ref.color.violet-500}identity

Identity violet — the same value as status.merged, spent on identity rather than a merge. Stylesheet and image file glyphs. Ink of a file-type glyph whose kind wears violet, and of a machine's glyph when the machine wears violet (owner ruling 2026-10-04); nothing else. Do not: Status (that is status.*), the accent, selection, text, borders, or any background. Never a category code on a control, a row, or a section; never on a glyph that answers an action, lifecycle or status question.

sem.color.chart.1#077ef0data

Categorical chart series 1 (blue). The eight slots are one ordered set: the order is what keeps neighbouring series apart under protanopia and deuteranopia, so series N always takes slot N. Validated per mode: >= 3:1 against bg.surface on every theme of that mode, adjacent CVD separation >= 12 and normal-vision separation >= 18 (OKLab x100). A categorical chart series: the fill or stroke of the Nth series in a bar, line, area or pie chart, assigned in slot order and never cycled. Do not: Status (that is status.*), the accent, selection, text, borders, or any background. Never a series that MEANS good/warn/error (that series wears status.*), never re-assigned by rank, and never a ninth generated hue: a ninth series folds into chart.other.

sem.color.chart.other{ref.color.paper-500}data

The neutral for a chart's "Other" bucket: everything past the eighth series, folded into one. Grey on purpose, so the bucket never reads as a ninth identity. The fill or stroke of the folded "Other" series of a categorical chart, and of a series that is deliberately de-emphasised beside the ones being compared. Do not: A real series of its own, text, borders, backgrounds, or a status.

sem.color.scaffold.ink{ref.color.violet-500}scaffold

Ink of the chip that names something a chat is about to make, such as the extension-name chip on the New chat door (owner, 2026-09-30). Violet so it cannot read as the worktree chip beside it, which several themes draw in a blue accent. Glyph ink and the dashed empty edge of a name chip for something being made. Do not: A second accent on buttons or selection, status of any kind, or file-type glyphs (mark.violet).

sem.color.scaffold.softrgba(137, 87, 229, 0.16)scaffold

Soft fill of a named scaffold chip: scaffold.ink at 16%. Fill of a name chip for something being made, once it holds a name. Do not: Row selection, banners, or any fill that is not a scaffold chip.

sem.color.find.match#ffe9a8find

The wash behind every match of a find in text the app draws itself, such as Find in chat. Highlighter amber, the same pair the terminal's find decorations paint, so a match looks like a match in a chat and a pane alike; amber because no syntax ink, status mark or selection in the app is a background of that hue. Background of a find match painted over rendered text (a ::highlight pseudo-element). Do not: Warning or needs-input (that is status.warn), selection, row backgrounds, or any fill that is not a find match.

sem.color.find.match-current#ffc93cfind

The wash behind the match a find is on: find.match one step stronger, so the current match stands out from the rest without a second hue. Background of the one current match of a find, painted over rendered text. Do not: Anything but the current find match; never a selection or focus indicator.

sem.color.agent-trail.ink{ref.color.violet-600}agent-trail

Ink of the agent trail in the Files tree: the verb, the count and the agent's mark on a row an agent is at work on (file-tree component.md, Agent trail). Deep violet on light, light violet on dark, so it clears AA as 11px text on its own wash. The trailing group of a file-tree row an agent is reading or editing. Do not: Status, selection, the accent, a file's name (that is its git tint), or a file-type glyph (mark.violet).

sem.color.agent-trail.softrgba(137, 87, 229, 0.12)agent-trail

Wash of a file-tree row an agent is reading, and of a closed folder leading to one: violet at 12%. The row wash of the agent trail's reading state. Do not: Selection, banners, or any fill that is not the agent trail.

sem.color.agent-trail.soft-strongrgba(137, 87, 229, 0.22)agent-trail

Other tokens

sem.color.mark.project.lightness0.54identity

OKLCH lightness every project identity hue is drawn at (owner, 2026-09-11). The hue angle is hashed from the project's name at runtime, so it is the same on every machine; this and project.chroma are the parts that follow the theme. Measured over all 360 hues against every theme surface: 4.12:1 worst on the light tier, 5.83:1 on the dark. The L channel of the oklch() a project's folder glyph and its picker swatch are drawn in; nothing else. Do not: Any colour that is not a project's identity hue. Never text, status, the accent, selection, borders, or a background.

sem.color.mark.project.chroma0.09identity

OKLCH chroma every project identity hue is drawn at (owner, 2026-09-11): the highest at which every hue on the wheel stays inside sRGB at project.lightness, so no project is more saturated than another. Never zero, so a project is never black, white or grey. The C channel of the oklch() a project's folder glyph and its picker swatch are drawn in; nothing else. Do not: Any colour that is not a project's identity hue. Never text, status, the accent, selection, borders, or a background.

The one canonical elevation shadow, shared by drawers and overlay panels. Drawer and overlay-panel elevation — the only drop shadow in the system. Do not: Cards, rows, or hover states — structure comes from hairline borders.

sem.shadow.popover0 1px 2px rgba(16, 20, 24, 0.08), 0 4px 12px -4px rgba(16, 20, 24, 0.12)elevation

Elevation for trigger-anchored surfaces: popovers, menus, tooltips. Popover, ContextMenu, Select listbox, and Tooltip shells. Do not: Cards, rows, or hover states — structure comes from hairline borders.

sem.shadow.modal0 2px 6px rgba(16, 20, 24, 0.08), 0 16px 48px -12px rgba(16, 20, 24, 0.18)elevation

Elevation for centred modal shells sitting over a scrim. Modal and ConfirmDialog shells only. In dark mode the value leads with an inset top highlight — the lit edge — because a black drop shadow over a scrimmed near-black ground separates nothing; light mode needs no such line. Do not: Anchored surfaces — those use shadow.popover.

sem.shadow.toastinset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7), 0 1px 2px rgba(16, 20, 24, 0.08), 0 10px 28px -8px rgba(16, 20, 24, 0.22)elevation

Elevation for the toast card: a 1px lit top edge over a lifted drop, so the corner report reads as sitting above the page it floats over. The toast card only. The inset highlight is the control-raised light source (lit from above); the drop sits between popover and modal because a toast floats over live content with no scrim and no anchor to lean on. Do not: Anchored surfaces (shadow.popover) or scrimmed shells (shadow.modal).

sem.shadow.control-raisedinset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.16)elevation

The one highlight a control carries: a faint 1px lit top edge across the primary filled action, with nothing under it (owner ruling 2026-10-04). Tier 1 only — the filled primary and destructive buttons at rest. The inset highlight is the light source and the whole treatment: no drop, no sheen. The control presses by scale(0.97), not by swapping shadows, and a disabled one drops the highlight. Do not: Tier 2 standalone secondaries (flat, on a border.strong hairline) and tier 3 controls inside a surface (ghost, a hover fill only). Not overlays either — those take shadow.popover / shadow.modal / shadow.drawer.

sem.shadow.control-thumb0 1px 2px rgba(16, 20, 24, 0.1)elevation

The small lift under a segmented control’s selected thumb: a drop only, so the chosen segment reads as a piece set on the track (owner ruling 2026-10-04). A segmented control’s selected segment, over its bg.selected fill. No lit lip and no sheen. Reached through the app’s .control-thumb class, never spelled at a call site. Do not: A control a person presses to act — those are flat, or carry shadow.control-raised on the primary — the track under the thumb, or any surface that is not a thumb.

Inner chips (rarely needed). Small inner chips nested inside a rounded parent.

Cards, rows, buttons, and inputs in panel chrome. The default control radius: buttons, inputs, cards, rows — keep at most 2 radii per view. Sits on the same 7px step as radius.overlay so a control and the popover it opens share one corner.

Popovers and drawers. Popovers, drawers, and floating surfaces.

sem.radius.shell9pxshape

Large overlay and modal shells. Modal shells and the largest overlay surfaces. Do not: Operational chrome — larger radii are marketing-only.

The window shell's own inset cards. The window shell's inset cards only — the conversations sidebar, the workspace card, the side pane, and each terminal tabset inside the workspace card. One step above `shell` because these are the largest surfaces the product has and they read as objects floating on the window material rather than as overlays over a page. Do not: Anything inside a card. A panel, a control, a chip or an overlay stays on `shell` or below. Still under the 16px marketing floor, so it is operational chrome, not a marketing shape.

sem.radius.composer22pxshape

The New chat composer's box (owner ruling 2026-10-04). The composer box alone: the prompt field and its control row, as one rounded surface, in New chat and in an open conversation. A named exception to the radius ceiling (owner ruling 2026-10-04): the composer is the one surface a person types into all day, and a soft corner is what sets it apart from the chrome around it. Do not: Anything that is not the composer box. Not a card, a popover, a panel or a control inside the composer, which keep the ramp. Not a ramp step: a tool reading sem.radius.* as a ramp must exclude it, as it does pill.

sem.radius.composer-strip16pxshape

The bottom corners of the context strip tucked under the composer (owner ruling 2026-10-04). The bottom-left and bottom-right corners of the context strip under the New chat composer (machine, project, worktree, branch), which reads as one piece with the composer above it. Its top corners are hidden under the composer and take no radius. Do not: Any other surface, and the strip's top corners. Not a ramp step: a tool reading sem.radius.* as a ramp must exclude it.

The cards that sit against the composer and read as a set with it (owner ruling 2026-10-05). The tiles under the New chat composer (the suggestion and extension-idea cards) and the top corners of the tray docked on an open conversation's composer, where a question, permission or plan waits. Beside a 22px composer a ramp corner reads as a different family; this is the strip's 16px, one step softer than the box, so the set reads as one. Do not: A card, popover or control anywhere else, or inside the composer, which keep the ramp. The tray's bottom corners, hidden under the composer. Not a ramp step: a tool reading sem.radius.* as a ramp must exclude it.

sem.radius.pill999pxshape

Fully-rounded ends. An idiom, not a step of the shape ramp. Badges, status chips, switch tracks and progress rails — anything whose shape says "this is a marker, not a control". Referenced by liveness, which spelled var(--sem-radius-pill) before this token existed and therefore rendered square. Do not: Buttons, inputs, cards and rows — those take radius.control. A pill-shaped button wears the badge shape, and the two stop being tellable apart; the one exception is the composer's round send (owner ruling 2026-10-04). Nor is this a ramp step: it sits outside the 3/7/9 scale on purpose, so a tool reading sem.radius.* as a ramp must exclude it.

sem.motion.duration.fast120msmotion

Hover, focus, and small state flips. Hover and focus transitions, small state flips.

sem.motion.duration.normal180msmotion

Reorder and popover enter. Popover enters and list reorders.

sem.motion.duration.deliberate260msmotion

Drawer enter/exit. Drawer and large-surface enter/exit.

sem.motion.duration.pulse620msmotion

A one-shot attention pulse. Not a transition step. The single play of a change pulse — a count that just moved, a status icon that just flipped. Long enough to be noticed after the eye arrives, where a transition only has to keep up with a pointer already there. Value taken from the shipped .status-icon-pulse, which hard-coded 620ms. Do not: Transitions and state changes — those take fast / normal / deliberate. A 620ms hover is a control that feels broken. Never loop it either: the pulse means "this just changed", and a loop means "this is still happening".

How much of itself content keeps when it is set back so one region can lead — the code around a diff tour step. sem.focus.ring-offset2pxfocus

The transparent gap between a focused control and its focus outline. outline-offset, wherever focus.ring is applied. The gap is what keeps focus readable on a control whose own fill is the accent: color.border-focus and accent.primary resolve to the same hue, so a zero-offset ring on an accent fill has nothing to contrast against. Do not: A wider offset to make focus louder — the gap is spatial separation, not emphasis.

sem.focus.ring2px solid var(--sem-color-border-focus)focus

The single focus treatment: an outline drawn on :focus-visible at focus.ring-offset. Keyboard focus on every interactive element. Apply as `outline` on :focus-visible together with focus.ring-offset, never on :focus. An outline rather than a box-shadow ring: the offset gap is transparent and shows whatever surface is actually behind the control, where a ring offset has to be told that background and gets it wrong the moment the control changes surface. Do not: Hover, selection, or validation — focus is its own signal and never shares a treatment. Never at a zero offset, and never suppressed without a replacement.

sem.glass.blur12pxelevation

Backdrop blur radius of the glass surfaces — the toast card, the popover family's glass material, and the command palette's shell. Four kit shells and nothing else: the toast card (owner ruling 2026-09-04, a corner-sized area), the popover family's opt-in glass material (2026-09-07/08), and the command palette's shell (2026-09-10), which holds the terminal repaint pause while it is up so the blur beneath it is computed once rather than on every PTY chunk. Dark mode blurs a little more because the lighter glass over near-black needs it to read as a pane. Do not: Any scrim, drawer, menu, or full-width surface, and any modal other than the palette — blur over terminal panes re-samples every frame and was measured at ~10fps on a full-window scrim; the palette escapes that only by pausing the panes. The conformance lint pins glass to the four shells.

sem.glass.opacity0.8elevation

How much of bg.surface-raised the glass keeps; the rest is the page showing through. The glass shells' ground: color-mix(bg.surface-raised, glass.opacity) over the blur. Where backdrop-filter is unsupported each falls back to solid bg.surface-raised. Do not: Tinting any other surface translucent.

sem.glass.saturation1.14elevation

Saturation boost applied with the blur so what shows through stays lively rather than grey. Paired with glass.blur in the glass shells' backdrop-filter. Dark mode boosts less: near-black grounds have little to saturate and over-boosting shows as colour fringing. Do not: Anywhere glass.blur is not.
