Agent glyph

In a chat — the glyph beside the agent, its state in words

Explore agent· Map the routerWorking · 42s
Plan agent· Design the Agents panelDone in 2m 4s
general-purpose agent· Check the SDK exportsFailed after 9s

Everyday · Most of the year

Robot

Bubble

Balloon

Bear

Gent

Mushroom

Halloween · 1–31 October

Robot

Pumpkin

Ghost

Black cat

Witch

Skull

Christmas · 1–26 December

Robot

Elf

Santa

Reindeer

Present

A spawned agent drawn as a small character. While its agent works the character moves; when the agent ends it stands still and its face says how it ended.

It answers one question, *where is this agent*, for the agents a conversation sends off to do part of the work: a search, a plan, a review. It is the [liveness](../liveness/component.md) mark for an agent, and the one mark in the system that is allowed a personality (ruling 2026-09-28): an agent is a helper someone is waiting on, and a character they can recognise across a long run reads faster than a fourth identical row.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Glyph | .ds-agent-glyph | yes — a 16px SVG on the glyph grid, currentColor line work (1.4 stroke for the outline, 1.3 for detail) | | Character | .ds-agent-glyph--<character> | yes — which drawing | | State | .ds-agent-glyph--<state> | yes — working, done, failed, stopped or unknown; picks the ink and the face | | Moving parts | .ds-agent-glyph-whole, -eyes, -antenna, -string, -whiskers, -hat, -nose, -bow | while working — the parts a character's loop moves |

Variants

The characters come in seasonal pools. Each pool holds at least three, and the robot is in every one, so an agent is never a stranger.

| Pool | When | Characters | |---|---|---| | Everyday | most of the year | robot, bubble, balloon, bear, gent, mushroom | | Halloween | 1–31 October | robot, pumpkin, ghost, black cat, witch, skull | | Christmas | 1–26 December | robot, elf, Santa, reindeer, present |

The character is picked from the current pool by the agent's id (the id of the tool call that spawned it), so an agent keeps its face for as long as it is on screen and agents running side by side usually differ. The season follows the local calendar.

Each character moves in its own way while it works: the robot's antenna blinks and its eyes scan, the bubble squishes and glances about, the balloon drifts on its swaying string, the bear nods, the gent tips his hat, the mushroom squishes, the ghost floats and blinks, the pumpkin and the skull rock by candlelight, the cat's whiskers twitch, the witch's hat flops, the elf's hat flops, Santa bounces, the reindeer's nose blinks and the present hops.

At 16px one unit of the grid is one pixel, so every character keeps a clear face: solid eyes with room around them, and whatever says who it is (a hat, ears, antlers, a string) outside the face rather than on it. A ring round an eye, or a feature squeezed between the eyes and the outline, blurs into mush at this size and leaves no room for the finished faces.

States

| State | Ink | Face | |---|---|---| | Working | accent.primary | eyes open, moving | | Done | text.subtle | eyes closed, content (^ ^) | | Failed | status.danger | crossed out (x x) | | Stopped | text.subtle | switched off (- -) | | Unknown | text.subtle | as done — an agent from a transcript that never recorded how it ended | | Reduced motion | as its state | a working character holds still, eyes open |

Every loop also holds still while the window is hidden or in the background, and a transcript row pauses its own when it scrolls out of view.

Usage

  • On the row of the agent it stands for: an agent lane in a chat, a row of the Agents panel. Beside the agent's name and its state in words (Working · 42s, Done in 1m 29s, Failed after 9s), never instead of them.
  • One per agent. A glyph and a working mark on the same row is two marks saying one thing.
  • Not for conversations, terminals or jobs. Those are working [liveness](../liveness/component.md) marks; the characters are for agents a conversation spawned.
  • People can turn the characters off (Settings → Appearance). Then a working agent wears the working mark and a finished one a lifecycle glyph.
  • Never a status dot beside it (ruling 2026-09-28).

Accessibility

  • Decorative (aria-hidden) when the text beside it names the agent and its state, which is the normal case. Given a label it is role="img".
  • The state is never carried by the character or its motion alone: the words beside it say working, done, failed or stopped.
  • Reduced motion is honoured in the stylesheet: the class that animates is the class that carries the guard.
components/agent-glyph/component.css
/* Agent glyph — a spawned agent drawn as a small character.
 *
 * The drawing is currentColor line work on the 16px glyph grid; the state
 * picks the ink. While its agent works the character moves, each part on its
 * own loop; done, failed and stopped characters stand still. The motion lives
 * here with its reduced-motion guard, so a consumer cannot forget it. */

.ds-agent-glyph {
  width: var(--sem-icon-size-sm);
  height: var(--sem-icon-size-sm);
  flex: none;
  overflow: visible;
}

.ds-agent-glyph--working {
  color: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
}
.ds-agent-glyph--done,
.ds-agent-glyph--stopped,
.ds-agent-glyph--unknown {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
}
.ds-agent-glyph--failed {
  color: var(--sem-color-status-danger);
}

/* Parts turn and scale about their own box, so each keyframe names its pivot. */
.ds-agent-glyph * {
  transform-box: fill-box;
}

@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-float {
  0%,
  100% {
    transform: translateY(0);
  }
  50% {
    transform: translateY(-1.2px);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-blink {
  0%,
  90%,
  100% {
    transform: scaleY(1);
  }
  94% {
    transform: scaleY(0.1);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-look {
  0%,
  20%,
  100% {
    transform: translateX(0);
  }
  30%,
  55% {
    transform: translateX(1px);
  }
  65%,
  85% {
    transform: translateX(-1px);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-scan {
  0%,
  100% {
    transform: translateX(-0.9px);
  }
  50% {
    transform: translateX(0.9px);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-nod {
  0%,
  100% {
    transform: rotate(0);
  }
  25% {
    transform: rotate(-3deg);
  }
  75% {
    transform: rotate(3deg);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-rock {
  0%,
  100% {
    transform: rotate(-4deg);
  }
  50% {
    transform: rotate(4deg);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-squish {
  0%,
  100% {
    transform: scale(1, 1);
  }
  40% {
    transform: scale(1.07, 0.92);
  }
  70% {
    transform: scale(0.96, 1.05);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-antenna {
  0%,
  49% {
    opacity: 1;
  }
  50%,
  100% {
    opacity: 0.25;
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-flicker {
  0%,
  100% {
    opacity: 1;
  }
  30% {
    opacity: 0.55;
  }
  45% {
    opacity: 0.9;
  }
  70% {
    opacity: 0.65;
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-flop {
  0%,
  100% {
    transform: rotate(-4deg);
  }
  50% {
    transform: rotate(5deg);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-hoho {
  0%,
  24%,
  48%,
  100% {
    transform: translateY(0);
  }
  12%,
  36% {
    transform: translateY(-1.1px);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-wiggle {
  0%,
  100% {
    transform: skewX(-6deg);
  }
  50% {
    transform: skewX(6deg);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-twitch {
  0%,
  80%,
  100% {
    transform: rotate(0);
  }
  85% {
    transform: rotate(-6deg);
  }
  90% {
    transform: rotate(4deg);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-drift {
  0%,
  100% {
    transform: translateY(0) rotate(-2deg);
  }
  50% {
    transform: translateY(-1.4px) rotate(2deg);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-doff {
  0%,
  70%,
  100% {
    transform: rotate(0) translateY(0);
  }
  78%,
  88% {
    transform: rotate(-14deg) translateY(-1.2px);
  }
}
@keyframes ds-agent-glyph-hop {
  0%,
  60%,
  100% {
    transform: translateY(0);
  }
  70% {
    transform: translateY(-1.6px);
  }
  80% {
    transform: translateY(0);
  }
  86% {
    transform: translateY(-0.6px);
  }
}

.ds-agent-glyph--robot .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-nod 1600ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--robot .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-scan 1600ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--robot .ds-agent-glyph-antenna {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-antenna 1000ms steps(1) infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--blob .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-squish 1100ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--blob .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-look 2600ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--balloon .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-drift 2400ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--balloon .ds-agent-glyph-string {
  transform-origin: center top;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-wiggle 1200ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--balloon .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  transform-origin: center;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-blink 3000ms infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--bear .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-nod 1800ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--bear .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  transform-origin: center;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-blink 3200ms infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--gent .ds-agent-glyph-hat {
  transform-origin: left bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-doff 2600ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--gent .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-look 2600ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--mushroom .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-squish 1300ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--mushroom .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  transform-origin: center;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-blink 2800ms infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--ghost .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-float 1800ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--ghost .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  transform-origin: center;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-blink 3200ms infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--pumpkin .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-rock 1400ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--pumpkin .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-flicker 900ms steps(1) infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--cat .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-float 2000ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--cat .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-look 2800ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--cat .ds-agent-glyph-whiskers {
  transform-origin: center;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-twitch 2200ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--elf .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-float 1200ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--elf .ds-agent-glyph-hat {
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-flop 1200ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--elf .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  transform-origin: center;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-blink 2800ms infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--santa .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-hoho 1800ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--santa .ds-agent-glyph-hat {
  transform-origin: left bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-flop 1800ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--santa .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  transform-origin: center;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-blink 3400ms infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--witch .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-float 1800ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--witch .ds-agent-glyph-hat {
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-flop 1800ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--witch .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-look 2800ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--skull .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-rock 1400ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--skull .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-flicker 900ms steps(1) infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--reindeer .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-nod 1600ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--reindeer .ds-agent-glyph-nose {
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-antenna 1000ms steps(1) infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--reindeer .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  transform-origin: center;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-blink 3000ms infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--present .ds-agent-glyph-whole {
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-hop 1600ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--present .ds-agent-glyph-bow {
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-flop 1600ms ease-in-out infinite;
}
.ds-agent-glyph--present .ds-agent-glyph-eyes {
  transform-origin: center;
  animation: ds-agent-glyph-blink 3000ms infinite;
}

/* As specific as the character rules above and after them, so it wins: a bare
 * `.ds-agent-glyph *` is outranked by `.ds-agent-glyph--robot
 * .ds-agent-glyph-eyes` and left every character moving. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .ds-agent-glyph--working [class^='ds-agent-glyph-'] {
    animation: none;
  }
}
components/agent-glyph/component.html (demo)
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8" />
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
<title>Agent glyph</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../../foundations/tokens.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="component.css" />
<style>
  body {
    margin: 0;
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  }
  .demo-stage {
    padding: var(--sem-space-3xl);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-app);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  }
  .demo-label {
    margin: var(--sem-space-2xl) 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  }
  .demo-grid {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: var(--sem-space-2xl);
  }
  .demo-name {
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-xs);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  }
  .demo-faces {
    display: flex;
    gap: var(--sem-space-md);
  }
  .demo-face {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-2xs);
    margin: 0;
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  }
  .demo-face .ds-agent-glyph {
    width: 40px; /* ds-lint-allow: an enlarged specimen, not a layout size */
    height: 40px; /* ds-lint-allow: an enlarged specimen, not a layout size */
  }
  .demo-row {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
    padding: var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-sm);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  }
  .demo-agent {
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  }
  .demo-task {
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
  }
  .demo-time {
    margin-left: auto;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
    font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  }
  .demo-time--working {
    color: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  }
  .demo-time--failed {
    color: var(--sem-color-status-danger);
  }
</style>
</head>

Attachment chip

Review Unavailable
src/app.ts

A removable piece of context staged on a composer, shared by the launcher and conversation. Its neutral selected ground marks attached content without spending the primary action accent.

Anatomy

  • .ds-attachment-chip: inline wrapper, selected ground, chip radius, meta type, medium weight.
  • Optional leading glyph, followed by a truncating label.
  • A separate close button names the attachment it removes.
  • An inspectable label can contain a chip button opening a popover; removal remains a sibling control.
  • The file card (.ds-attachment-chip--file) is one button, .ds-attachment-chip-file-open: a preview square the height of an image thumbnail (.ds-attachment-chip-file-preview, the operating system's thumbnail of the file or its file-type glyph), then a caption of the name, cut in the middle so its extension survives, over the type in micro text (.ds-attachment-chip-file-type: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, Folder). The close button is pinned to the card's top-right corner.

Variants

Static label or inspectable label. Skills, @-mentioned files and folders use the same shape.

File card. A file attached by path — dropped, picked or pasted from the system — is a card, not a chip: it has something to show and something to do. The card shows the file (a thumbnail where the system draws one, the type glyph until then and wherever it does not) and opens it in the app the system picks for it. Only a kind of file that is shown rather than run opens that way — a document, plain text or data, a picture, a recording; anything else (a program, a script, a shortcut, an archive, a file with no extension) is only revealed in its folder, so the same click shows it in Finder or Explorer instead. A sent message shows its files as the same cards, without the close button; in a chat on another machine, whose files this computer cannot open, they are badges with each file's name.

States

The wrapper does not hover or focus. The close button and optional inspect control inherit the button and chip-button states, including focus-visible and disabled behavior.

Usage

Place attached context above the composer field. File cards share the image thumbnails' strip and row height; the consuming implementation is AttachmentFileCard in the same file, wired to the file by ComposerFileChip. Use neutral selected ground: a staged attachment is a selection. The consuming implementation is src/renderer/src/components/ui/AttachmentChip.tsx.

Accessibility

Removal is a separately focusable button labelled Remove <attachment name>. A file card's button is labelled with what it does — Open <name>, or Reveal in Finder: <name> where the file is only revealed — and its context menu (the pointer's secondary click, or the keyboard's menu key) offers Open and Reveal in Finder / Show in Explorer. Never nest it inside the inspect button. A truncated static label exposes the complete text through the shared truncated-text component.

components/attachment-chip/component.css
.ds-attachment-chip {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
  padding: var(--sem-space-3xs) var(--sem-space-sm);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-chip);
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
}
.ds-attachment-chip-label {
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

/* The file card: a file attached by path, with the system's own picture of it
   (or its type glyph) in a square the height of an image thumbnail, and its
   name over its type. The whole card opens the file; removal is a sibling
   control pinned to its corner, as on an image thumbnail. */
.ds-attachment-chip--file {
  position: relative;
  padding: 0;
  gap: 0;
  background: transparent;
}
.ds-attachment-chip-file-open {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
  height: 48px; /* the image attachment thumbnail's edge, so the two share a row */
  max-width: 220px;
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-xl) 0 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-chip);
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  font: inherit;
  text-align: left;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.ds-attachment-chip-file-open:hover {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-border-strong);
}
.ds-attachment-chip-file-open:focus-visible {
  outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
}
.ds-attachment-chip-file-preview {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  align-self: stretch;
  width: 48px;
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected);
  overflow: hidden;
}
.ds-attachment-chip-file-preview img {
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  object-fit: cover;
}
.ds-attachment-chip-file-caption {
  display: inline-flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  min-width: 0;
}
.ds-attachment-chip-file-type {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-regular);
}
.ds-attachment-chip--file > .ds-button {
  position: absolute;
  top: var(--sem-space-3xs);
  right: var(--sem-space-3xs);
}

Badge

Light — labels: the tone classifies the row, the ink stays readable. One badge per row.

MC-2117 · Component kit Merged
MC-2138 · Canon survivors In review
MC-2139 · Renderer tests Blocked
MC-2140 · Tracker write-back Failing
MC-2141 · Overlay geometry Draft

Counts — one digit is a circle, two grow it into a pill, and the figures are tabular so 9 → 10 does not shift the row.

3 12 99+ 4 2 1

Corner — docked to a trigger, with a hairline in the ground behind it so the count reads as sitting on the control.

5 12 7

Dark — the same two species, retuned by the tokens. The soft fills carry the tone; the ink does not change.

MC-2117 · Component kit Merged
MC-2138 · Canon survivors In review
MC-2139 · Renderer tests Blocked
MC-2141 · Overlay geometry Draft
3 4 8 99+
5 12

Status: shipped 2026-08-05 — src/renderer/src/components/ui/.

The small display-only label or count chip: a tone-carrying word ("draft", "merged") or a number docked on a row or a control. "Badge" appears across 10+ files today (BacklogRow, WorkspaceActions, PanelSwitches, ThirdPartyModuleList, NotificationsPopover, …) as ad-hoc rounded spans, with count-badge styling reinvented per surface. This entry replaces those with one primitive: font.size.micro/meta type on radius.chip, tones drawn from the status.*-soft fills with their matching ink, never interactive, and never a second status idiom beside a status mark that already says the same thing.

As shipped

Two species under one name, because the audit found two:

| | Shape | Fill | Ink | |---|---|---|---| | Count | circle at one digit, pill beyond | solid tone.* | text.on-accent | | Label | pill | tone.*-soft with a tone.* hairline | text.muted |

tabular-nums on counts, so 1 → 2 does not jog the row. A max caps the number ("99+") rather than letting the badge widen past its trigger.

Ruling — radius is pill, not radius.chip. The intent above said radius.chip (3px); every badge actually shipping is rounded-full, and a one-digit counter has to be a circle for the docked corner position to read as a badge rather than a clipped square. radius.chip is the right token for a *rectangular* chip; this is not one.

Ruling — a count's ink is text.on-accent, not bg.app. All three shipped counters hardcoded bg.app as their foreground, which is only legible while the badge sits on a saturated tone. text.on-accent is the token that means "foreground for a filled surface" and holds on every theme.

Corner mode docks the badge to the top-right of a positioned trigger with a 1px border in the surface behind it, so it reads as sitting *on* the control. A box-shadow ring would hold the box at exactly 16px, but the token lint's no-glow-shadow rule forbids that spelling — and every counter this replaces already used a border.

Never interactive, and never a second status idiom beside a status-dot mark that already says the same thing. A badge carrying meaning takes an ariaLabel (a bare "3" tells a screen reader nothing); one that merely repeats adjacent text is marked decorative so it is not read twice.

On the app rail (2026-09-07) the corner count reports unread activity: each section square wears the number of things in its area the person has not seen or that are waiting on them (principles.md, "The app rail", item 8). It is named, never decorative — nothing beside a glyph says what the number is — and its ring is the rail's own bg.canvas, since the square sits on the canvas rather than the app ground the default ring assumes.

On a drawer row (2026-09-08) the same counter is the row's unread pip: the Extensions drawer's rows each wear the news that belongs to them, trailing the label when the column is expanded and docked on the icon's corner — ringed in bg.canvas, the column's ground — when it is collapsed. It replaces the row's status mark while it shows (one status idiom per surface; the count is the one that says how much), and its accessible name carries the row's name and what is counted ("Design: 2 new"), because the row beside it names a place, not the news. The app rail's square above the drawer is the sum of its rows: same primitive, same tone precedence, and the two cannot disagree because one derivation feeds both (principles.md, "The app rail", item 9).

On a list row's mark (2026-09-10) the same corner count is the row's own pip: a plugin installed at a commit its source has moved past (and, until 2026-09-25, an agent CLI behind its published version — see "In Settings" below for where that one went). The number is usually 1, and on a row that is the point — a rail square's count is a quantity, a row's is a pointer, and the number is what makes it a pip rather than one more status colour. It replaces the row's health mark rather than joining it (provider-row, "One status idiom"): the owner opened a list of ten agent CLIs from an update notification and could not tell which row it was about, because all ten rows wore the same green health mark. Its ring is bg.surface, the ground those lists sit on, and its accessible name carries the row's name and the version it is behind ("Codex — update available: 0.153.4").

On a tab (2026-09-10) it is the same pip again, docked top-right of the tab and counting what is waiting INSIDE: "3 updates available" before the tab is opened, with a pip on each row underneath saying which. It is not the tab's count — that is how many things the tab holds and rides beside the label in the reading line; this is how many of them want the person, and it sits above the words because it is not part of them. On a tab the count is docked by the strip in reserved trailing padding rather than overhanging the way --corner does, because a tab strip scrolls inside an overflow container that clips anything hanging past the edge — and it needs no keyline there, since it covers the band rather than a glyph.

In Settings (owner ruling 2026-09-25) the same count marks an update waiting to be installed — an agent CLI behind its published release, or a newer SprintEngine Studio — from wherever the person is, down to the control that installs it:

| Where | Counts | Drawn as | |---|---|---| | The Settings gear at the app rail's foot | every outstanding update | --corner, ringed in bg.canvas like a rail square ("2 updates available") | | General in the Settings nav | the app update | trailing the label, as a drawer row wears its count ("Update available") | | Agents in the Settings nav | the CLI updates | trailing the label ("2 CLI updates available") | | A machine's segment on the Agents switcher | that machine's CLI updates | trailing the segment's label (segmented-control, "Badged segment") | | A CLI's row | that CLI | beside its Update button, not on the mark ("Codex — update available: 0.41.0") |

One derivation feeds all five, so the gear, the nav, the switcher and the rows cannot disagree about how many there are. Every one is the accent tone — plain news, the tone the rail gives news — and every one is named, so the number is never the whole message and colour is never the only signal.

On the CLI row the count sits beside the button that answers it rather than on the mark: the row wears one count, next to the one thing that clears it, and a person who arrived from the gear follows the number to the action. It still replaces the row's health mark (provider-row, "One status idiom").

The app update's count holds through every step update-service reports — available, downloading, downloaded, installing — and through a download that failed (the update is still there to take, and General's version row offers Download again); it goes when the new build starts and reports nothing waiting. General's count says which question is open: "Update available", then "Update ready to install".

An update stops being counted when it installs, or when the person dismisses it — Later or Dismiss on its toast (the toast entry, "Dismissing an update is 'not now'"). A dismissal names one version, so the next release is counted again; and it takes only the badges — the Update button and the version line stay, because the update is still there to take. A tab or nav row whose count is showing names itself with the count in it ("Agents, 2 CLI updates available"), the same call the tab strip makes: the count is a named live region, and inside the button it would otherwise land in the name twice.

Only a count is a live region (2026-09-02)

The two species announce differently, and this is the part a consumer gets wrong in both directions.

  • Count — role="status", so a value changing in place beside its trigger (the attention bell) is announced. This is what an announcement is *for*: the number moved while the reader was elsewhere.
  • Label — never a live region. role="img" when it carries an ariaLabel (a bare <span> has no role for the name to hang on), plain text otherwise.

The audit found the label species emitting role="status", which turned a hundred-row skill listing into a hundred polite live regions that re-announced every time the list narrowed. The fix belongs here rather than at the call sites: marking those chips decorative would have silenced them, and decorative means "the adjacent text already says this" — it is not a mute button. Used as one it hides a fact nothing else states, which the same audit found at three settings rows whose chip was the only thing saying a module was unavailable or that a row was a skill rather than a server.

The New mark (2026-09-08)

A third, narrower drawing under the same name: a pill saying a thing arrived recently. accent.primary ink on accent.primary-soft, font.size.micro at medium weight, radius.pill, and — the part that separates it from the label species — no hairline. A border would make it read as a state chip, and this is not a state: it is the system pointing at something, which is the one job accent.primary has. It is the entire accent spend on the row that carries it.

Three surfaces wear it and they must not diverge, which is why it is one shipped component (src/renderer/src/components/ui/NewChip.tsx) rather than a span in each: the CLI model picker marks a model the hosted feed released inside its thirty-day window, the Design door marks a component, pattern, glyph or foundations file that arrived in a bundle since the person last opened it, and (2026-09-08) the Extensions home marks a hosted card published since the home was last open — the cards the app rail's square was counting, still marked when the person arrives. The window is literally the same constant.

  • Never a hoist and never a sort key. The row stays exactly where its list put it; the chip is the only difference, so a muscle-memory pick still lands.
  • It expires. Both consumers stop drawing it on their own — the feed window passes, or the visit is stamped and the next open is clean. A mark that never clears is decoration.
  • It is plain text in reading order, immediately after the name it qualifies, so a screen reader hears "command-palette, New". Where the row's own accessible name is written by hand (a tile whose aria-label composes name and counts), the word is composed into that name too rather than left for a nested span to supply.
components/badge/component.css
/* Badge — the small display-only mark: a count docked on a control, or a
 * tone-carrying word sitting on a row. Extracted from the shipped Badge
 * primitive (src/renderer/src/components/ui/Badge.tsx).
 *
 * Two species under one name, because the audit found two hiding under the
 * one word: a numeric COUNT (solid tone, on-accent ink) and a LABEL chip
 * (soft tone fill with a matching hairline, muted ink). They share a size
 * and a radius and nothing else, so they are two classes rather than one
 * class with a variant that swaps every property.
 *
 * Never interactive — a badge is a readout, and a clickable one is a button
 * wearing a badge. Never a second status idiom beside a status mark that
 * already says the same thing. */

/* ── Count ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * The 16px box every shipped counter converged on, stated in the space
 * scale's own step for it. `min-width` with symmetric padding is what keeps
 * one digit circular and grows two into a pill instead of clipping. */
.ds-badge-count {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  box-sizing: border-box;
  height: var(--sem-space-xl);
  min-width: var(--sem-space-xl);
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-2xs);
  /* Pill, not radius.chip: a one-digit counter has to be a circle for the
     docked corner position to read as a badge rather than a clipped square.
     radius.chip is the right token for a RECTANGULAR chip; this is not one. */
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--sem-color-status-neutral);
  /* text.on-accent is the token that means "foreground for a filled
     surface". The three counters this replaces each hardcoded the app
     ground, which is legible only while the badge sits on a saturated
     tone. */
  color: var(--sem-color-text-on-accent);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
  line-height: 1;
  /* So 1 → 2 does not jog the row it is docked to. */
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}

/* ── Label ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * A short word about the row it sits on. Soft fill, tone hairline, muted
 * ink: the tone classifies, the ink stays readable, and the chip never
 * competes with the row's own text. */
.ds-badge-label {
  display: inline-flex;
  min-width: 0;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-2xs);
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-xs);
  border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-status-neutral);
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--sem-color-status-neutral-soft);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
  line-height: var(--sem-space-xl);
}

/* ── Tones ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * The status ramp plus the accent. A count takes the solid tone as its
 * ground; a label takes the soft tone as its ground and the solid one as
 * its edge. */
.ds-badge-count--accent {
  background: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
}
.ds-badge-count--good {
  background: var(--sem-color-status-good);
}
.ds-badge-count--warn {
  background: var(--sem-color-status-warn);
}
.ds-badge-count--danger {
  background: var(--sem-color-status-danger);
}

.ds-badge-label--accent {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  background: var(--sem-color-accent-soft);
}
.ds-badge-label--good {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-status-good);
  background: var(--sem-color-status-good-soft);
}
.ds-badge-label--warn {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-status-warn);
  background: var(--sem-color-status-warn-soft);
}
.ds-badge-label--danger {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-status-danger);
  background: var(--sem-color-status-danger-soft);
}

/* ── Corner ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Docks the count to the top-right of a positioned trigger, with a border
 * in the ground behind it so the badge reads as sitting ON the control
 * rather than inside it. The host must establish a positioning context.
 *
 * A ring spelled as a box-shadow would hold the box at exactly 16px, but
 * the product's token lint forbids that spelling outright — and every
 * counter this replaces already used a border, so this is their behaviour
 * rather than a compromise introduced here. */
.ds-badge-count--corner {
  position: absolute;
  top: calc(var(--sem-space-2xs) * -1);
  right: calc(var(--sem-space-2xs) * -1);
  border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-bg-app);
}

Banner

Light — danger with its required recovery, warn as a polite advisory.

Sessions unavailable — the daemon is not responding.
The panel's own content continues below the strip.
Posting paused — the tracker token expires in 2 days.
Degraded but working: the feature still runs.

Dark — the same strips from the same tokens.

Sessions unavailable — the daemon is not responding.
The panel's own content continues below the strip.
Posting paused — the tracker token expires in 2 days.
Degraded but working: the feature still runs.

The panel-spanning notice: one line at the top of a panel's content region saying that the panel's own data is failing or degraded, with the recovery beside it. Extracted from the source product's Banner (src/renderer/src/components/ui/Banner.tsx).

A banner is about this panel's content — the feed did not load, posting is paused, the connection dropped. A problem scoped to one section, row, or operation belongs to an inline-notice inside that scope; a transient confirmation belongs to a toast. And a banner is not chrome: it is a notice *about* the content, so it keeps its own band below the panel's chrome row without violating the one-chrome-band rule.

Tone vocabulary — the same two tones as inline-notice, and the same meanings:

  • danger — a failure. Something did not happen. Always paired with a recovery action; a dead-end failure banner is a bug.
  • warn — degraded but working. Reduced, paused, or partial — never a hard failure recolored, and never a failure softened to amber.

There is no info banner and no success banner. Information that matters is the panel's content; success is the state the screen already shows.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Strip | .ds-banner | yes — full width of the panel's content region | | Body | .ds-banner-body | yes — mark + message cluster; shrinks first | | Mark | .ds-status-dot + the tone modifier | yes — the status-dot component's glyph in the tone's ink, aria-hidden | | Message | .ds-banner-message | yes — one line, truncates | | Action | .ds-banner-action | danger: required; warn: optional — holds a ghost button (.ds-button.ds-button--ghost) |

The strip: the tone's soft tint over the surface, a border.default hairline on the bottom edge only (it shares every other edge with the panel), space.lg / space.sm padding, message at font.size.meta in text.primary.

No left tone-bar — the rejected-on-sight rule applies to banners exactly as it does to notices. The mark is the tone's shape; the tint is its echo.

Variants

  • ds-banner--danger — failure. The danger glyph (a ring with "×", in status.danger) on status.danger-soft.
  • ds-banner--warn — degraded. The warn glyph (a ring with "!", in status.warn) on status.warn-soft.

Nothing else: no sizes, no icon slots, no dismiss-x variant. A banner leaves when its condition resolves — a dismissable failure is a failure you are still having with worse visibility.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Present | The condition holds. One banner per panel — the worst condition wins | | Resolved | The banner unmounts. No success flash in its place |

The banner itself has no hover or selection; its one action is the only interactive part.

Usage

  • Top of the content region, directly under the panel's chrome, full width of the column it describes — not the screen, if the panel is one pane of many.
  • One line. The message states the condition ("Feed unavailable"), not the exception; detail belongs behind the action or in an inline-notice at the failure site. A banner that needs to wrap is carrying a paragraph that belongs elsewhere.
  • The action names the recovery, usually "Retry". It is a ghost button — the banner's tint is already the emphasis, and a solid button here would compete with the view's real primary action.
  • The status mark is the status idiom, and it is the only one: no additional glyph, no tinted pill, no second mark saying the same thing. Never a dot: the product draws no status dots (owner ruling 2026-09-28).
  • Do not stack banners. Two conditions at once is one banner for the worse condition; the other surfaces where it lives.

Accessibility

  • role="alert" on danger — a failure interrupts. role="status" on warn — degradation informs politely. This split is the tone vocabulary made audible; do not flatten both to one role.
  • The mark is aria-hidden: the message carries the meaning in words, so the state is never conveyed by color alone — and the two roles differ, so it is not conveyed by the glyph's shape alone either.
  • The action is a real button, reachable by Tab, with the banner's context in its accessible name where "Retry" alone is ambiguous ("Retry loading sessions").
  • Truncated messages still expose their full text (the list-row/tooltip truncation contract applies).

The action slot (2026-08-05)

The anatomy above says the action slot "holds a ghost button" — it did not say that button has to be spelled *Retry*, and the two strips that were rebuilding this component by hand both needed to say something else: a Relink beside the retry on a surface whose saved folder went missing, and Refresh walkthrough on a review whose head moved. Shipped Banner takes an optional action node for exactly that, rendered after the Retry when both are given.

It is still one recovery cluster, not a toolbar. A condition that wants a third control is not a banner condition — it belongs in an inline-notice at the site of the failure.

Ruling — there is no quiet banner. The review canvas's freshness strip had invented a third "quiet" tone for the walkthrough being current. A resolved condition unmounts its banner; what is left when nothing is wrong is a plain provenance line, not a tinted strip in a calmer colour.

Remaining drift: paddings here are Tailwind steps (px-3 py-2) that land on the scale but bypass the variables.

components/banner/component.css
/* Banner — the panel-spanning failure/degradation strip at the top of a
 * panel's content region (src/renderer/src/components/ui/Banner.tsx).
 *
 * Tone rides in the status mark and the soft tint — no left tone-bar, ever: a
 * coloured stripe doubles the hairline, breaks the 1px rule, and carries tone
 * by colour alone. The mark is the status-dot component's glyph
 * (`.ds-status-dot` + the tone's modifier), not a bespoke part: the ring with
 * "×" on danger, the ring with "!" on warn. The bottom hairline is the strip's only border; the other
 * three edges belong to the panel. */

.ds-banner {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--sem-space-lg);
  padding: var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-lg);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-default);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
}

.ds-banner--danger {
  background: var(--sem-color-status-danger-soft);
}

.ds-banner--warn {
  background: var(--sem-color-status-warn-soft);
}

/* The body leads with the status mark — the surface's one status idiom.
 * Decorative to a reader (the message and the role carry the meaning), shape
 * to an eye. It is `components/status-dot`, so it brings its own size and
 * ink; the body's centred flex line is all the placement it needs. */
.ds-banner-body {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
  min-width: 0;
}

/* One line. A message that wraps is a paragraph that belongs elsewhere. */
.ds-banner-message {
  min-width: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

/* The recovery action slot; the control itself is the button component's
 * ghost variant — the tint is already the emphasis. */
.ds-banner-action {
  flex: none;
}

The column chrome of a board: a header band naming the stage, a scrollable list of task cards, and the drag-and-drop states a card moves through. Extracted from the shipped BoardLane primitive (src/renderer/src/components/ui/BoardLane.tsx).

The lane owns the column — its header rhythm, its scroll region, and its drop states. It does not own the cards: children are task-card components (already documented), and the card contract is unchanged inside a lane. Use list-row when the items form a pick-one list; a lane is a stage that work moves through.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Lane | .ds-board-lane | yes — a <section> with an aria-label | | Header | .ds-board-lane-header | yes — one band: label left, count right | | Glyph | .ds-board-lane-glyph | no — a lifecycle glyph beside the label, aria-hidden | | Label | .ds-board-lane-label | yes — font.size.meta at font.weight.emphasis, text.primary, sentence case, truncates | | Count | .ds-board-lane-count | yes — tabular, font.size.micro, text.subtle | | Body | .ds-board-lane-body | yes — an <ol> of cards, the lane's scroll region | | Drop indicator | .ds-board-lane-drop | during a drag — a 2px accent hairline <li> |

Lanes flex to fill the board row and shrink to a floor — --ds-board-lane-min-width, 260px by default (a comfortable card width). Past the floor the board row scrolls horizontally; inside the lane only the body scrolls vertically. The header never scrolls away.

Variants

  • Default — transparent: the lane is a region of the board canvas, and hairlines between cards carry the structure.
  • --surface — the lane is a filled, hairline-bordered panel (bg.surface, radius.overlay, border.subtle), and the cards inside lift one step to bg.surface-raised with an inset hairline. The inset hairline is load-bearing in light mode, where bg.surface and bg.surface-raised are deliberately the same white and the tone step does nothing. Opt in when columns must read as discrete panels; default off so a board canvas is not a grid of cards inside cards.

States

Four drag states, and the lane is always in exactly one:

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Default | No special chrome | | --dimmed | opacity: 0.4 — not a legal target for the dragged card | | --drop-target | 1px accent ring — this lane will accept the card | | --source | Neutral, same as default — the lane the card left |

The accent ring and the 2px drop indicator are the accent as ink marking a genuinely live process — the one thing besides focus the accent budget lets a hairline say. At rest a board shows no accent at all.

Usage

The header is one band. Label and glyph on the left, count on the right, nothing else. Lane-level actions belong in the board's own chrome or a context menu — a button row per lane multiplies controls by column count.

The count is the lane's canonical count. Never restate it in the lane (an empty-state line that says "0 items" under a header that says 0).

Drop position is the card midpoint. During a drag, the drop index is found by comparing the pointer's y position with each card's vertical midpoint; the consumer interleaves one drop indicator at that index. One indicator on the whole board — it marks the place, not the possibilities.

Reordering is the just-changed motion. When cards move, they slide to their new slots (a FLIP pass in the shipped primitive) composing motion.duration.normal and motion.ease.standard — a pattern-owned entrance, not a fourth motion. Reduced motion swaps the slide for an immediate move; the reorder itself is never withheld.

Drag is never the only path. A pointer drag has no keyboard equivalent, so every card move must also be reachable another way — a context-menu "Move to…" or the detail pane. A board you cannot operate from the keyboard is a bug, not a style.

Empty is a state, not an absence. An empty lane keeps its header and its body height, and says what the emptiness means ("Nothing in review") — otherwise an empty column and a failed load render identically.

Accessibility

  • Each lane is a <section> with an aria-label naming the stage ("In review lane"); the body is an <ol>, so assistive technology reports position in set for free.
  • The lane label's glyph is aria-hidden — the label carries the meaning.
  • The drop indicator is aria-hidden; the *result* of a drop is announced by the move's non-drag path, not by decoration.
  • The dimmed state keeps its content readable — 0.4 opacity signals ineligibility during a drag that a pointer user is already mid-gesture on; it never carries information a keyboard user cannot get elsewhere.
  • If the lane's body scrolls and must be keyboard-scrollable on its own, give it tabindex="0" and the inward focus ring, as tabs does for its panel. When every card inside is focusable, the cards themselves usually carry the scroll and the extra tab stop is noise — decide per surface.

Shipped implementation

src/renderer/src/components/ui/BoardLane.tsx, exporting BoardLane, BoardLaneDropIndicator (the between-cards insertion mark) and computeBoardLaneDropIndex (the pure drop-target maths, kept separate so the drop position is testable without a drag).

components/board-lane/component.css
/* Board lane — the column chrome of a board: header band, scrollable card
 * list, drag states. Extracted from the shipped BoardLane primitive
 * (src/renderer/src/components/ui/BoardLane.tsx).
 *
 * Family contract: the lane owns the column, never the cards — children are
 * ds-task-card components and their contract is unchanged inside a lane. At
 * rest a board shows no accent; the accent appears only as the live-process
 * ink of a drag (the drop-target ring and the 2px drop indicator). */

.ds-board-lane {
  display: flex;
  flex: 1;
  flex-direction: column;
  height: 100%;
  /* The scroll floor, not a fixed width: lanes grow to share the row and
   * shrink to this, past which the BOARD row scrolls horizontally. 260px is
   * a comfortable card width; a denser board narrows it via the property. */
  min-width: var(--ds-board-lane-min-width, 260px);
  transition: opacity var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

/* ── Surface variant ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * The lane as a discrete panel. The cards inside lift one step to
 * bg.surface-raised with an inset hairline — load-bearing in light mode,
 * where bg.surface and bg.surface-raised are deliberately the same white
 * and only the hairline keeps a card legible on the fill. */
.ds-board-lane--surface {
  border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-overlay);
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
}

.ds-board-lane--surface .ds-task-card {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface-raised);
  border-color: transparent;
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
}

/* ── Drag states ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Four, and the lane is always in exactly one. --source is deliberately
 * absent: the lane a card left stays neutral, so it needs no rule. */

/* Not a legal target for the dragged card. Signals ineligibility to the
 * pointer user mid-gesture; never the only carrier of that information. */
.ds-board-lane--dimmed {
  opacity: 0.4;
}

/* Will accept the card: a 1px accent ring — the accent as ink marking a
 * genuinely live process, not elevation (no blur, no offset). */
.ds-board-lane--drop-target {
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
}

/* ── Header ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * One band: glyph + label left, count right. It never scrolls away — only
 * the body below it scrolls. */
.ds-board-lane-header {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
  padding: var(--sem-space-md) var(--sem-space-lg) var(--sem-space-sm);
}

.ds-board-lane-title {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
  min-width: 0;
}

.ds-board-lane-glyph {
  flex: none;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
}

.ds-board-lane-glyph svg {
  width: var(--sem-icon-size-xs);
  height: var(--sem-icon-size-xs);
}

.ds-board-lane-label {
  min-width: 0;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

/* The lane's canonical count — shown here, never restated inside the lane. */
.ds-board-lane-count {
  flex: none;
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
}

/* ── Body ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * An <ol> of cards and the lane's one scroll region. min-height: 0 lets the
 * flex column actually shrink it; without it the lane grows instead of
 * scrolling. */
.ds-board-lane-body {
  flex: 1;
  min-height: 0;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
  margin: 0;
  padding: var(--sem-space-sm);
  overflow-y: auto;
  list-style: none;
}

/* ── Drop indicator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * A 2px accent hairline the consumer interleaves at the computed drop index
 * during a drag — one on the whole board. Negative block margins let it sit
 * inside the list gap without shifting the cards it slots between. */
.ds-board-lane-drop {
  height: 2px;
  margin-block: calc(-1 * var(--sem-space-2xs));
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .ds-board-lane {
    transition: none;
  }
}
