Anatomy

  • ds-field — vertical stack, 6px gap: label, control, one supporting message.
  • ds-field-label — font.size.body at font.weight.medium in text.default; a required mark (*) in text.subtle — neutral, because an untouched required field is empty, not invalid (see field) — is aria-hidden and mirrored by aria-required on the control.
  • ds-input — a size.control.sm control on bg.surface-raised with a border.default hairline and radius.control.
  • ds-field-help / ds-field-error — font.size.meta; help in text.subtle, error in status.danger.

Variants

  • Default — the field material: bg.field (the raised surface on an opaque window, translucent under glass), a border.default hairline, radius.control. A field READS as raised: it is the thing you put something into. The same chrome serves search inputs (add a leading search glyph) and other single-line controls.
  • --well — the recessed step, on bg.app, for a control inside a settings row where the body is already bg.surface and a raised field would have nothing to lift away from.
Variants whose box belongs to something else (2026-09-08)

Three cases where the default box was the wrong object, not the wrong colour. Each existed as a hand-roll in the consuming product, and each hand-roll began by cancelling four things the field chrome had decided.

  • --quiet — transparent ground, a border.subtle hairline, and no hover lift. For a field inside an already-grounded floating surface: a filter box at the head of a popover, a search inside a menu. There the field ground reads as a second panel nested in the first — the card-in-a-card *Hairlines carry the structure* rejects — and a border moving on hover inside a surface that already has one reads as the surface itself changing.
  • --seamless — no box at all: no border, no ground, no radius, and no focus indicator of its own. The visible box is the wrapper (ds-field-box), which draws the border and takes the ring keyed to the field's own focus. The system already shipped the wrapper half of this pattern and had no field to put inside it.

Keyed to the field's focus, never :focus-within: a clear button or a send button in the same box is a descendant, and a focus-within outline stays painted while that button draws its own, putting two indicators on one stop.

Never ship one without a wrapper that lights up. A seamless field alone has no focus indicator, which is a defect rather than a style.

  • --inline — the title edited in place. Quiet at rest, revealing the field chrome on hover or focus, so the head of a page reads as a heading rather than as a form field wearing one, and the name is still one click away. It states no font size: the type step is the surface's own decision, and one here would be a second font-size for the cascade to resolve.

Sizes

sm (size.control.sm) is the default and the panel-chrome standard: an input, a select and a button sharing a row all sit on it. md is the overlay step.

xs (size.control.xs, 26px) was added on 2026-09-08 for the dense numeric or mono box in a toolbar of 26px icon buttons — a viewport width, a browser address bar — where a 30px field is the tallest thing in the row. It is a ramp step being *used*, not a height being invented, and the type drops with it to font.size.meta, which is what makes the cursor and its inset fit. It is not a licence to shrink a labelled form field, which stays at sm.

The seamless, composer and inline variants take no size step whatever the caller asks: their host owns the box, and a height here would be the one thing the caller then had to cancel.

Textarea

The multiline member of the same vocabulary — the field chrome above, with the height coming from rows and the content instead of the ramp, so the size step spends itself on the block inset. A textarea and the input above it in one form are the same field at two lengths.

  • --composer — seamless for the multiline case, plus content sizing: the box grows with what is typed, between the caller's bounds. A variant of its own rather than a flag on seamless, because a single-line field that content-sized would grow *sideways*, and the two must not be reachable by one name. The chat composer is its one surface: the wrapping composer material draws the border, the ground and the elevation, and takes the ring keyed to the textarea's own focus, while the ref, the row count and the paste, context-menu and key handlers pass straight through to the element.
  • --quiet — the same quiet ground as the single-line variant, for a note composer inside a floating card.
The file dialog (owner ruling 2026-10-04)

HiddenFileInput is the input's one invisible shape: an <input type="file"> that draws nothing, is never a tab stop, and is opened by a kit button or menu row that calls .click() on it — the New chat composer's "Attach files" row. That control carries the name and the focus ring; the input only brings the system's dialog. Its value is cleared after each pick, so the same file can be picked twice in a row.

Date and time (2026-10-09)

DateTimeInput is the input carrying the browser's own datetime-local, date or time control. The native control is kept on purpose — its segmented entry is keyboard-complete, each segment has an accessible name, the calendar is the platform's, and the day/month order follows the locale — and the box around it is this field, at the same sizes and grounds (default, well, quiet; never the hosted variants, because a date field always draws its own box). It adds tabular figures, so a value that changes does not change width, and tones the calendar button to the field's muted ink on dark themes.

Values are the control's own local-time strings (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm, YYYY-MM-DD, HH:mm). Which zone they mean is the caller's to decide; the field never converts. Label it with the field component like any input — a date alone is not a name.

States

  • Hover: border moves to border.strong.
  • Focus: the shared 2px border.focus ring, and nothing else — the border does not change colour.
  • Invalid: aria-invalid="true" moves the border to status.danger; the error message replaces the help text (never both).
  • Disabled: text.disabled ink, reduced opacity, not-allowed cursor.
  • Placeholder: text.disabled.

Usage

  • Exactly one supporting message at a time — help hides while an error shows.
  • Labels are sentence case, no trailing colon.
  • Do not stretch inputs beyond their content column; size.control.sm is the panel-chrome standard height.

Accessibility

  • The label is a real <label for> pointing at the control.
  • aria-describedby points at the visible help or error message, whichever is shown.
  • Invalid state is conveyed by aria-invalid, not color alone (the error text names the problem).

Drift ruling (2026-08-05)

Reconciled against src/renderer/src/components/ui/Input.tsx. The shipped behaviour wins on both counts, and the States section above now describes it.

  • No focus border swap. The spec moved the border to accent.primary on focus *as well as* drawing the ring. Two signals for one state, and the border one is the weaker: it is a 1px hue change on a control that already has a 2px ring around it, and it spends the accent on a state that is not a choice the person made. Every other focusable control in the system — button, switch, segmented control, checkbox, menu item — says focus with the ring alone; an input saying it twice is the odd one out. Hover keeps border.strong, which is a real second state the border is free to carry.
  • Placeholder ink is text.disabled. Placeholder text is not content and must sit clearly below the value that replaces it; text.subtle is close enough to real input ink to read as a filled field at a glance.

The reference CSS in component.css moves with this ruling.

Shipped implementation

src/renderer/src/components/ui/Input.tsx, exporting Input, Textarea and INLINE_TITLE_EDIT_CLASS. That constant is the inline variant's chrome, exported separately because several sites consume it on an element of their own where the type step is theirs to set; a caller who wants only the chrome should take the variant, so the primitive is what draws it.

components/input/component.css
/* Input — extracted from the source product's Field wrapper and the
 * size.control.sm input chrome (src/renderer/src/components/ui/Field.tsx,
 * InboxSearchInput.tsx). */

.ds-field {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
}

.ds-field-label {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
}

.ds-field-required {
  margin-left: var(--sem-space-2xs);
  color: var(--sem-color-status-danger);
}

.ds-input {
  height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
  border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-default);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface-raised);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  font-family: inherit;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  transition: border-color var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

.ds-input::placeholder {
  /* Placeholder is not content: it must sit clearly below the value that
   * replaces it, or an empty field reads as a filled one at a glance. */
  color: var(--sem-color-text-disabled);
}

/* Hover is the border's state. */
.ds-input:hover {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-border-strong);
}

/* Focus is the ring, and only the ring. This used to move the border
 * to the accent as well — two signals for one state, and the weaker of the two:
 * a 1px hue change on a control that already has a 2px ring around it, spending
 * the accent on something the person did not choose. Every other focusable
 * control in the system says focus with the ring alone. */

.ds-input:focus-visible {
  outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
}

.ds-input[aria-invalid='true'] {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-status-danger);
}

.ds-input:disabled {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-disabled);
  cursor: not-allowed;
  opacity: 0.6;
}

/* One supporting message at a time: help hides when an error shows. */
.ds-field-help {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
}

.ds-field-error {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  color: var(--sem-color-status-danger);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .ds-input {
    transition: none;
  }
}

/* ── Grounds and hosts (2026-09-08) ──────────────────────────────────────
 * The field's box is not always the field's to draw. Three variants below
 * quiet it or hand it away, and each answers a case where the default box was
 * the wrong object rather than the wrong colour. */

/* well — the recessed step for a control inside a settings row, where the body
 * is already bg.surface and a raised field would have nothing to lift away
 * from. */
.ds-input--well {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-app);
}

/* quiet — transparent ground, a border.subtle hairline, and NO hover lift. For
 * a field inside an already-grounded floating surface: a filter box at the head
 * of a popover, a search inside a menu. There the field ground reads as a
 * second panel nested in the first — a card inside a card — and a border that
 * moves on hover inside a surface that already has one reads as the surface
 * itself changing. */
.ds-input--quiet {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
  background: transparent;
}

.ds-input--quiet:hover:not(:disabled) {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
}

/* seamless — no box at all: no border, no ground, no radius, and no focus
 * indicator of its own. The visible box is the WRAPPER, which draws the border
 * and takes the ring keyed to this field's own focus. The system already
 * shipped the wrapper half of the pattern and had no field to put inside it,
 * so every composed control (a glyph + field + menu row, a chat composer) wrote
 * the four cancelling declarations by hand.
 *
 * `outline: none` is unprefixed on purpose: the UA outline is replaced by the
 * wrapper's in EVERY focus state, not only the keyboard one, because the
 * wrapper is the box a person sees. Never ship one of these without a wrapper
 * that lights up — a seamless field alone has no focus indicator, which is a
 * defect rather than a style. */
.ds-input--seamless {
  height: auto;
  padding: 0;
  border: none;
  border-radius: 0;
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  outline: none;
}

.ds-input--seamless:hover:not(:disabled) {
  border-color: transparent;
}

/* The wrapper that owns the box for a seamless field. It lights up on the
 * FIELD's focus, never on :focus-within: a clear button or a send button in the
 * same box is a descendant, and a focus-within outline stays painted while that
 * button draws its own, putting two indicators on one stop. */
.ds-field-box {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
  height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
  border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-default);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface-raised);
}

.ds-field-box:hover {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-border-strong);
}

.ds-field-box:has(.ds-input--seamless:focus) {
  outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
}

/* inline — the title edited IN PLACE. Quiet at rest — no box at all — and the
 * field chrome appears on hover or focus, so the head of a page reads as a
 * heading rather than as a form field wearing one, and the name is still one
 * click away. It states no font size: the type step is the surface's own
 * decision, and one here would be a second font-size for the cascade to
 * resolve. */
.ds-input--inline {
  height: auto;
  padding: var(--sem-space-3xs) var(--sem-space-xs);
  border-color: transparent;
  background: transparent;
  font-size: inherit;
  font-weight: inherit;
}

.ds-input--inline:hover:not(:disabled) {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-border-default);
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface-raised);
}

/* ── The xs step (2026-09-08) ────────────────────────────────────────────
 * A dense numeric or mono box in a toolbar of 26px icon buttons — a viewport
 * width, a browser address bar — where a 30px field is the tallest thing in the
 * row. It is a ramp step being used (size.control.xs), not a height being
 * invented, and it is not a licence to shrink a labelled form field, which
 * stays at sm. The type drops with it: font.size.meta, which is what makes the
 * cursor and its inset fit. */
.ds-input--xs {
  height: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
}

/* ── Textarea ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * The multiline member of the same vocabulary. Its height comes from `rows` and
 * its content, so the size step spends itself on the block inset instead. */
.ds-textarea {
  height: auto;
  padding: var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-sm);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-default);
  resize: vertical;
}

/* composer — seamless for the multiline case, plus content sizing: the box
 * grows with what is typed, between the caller's bounds. A variant of its own
 * rather than a flag on seamless, because a single-line field that content-sized
 * would grow sideways and the two must not be reachable by one name. */
.ds-textarea--composer {
  padding: 0;
  border: none;
  border-radius: 0;
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  outline: none;
  resize: none;
  field-sizing: content;
}

Kbd chord

Light — chords in their habitat: the trailing hint on actions that already have a click path.

Dark — the raised capsule tone does its step here; the hairline carries it in light.

The keyboard-shortcut hint: each key a real <kbd> capsule, joined by a quiet separator. Extracted from the shipped KbdChord primitive (src/renderer/src/components/ui/KbdChord.tsx).

It *describes* a shortcut, it never *invokes* one — the control the chord labels owns the actual handler. Purely presentational, and the one place in the product exempt from sentence case: keys render as keys ("⌘", "Shift", "K").

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Chord | .ds-kbd-chord | yes — role="img" with an aria-label naming the chord | | Key | .ds-kbd-chord-key | yes — a real <kbd>: mono font.size.micro, bg.surface-raised, border.subtle hairline, radius.chip | | Separator | .ds-kbd-chord-sep | between keys — a + in text.disabled, aria-hidden | | Sequence word | .ds-kbd-chord-then | between strokes of a multi-stroke chord — the word "then", aria-hidden |

The capsule is a 16px-tall micro-type chip — glyph scale, deliberately below the 24px hit-target floor, because it is not a target. Anything this small that could be clicked would be a defect; a label cannot be.

Variants

None. One appearance, in every context — a settings row, a walkthrough step, a composer's footer. A chord that changes style per surface stops reading as the same vocabulary.

Not every shortcut hint is a chord. A [menu](../menu/component.md) row annotates its shortcut as plain mono micro text: there the shortcut is a footnote to an action, and capsules would out-weigh the label. The chord is for surfaces where the shortcut itself is the subject.

States

None. The chord is display-only: no hover, no focus, no pressed state. A "pressed key" animation would be motion meaning nothing.

Usage

Keys are keys, not prose. Platform-resolved symbols or names per key ("⌘" on macOS, "Ctrl" on Windows), resolved by the consumer before render. Never a sentence ("press Command and K").

One key per capsule. "⌘K" in a single capsule is a string wearing a costume; the chord's grammar is capsule + separator + capsule.

Multi-stroke chords say "then". "⌘K then P" renders as two capsule groups joined by the sequence word — the + separator means "together", "then" means "in order", and the two are never interchangeable.

A hint, never the only path. The chord annotates an action that is already reachable by click or menu. It sits in the trailing slot at text.disabled-adjacent quietness because it is an accelerator note, not a call to action.

Do not decorate identifiers with it. A capsule around anything that is not a key — a branch name, a flag — dilutes the vocabulary. Identifiers are mono text, not keys.

Accessibility

  • The chord carries role="img" and an aria-label reading the chord in words ("Command K", "Command K then P"). Screen readers hear one coherent name instead of a stutter of single letters and plus signs.
  • Separators and the sequence word are aria-hidden — they are spelled out by the label instead.
  • Real <kbd> elements, so the semantics survive wherever the markup travels.
  • The capsule's micro type is below the body floor, which is acceptable only because the chord is supplementary: the action's name — not the chord — carries the meaning, and text.muted on bg.surface-raised keeps the keys legible without promoting them.
components/kbd-chord/component.css
/* Kbd chord — the keyboard-shortcut hint: each key a real <kbd> capsule,
 * joined by a quiet separator. Extracted from the shipped KbdChord primitive
 * (src/renderer/src/components/ui/KbdChord.tsx).
 *
 * Family contract: describes a shortcut, never invokes one — no hover, no
 * focus, no pressed state. The one surface exempt from sentence case: keys
 * render as keys. */

.ds-kbd-chord {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-2xs);
}

/* A 16px micro-type capsule — glyph scale, deliberately below the hit-target
 * floor because it is a label, not a target. Mono per the type rules: a key
 * name is an identifier, not prose. */
.ds-kbd-chord-key {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  box-sizing: border-box;
  height: 16px;
  min-width: 16px;
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-2xs);
  border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-chip);
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface-raised);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-wide);
  line-height: 1;
}

/* "+" means together. The disabled ink is deliberate: the separator is
 * grammar, not content, and it must never compete with the keys. */
.ds-kbd-chord-sep {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-disabled);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
}

/* "then" means in order — the joint between the strokes of a multi-stroke
 * chord. Same quietness as the separator, plus breathing room. */
.ds-kbd-chord-then {
  padding-inline: var(--sem-space-3xs);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-disabled);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
}
components/kbd-chord/component.html (demo)
<!doctype html>

Link button

Light

Signed out ·

Walks the repository and lists every skill it finds.

Changed in this morning.

Dark

Signed out ·

Walks the repository and lists every skill it finds.

Changed in this morning.

An action set inside a sentence. "Reconnect" at the end of a ·-separated state line, "More" under a clamped description, "Search GitHub" beside a field, a repository path in rendered prose that opens a file rather than a URL.

It is the smallest member of the button family and the only one with no box at all: no height, no inset, no ground, no press scale.

Why it is not an <a>. None of these navigates. They call something. A link that is not a link is a lie to the keyboard and to assistive technology, and the address bar it implies never appears.

Why it is not a ghost [button](../button/component.md). The ghost is the quietest sized member and still brings a size.control.xs height, an space.sm inset, font.weight.medium and a hover fill. Put that inside a 20px metadata line and the line grows, the words either side stop sitting level with it, and the "link" reads as a control someone forgot to finish. In the consuming product every one of these had stayed a raw <button> with border: 0; background: transparent; padding: 0 written out by hand — four declarations cancelling the browser, rather than a shape the system had named.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Link | .ds-link-button | yes — a <button> | | Ink | --quiet, --name | no — the default is accent ink | | Type | --inherit | no — the default is font.size.meta |

display: inline, so the link wraps with the sentence rather than sitting in it as a box. The radius exists only so the focus ring has corners to draw round; nothing is painted inside it.

Variants

  • Default (accent) — accent ink, deepening to accent.hover, underlined on hover. Accent as ink is inside the budget; what the budget forbids is the accent as a fill, which this never takes.
  • --quiet — text.muted lifting to text.primary, with a permanent underline in border.strong at a 2px offset. The disclosure case: "More", "Show details". The underline is standing rather than a hover reveal because a quiet link with no colour and no box is indistinguishable from the sentence around it until the pointer happens to cross it.
  • --name — text.primary, underlined on hover. The name of the thing a list row is about, when the name is what opens that thing's details: the extensions list in Settings, where a row's name opens its details popover. At rest it has to read as the row's title, not as an action — and the accent would turn every title in the list into a second accent. The hover underline is what says it can be pressed; the row around it may also open the same details on a click, but the name is the keyboard's way in.
  • --row — a full-width flex row with its parts baseline-aligned, for a LIST of links rather than one set inside a sentence: a column of changed files where the name, the folder and the counts have to line up down the list. It is a variant rather than a caller's own display, because display is the one property the base rule spends on being inline — a competing declaration at equal specificity is resolved by stylesheet order, and a row that quietly fell back to inline would lose its columns entirely. Everything else about the link is unchanged: still no box, no height and no ground.
  • --inherit — takes the surrounding text's size and weight instead of font.size.meta. For the link set inside prose the caller has already sized: a path inside rendered markdown, a name inside a heading. A size of our own there would make one word of a sentence a different size from the rest of it, which is worse than any consistency it buys.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Rest | Per ink above | | Hover | Ink one step; accent and name add an underline, quiet already has one | | Focus-visible | The shared ring, at the standard offset | | Disabled | 45% opacity, not-allowed, underline dropped, ink kept | | Pressed | Nothing. A control that shrank mid-sentence would move the words after it |

Disabled keeps its ink. A sentence whose one action has fallen to text.disabled reads as broken copy rather than as an unavailable action, and the disabled step is certified for 3:1 non-text contrast only — it may not carry words.

Usage

  • One per sentence. Two link buttons in one line of copy is a line that wanted a control row.
  • The label is a verb or a noun the sentence needs, never "click here" or "learn more" as a stand-alone. principles.md rejects empty-state copy that explains an obvious interaction; a link is copy.
  • Not for a primary action. If the action is what the view is for, it is a button with a box. A link is for an action the sentence mentions in passing.
  • Not for navigation. A destination the shell can route to is a door and gets a real navigation affordance.

Accessibility

  • It is a <button>, so Enter and Space both activate it, and it announces as a button rather than as a link that goes nowhere.
  • The focus ring is the product's one indicator and is not suppressed. On an inline element the outline follows the line boxes, including across a wrap, which is correct.
  • The hit target is the text, deliberately: the size.hit-target-min floor governs a standalone glyph, which has no line to belong to. Growing an inline control's box to 24px would push the lines around it apart.
  • A disclosure link states aria-expanded for the region it opens.

Shipped implementation

src/renderer/src/components/ui/LinkButton.tsx, exporting LinkButton with ink, underline and size.

components/link-button/component.css
/* Link button — an action set inside a sentence. Extracted from the shipped
 * `LinkButton` primitive (src/renderer/src/components/ui/LinkButton.tsx).
 *
 * It is the smallest member of the button family and the only one with no box at
 * all: no height, no inset, no ground, no press scale. Everything a button
 * normally decides belongs to the line of text it is set in. */

.ds-link-button {
  display: inline;
  padding: 0;
  border: none;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-chip);
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  text-align: left;
  text-decoration: none;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: color var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

/* The radius exists only so the focus ring has corners to draw round; nothing is
 * painted inside it. And no `transform` press: a control that shrank
 * mid-sentence would move the words after it. */

.ds-link-button:hover:not(:disabled) {
  color: var(--sem-color-accent-hover);
  text-decoration: underline;
}

.ds-link-button:focus-visible {
  outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
}

/* Disabled keeps the ink and drops the underline. A sentence whose one action
 * has gone text.disabled reads as broken copy rather than as an unavailable
 * action, and the disabled step is certified for non-text contrast only. */
.ds-link-button:disabled {
  cursor: not-allowed;
  opacity: 0.45;
  text-decoration: none;
}

/* quiet — the disclosure ink. With no colour and no box, it needs a standing
 * rule to be findable at all, so the underline is permanent here rather than a
 * hover reveal. */
.ds-link-button--quiet {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
  text-decoration: underline;
  text-decoration-color: var(--sem-color-border-strong);
  text-underline-offset: 2px;
}

.ds-link-button--quiet:hover:not(:disabled) {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

/* name — the name of the thing a list row is about, when the name opens its
 * details. Title ink at rest so it reads as the row's title; the hover
 * underline is what says it can be pressed. */
.ds-link-button--name {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

.ds-link-button--name:hover:not(:disabled) {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

/* inherit — the link set inside prose the caller has already sized: a repo path
 * in rendered markdown, a name inside a heading. A size of our own there would
 * make one word of a sentence a different size from the rest of it. */
.ds-link-button--inherit {
  font: inherit;
  line-height: inherit;
}

/* row — a full-width flex row, for a LIST of links rather than one set inside a
 * sentence: the conversation peek's changed files, where the name, the folder
 * and the counts are three columns that have to line up down the list.
 *
 * A variant and not something a caller adds on top, because `display` is the one
 * property this component's base rule spends on being inline: a `flex` written
 * beside `.ds-link-button` competes at equal specificity, so which wins is
 * stylesheet order rather than the author's intent, and a row that silently fell
 * back to `inline` would put the whole path on one baseline with no columns at
 * all. */
.ds-link-button--row {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  inline-size: 100%;
  min-inline-size: 0;
}

List row

Light — a rail → list → detail surface. Only the focused pane carries the strong selection.

Marketplace — focused

Sources — resting

Cursor — a third channel, readable on the selected row

anthropics/skills
mattpocock/skills
pbakaus/impeccable

Hover or tab a row to reveal its actions

Attention — the row is the mark; gold outranks green

Narrow — long lines truncate

Dark — the same four panes.

Marketplace — focused

Sources — resting

Cursor — a third channel, readable on the selected row

anthropics/skills
mattpocock/skills
pbakaus/impeccable

Hover or tab a row to reveal its actions

Attention — the row is the mark; gold outranks green

Narrow — long lines truncate

The pick-an-item worklist row: rails, source lists, inboxes, categories, search results. The most repeated surface in the product, and the default answer for any list of things a person chooses between.

Use task-card instead when the item is a card on a board. Use this when the item is a row in a list.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Row | .ds-list-row | yes — renders as <button> when interactive | | Leading mark | .ds-list-row-leading | no — a status glyph, type icon, or monogram | | Text block | .ds-list-row-text | yes | | Title | .ds-list-row-title | yes — the row's one priority, claims the width | | Supporting line | .ds-list-row-supporting | no — one line, truncated | | Identifier | .ds-list-row-id | no — mono, tabular, inside the supporting line | | Trailing meta | .ds-list-row-trailing | no — display only, never interactive | | Action host | .ds-list-row-host | only when the row has revealed actions | | Action count | data-actions on the host | yes when there are actions — "1" or "2", the value the trailing padding is reserved from | | Actions | .ds-list-row-actions | no — at most two | | Action | .ds-list-row-action | — | | Flash | .ds-list-row-flash | only as a row enters an attention state — a one-shot overlay, aria-hidden |

At most four visual elements at rest. A fifth means the row is carrying work that belongs in the detail pane.

Variants

  • Default — no modifier. The resting, unselected row.
  • --selected — the selected row of the pane that currently has focus. Neutral bg.selected fill, a 2px inset accent.primary edge, title lifts to text.primary.
  • --resting — the selected row of a pane that does not have focus. Quieter bg.selected-resting fill, no edge, title stays at text.default.

A surface has exactly one --selected row on screen. In a rail → list → detail layout the other two panes use --resting, so the person can always see which list their keyboard is driving. The edge is what makes that legible: one accent edge on screen, on the pane with focus.

The accent appears as an edge, never a fill (owner ruling 2026-09-05). A neutral fill on its own lost to every row wearing a status tint, so the person could not find the row they were driving; an accent *fill* would have fixed that by making a chosen row outrank the primary button beside it, which is the accent's other job. Selection still never carries a left bar or a glow. See patterns/selection.

Attention

Two states a row can say on its own, each taking the whole row — a tinted fill and the title in the tone's ink:

  • --needs-input — an agent on this row is waiting for the person. status.warn-soft fill, status.warn ink. The loudest thing a row can say.
  • --finished — a turn on this row finished while the person was looking elsewhere, and they have not opened it since. status.good-faint fill, status.good ink. One notch under needs-input by construction: it asks for a look, not an answer.

Status is the fill; selection is the edge. Neither attention state draws a ring (owner ruling 2026-09-05, removing the one they used to carry). A green ring around a finished row is the same mark as the accent edge on the row being driven, and it was the louder of the two — so "I finished while you were out" was read as "this is the one you are in". Two questions, two channels: a row can wear a status wash and the selection edge at once, and neither is mistaken for the other.

When a row is both attention states, needs-input wins. Both hold until the person opens the row and clear the moment it becomes the selected one.

Both are colour plus words: the trailing slot or a visually-hidden clause says "needs input" / "finished" in text. Never a status mark or a chip beside an otherwise quiet row — that was ruled out twice (2026-09-04): the one state that wants the person to look must not be the quietest thing on the row.

A row entering either state plays .ds-list-row-flash once: the "just changed" mark from [liveness](../liveness/component.md), in the tone the row is already wearing. It never loops — what keeps a waiting row loud is ink, not motion.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Rest | Transparent background, text.muted | | Hover | bg.hover, ink lifts to text.default. Background only — no shadow, scale, glow, or border that shifts geometry | | Focus-visible | focus.ring, outline: none. Never on :focus — a mouse click must not draw a ring | | Selected (focused pane) | bg.selected fill + 2px inset accent.primary edge + text.primary | | Selected (resting pane) | bg.selected-resting fill, no edge, + text.default | | Cursored | .ds-list-row-cursor — a 2px text.primary mark in the leading gutter. Only for a list that is one tab stop and walks with aria-activedescendant | | Needs input | --needs-input: status.warn-soft fill, status.warn ink, no ring. Keeps the selection edge underneath when also selected. One-shot flash on entry | | Finished, unseen | --finished: status.good-faint fill, status.good ink, no ring. Keeps the selection edge underneath when also selected. One-shot flash on entry. Clears on open | | Disabled | opacity: 0.5, cursor: not-allowed. Stays in layout and stays readable |

The cursor is a third channel, not a third selection. A list that walks with aria-activedescendant keeps DOM focus on one element, so it has a row the keyboard is *on* that is neither the row a person picked nor the element they are typing in. It cannot borrow either treatment: it must stay visible on a row that is already selected and stay distinct from one that is merely hovered. A gutter mark composes over both fills, which neither fill can do over the other.

It takes text.primary, not the accent: border.focus and accent.primary are the same value in all but one theme, so an accent bar in the gutter reads as a focus ring that has slipped. And a list that *does* move real DOM focus with its cursor renders no mark at all — there the focus ring is already the answer, and one idiom beats two.

Added 2026-09-02, after a conformance sweep replaced two lists' private cursor outlines with bg.hover and made the cursor invisible on every row a person had already picked.

Usage

Actions are withheld until reached for. Per-row actions — remove, reveal in folder, roll back, close — live in .ds-list-row-actions and are invisible at rest. They appear on hover and on keyboard focus. Ceiling: two. A third action belongs in an overflow menu or the detail pane.

The row itself is the <button>, so an action cannot be nested inside it — that is invalid HTML and breaks Safari and JAWS. Wrap the row and its actions in .ds-list-row-host instead, which positions the actions over the row's trailing padding. Declare data-actions="1" or "2" on that host: the actions are positioned absolutely and reserve no width themselves, so the count is what the row reserves its trailing padding from. Without it the text runs under the icons. With it the space is held at rest, so revealing never reflows.

Do not put anything interactive in .ds-list-row-trailing. It is for a count, a timestamp, or a status word.

Titles truncate to one line. If the full value matters, attach the system's tooltip component, and only when the text actually overflows — never a native title attribute on a control.

Accessibility

  • Interactive rows render as <button type="button">. A row that only displays information renders as a <div> and takes no focus.
  • The selected row carries aria-current="true". A single-select list may instead use role="listbox" with role="option" and aria-selected; pick one model and hold to it for the whole list.
  • Every action button has an aria-label naming both the verb and the item ("Remove Engineering"), because the label is read out of the row's context.
  • Leading glyphs are aria-hidden="true" when the title already carries the meaning.
  • Revealed actions must be keyboard-reachable. They are in the tab order and become visible on :focus-within — an action that only exists on hover is unreachable for keyboard and touch users.
  • Status shown by a leading glyph reads by shape, not colour alone, and carries an accessible name when no adjacent text states it.
  • Disabled rows use the disabled attribute (or aria-disabled="true" when they must stay focusable to explain why).
  • Reduced motion removes the reveal fade but never the reveal itself, and drops the attention flash — the fill, ring and ink already carry the state.
  • An attention state is never carried by colour alone: the trailing slot, or a visually-hidden clause inside the title, says "needs input" or "finished".

Known drift

Verified against src/renderer/src/components/ui/InboxRow.tsx (2026-08-04), the shipped counterpart of this row:

  • Padding. The reference CSS uses space.xs / space.md (6/10px); shipped rows use px-3 py-2 (12/8px). Re-pointed 2026-09-02: this is not code drifting from a spec, it is two specs disagreeing. [inbox-row](../inbox-row/component.md) prescribes space.sm block and space.lg inline, which is exactly the 8/12 the code draws. The outlier is this entry's own reference CSS, and one row family cannot have two insets.
  • ~~Title size. This spec sets titles at font.size.body; shipped titles sit at font.size.meta, one step smaller.~~ Resolved — the drift ruling ruled for the spec and moved the code: InboxRow draws its title at font.size.body over supporting text at font.size.meta.
  • --resting mechanics. Shipped rows reach the resting tier via cascade (data-selection-pane rules in assets/index.css) rather than this spec's class modifier — same behaviour, different structure — and the data-actions reserved-padding action host is not implemented (InboxRow's trailing slot is display-only). The cascade half is a ruled difference, not debt; the reserved padding is still owed.
components/list-row/component.css
/* List row — the pick-an-item worklist row, and the most repeated surface in
 * the product: rails, sources, inboxes, categories, search results.
 *
 * Family contract: a neutral selection FILL plus an accent EDGE on the pane
 * being driven, two selection tiers so a multi-pane surface has one such row,
 * background-only hover, and trailing actions that stay hidden until pointed
 * at or focused. */

.ds-list-row {
  /* Positioned so `.ds-list-row-cursor` can hang in the leading gutter. The
     action host is positioned too, but it only exists on rows that reveal
     actions, and a cursor is not conditional on that. */
  position: relative;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
  width: 100%;
  padding: var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-md);
  border: 0;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-default);
  text-align: left;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition:
    background-color var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard),
    color var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

/* Hover is a background change only — no shadow, no scale, no glow, and no
 * border that would shift the row's geometry. */
.ds-list-row:hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
}

.ds-list-row:focus-visible {
  outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
}

.ds-list-row:disabled,
.ds-list-row[aria-disabled='true'] {
  cursor: not-allowed;
  opacity: 0.5;
}

/* ── Selection ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Two tiers. `--selected` is the pane the user is driving; `--resting` is
 * every other pane's remembered choice.
 *
 * `--selected` is a neutral fill PLUS a 2px inset accent edge (owner ruling
 * 2026-09-05). The fill alone lost: one step of neutral grey is the quietest
 * mark on the surface, and any row wearing a status tint — which is a hue,
 * a whole-row wash and an ink change — read as the chosen one instead. The
 * person could not find the row their keyboard was driving.
 *
 * The edge, not the fill: an accent FILL would still be wrong, because the
 * accent's other job is "this is the action worth clicking" and a filled row
 * outranks the button beside it. An edge marks the row without claiming that
 * weight. It is also the same 2px accent border the focused terminal wears
 * (`terminal-focus-ring`), so the row in the rail and the surface it drives
 * carry one mark between them — which is the question this treatment exists
 * to answer.
 *
 * `--resting` takes the fill and NOT the edge. That is the whole two-tier
 * rule made visible: exactly one edge on screen, on the pane with focus.
 *
 * Still ruled out, unchanged: an accent fill, a left bar, a glow. */
.ds-list-row--selected {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected);
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

.ds-list-row--selected:hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected);
}

.ds-list-row--resting {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected-resting);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
}

/* ── Cursor ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * The row the keyboard is on, in a list that is one tab stop and walks with
 * `aria-activedescendant`. A third channel: it has to stay visible on a row
 * that is already selected AND stay distinct from one that is merely hovered,
 * which neither of those two fills can manage over the other.
 *
 * A mark rather than a fill or an outline, and `text.primary` rather than the
 * accent — `border.focus` and `accent.primary` are the same value in all but
 * one theme, so an accent bar in the gutter reads as a slipped focus ring.
 * Mounts inside `.ds-list-row`, which is positioned for it.
 *
 * A list that moves real DOM focus with its cursor renders none of this: the
 * focus ring is already the mark. */
.ds-list-row-cursor {
  position: absolute;
  left: 0;
  top: var(--sem-space-2xs);
  bottom: var(--sem-space-2xs);
  width: var(--sem-space-3xs);
  /* Fully rounded, as the count badge's pill is: on a 2px bar a radius step
     and a pill are the same stub, and matching the pill keeps one spelling
     for "a small round-ended mark". */
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  pointer-events: none;
}

/* ── Leading ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * A status glyph, monogram, or type icon. Never a decorative avatar. */
.ds-list-row-leading {
  flex: none;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: var(--sem-icon-size-lg);
  height: var(--sem-icon-size-lg);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
}

.ds-list-row-leading svg {
  width: var(--sem-icon-size-sm);
  height: var(--sem-icon-size-sm);
}

.ds-list-row--selected .ds-list-row-leading {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
}

/* ── Text ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Title is the row's one priority and claims the width; everything else is
 * demoted to the supporting line or the trailing slot.
 *
 * The text block is a flex row so both children blockify: the ellipsis they
 * declare below is inert on an inline box. The gap also carries the word
 * space between title and supporting that inline layout used to supply. */
.ds-list-row-text {
  min-width: 0;
  flex: 1;
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
}

/* The title claims the width it needs; the supporting clause takes what is
 * left (basis 0) and so truncates first. */
.ds-list-row-title {
  flex: 0 1 auto;
  min-width: 0;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-normal);
  color: inherit;
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

.ds-list-row-supporting {
  flex: 1 1 0;
  min-width: 0;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

/* Identifiers are mono, tabular, and optically opened at this size. */
.ds-list-row-id {
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-wide);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
}

/* ── Trailing ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Display-only: a count, a timestamp, a status word. Never interactive —
 * the row itself renders as the button, and nesting a control inside it is
 * invalid HTML. Row actions go in the actions slot instead. */
.ds-list-row-trailing {
  flex: none;
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
}

/* ── Actions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Withheld until the row is pointed at or focused. The slot reserves its
 * width at rest so revealing never reflows the row, and the actions appear
 * on keyboard focus as well as hover — hover-only is a bug, not a style.
 * Ceiling: two actions. Anything more belongs in an overflow menu. */
.ds-list-row-actions {
  flex: none;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-3xs);
  opacity: 0;
  transition: opacity var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

/* Hover reveal hangs off the host, not the row: in the host pattern the actions
 * are the row's SIBLING, so a descendant selector on the row never matches.
 * The row-scoped focus rule stays for a row used without the host wrapper. */
.ds-list-row-host:hover .ds-list-row-actions,
.ds-list-row-host:focus-within .ds-list-row-actions,
.ds-list-row:focus-visible .ds-list-row-actions,
.ds-list-row-actions:focus-within {
  opacity: 1;
}

/* The row is a button, so its actions live in a sibling wrapper rather than
 * inside it. This is the wrapper's contract. */
.ds-list-row-host {
  position: relative;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
}

.ds-list-row-host .ds-list-row-actions {
  position: absolute;
  right: var(--sem-space-sm);
}

/* The absolute slot reserves no width of its own, so the host declares how
 * many actions it carries and the row reserves that much trailing padding —
 * text truncates before it reaches the icons, and revealing never reflows. */
.ds-list-row-host[data-actions='1'] .ds-list-row {
  padding-right: calc(var(--sem-space-sm) + var(--sem-size-control-xs) + var(--sem-space-xs));
}

.ds-list-row-host[data-actions='2'] .ds-list-row {
  padding-right: calc(
    var(--sem-space-sm) + var(--sem-size-control-xs) * 2 + var(--sem-space-3xs) + var(--sem-space-xs)
  );
}

.ds-list-row-action {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
  height: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
  min-width: var(--sem-size-hit-target-min);
  min-height: var(--sem-size-hit-target-min);
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-chip);
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
  /* Without this the button falls back to the UA font — a third family the
   * system does not have. Latent while the actions are icon-only. */
  font-family: inherit;
  cursor: pointer;
}

.ds-list-row-action:hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-active);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

.ds-list-row-action:focus-visible {
  outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
}

.ds-list-row-action svg {
  width: var(--sem-icon-size-sm);
  height: var(--sem-icon-size-sm);
}

/* ── Attention ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * The two things a row can say on its own: an agent on it is waiting for the
 * person (`--needs-input`), or it finished while they were looking elsewhere
 * and they have not opened it since (`--finished`). Each takes the WHOLE row
 * — a tinted fill and the title in the tone's ink — because a status mark or
 * a chip beside an otherwise quiet row is the weakest possible carrier for
 * the one state that actually wants the person to look (owner ruling
 * 2026-09-04, twice: first the needs-input dot — a mark the product no longer
 * draws anywhere — then the "Done" chip).
 *
 * A FILL, and only a fill. The edge is selection's channel and status may not
 * borrow it (owner ruling 2026-09-05, reversing the ring these two carried).
 * A green ring around a finished row is indistinguishable from the accent
 * edge on the row being driven — and because the ring is the louder of the
 * two marks, a row saying "I finished while you were out" was read as "this
 * is the one you are in". The two questions are answered by two channels:
 * status is the wash, selection is the edge, and a row can wear both at once
 * without either being mistaken for the other.
 *
 * A left bar remains a ruled rejection for both: the leading gutter belongs
 * to the cursor and to identity.
 *
 * `--finished` is one notch under `--needs-input` by construction: it asks
 * for a look, not an answer, so its fill is `status.good-faint` rather than
 * `-soft`. When a row is both, needs-input wins.
 *
 * Both hold until the person opens the row — a finished row clears the moment
 * it becomes the selected one — and both are colour PLUS words: the trailing
 * slot or a visually-hidden clause says "needs input" / "finished" in text. */
.ds-list-row--needs-input {
  background: var(--sem-color-status-warn-soft);
  color: var(--sem-color-status-warn);
}

.ds-list-row--needs-input:hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-status-warn-soft);
}

.ds-list-row--finished {
  background: var(--sem-color-status-good-faint);
  color: var(--sem-color-status-good);
}

.ds-list-row--finished:hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-status-good-faint);
}

/* Nothing to restate for the selected case: these rules declare no
 * `box-shadow`, so the accent edge set by `--selected` survives underneath a
 * status wash untouched. That composition IS the contract — the tint says
 * what happened, the edge says where you are. */

.ds-list-row--needs-input .ds-list-row-supporting,
.ds-list-row--finished .ds-list-row-supporting,
.ds-list-row--needs-input .ds-list-row-trailing,
.ds-list-row--finished .ds-list-row-trailing {
  color: inherit;
  opacity: 0.8;
}

/* The one-shot flash a row plays as it ENTERS either state — "just changed",
 * the second of the two things motion may mean (see liveness). It paints in
 * the tone the row is already wearing, plays once, and stops: what keeps the
 * row loud while it waits is the ink above, never a loop. Painted on a
 * pointer-inert overlay so replaying it never remounts the row. */
.ds-list-row-flash {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  border-radius: inherit;
  pointer-events: none;
  animation: ds-list-row-flash var(--sem-motion-duration-pulse) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard) 1;
}

.ds-list-row--needs-input .ds-list-row-flash {
  --ds-row-flash-tint: var(--sem-color-status-warn);
  --ds-row-flash-fill: var(--sem-color-status-warn-soft);
}

.ds-list-row--finished .ds-list-row-flash {
  --ds-row-flash-tint: var(--sem-color-status-good);
  --ds-row-flash-fill: var(--sem-color-status-good-soft);
}

@keyframes ds-list-row-flash {
  0% {
    background: var(--ds-row-flash-fill);
    box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--ds-row-flash-tint);
  }
  100% {
    background: transparent;
    box-shadow: none;
  }
}

/* Reduced motion removes the fade, never the reveal itself — the actions
 * must still become available. The attention flash drops entirely: the
 * fill, ring and ink already carry the state. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .ds-list-row,
  .ds-list-row-actions {
    transition: none;
  }

  .ds-list-row-flash {
    animation: none;
  }
}
components/list-row/component.html (demo)
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8" />
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
<title>List row</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../../foundations/tokens.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="component.css" />
<style>
  body {
    margin: 0;
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  }
  .demo-stage {
    padding: var(--sem-space-3xl);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-app);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  }
  .demo-label {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
  }
  .demo-panes {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr));
    gap: var(--sem-space-lg);
  }
  .demo-pane {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-overlay);
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm);
  }
  .demo-pane-title {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
    padding: var(--sem-space-2xs) var(--sem-space-md) var(--sem-space-sm);
  }
  /* Deliberately the narrowest pane the grid allows: the width at which
     truncation and the reserved action slot are actually exercised. A demo
     whose strings never overflow cannot show whether either one works. */
  .demo-pane--narrow {
    max-width: 220px;
  }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="demo-stage" data-mode="light">
  <p class="demo-label">Light — a rail → list → detail surface. Only the focused pane carries the strong selection.</p>
  <div class="demo-panes">

    <div class="demo-pane">
      <p class="demo-pane-title">Marketplace — focused</p>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row">
        <span class="ds-list-row-leading" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 14 14" fill="none"><path d="M7 1.5l1.7 3.5 3.8.5-2.8 2.7.7 3.8L7 10.2 3.6 12l.7-3.8L1.5 5.5l3.8-.5z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-list-row-text">
          <span class="ds-list-row-title">Featured</span>
          <span class="ds-list-row-supporting">2 ready to launch</span>
        </span>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row ds-list-row--selected" aria-current="true">
        <span class="ds-list-row-leading" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 14 14" fill="none"><rect x="2.5" y="1.5" width="9" height="11" rx="1.4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2"/><path d="M5 5h4M5 7.5h4M5 10h2.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-list-row-text">
          <span class="ds-list-row-title">Skills</span>
          <span class="ds-list-row-supporting">6 sources · 368 skills</span>
        </span>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row">
        <span class="ds-list-row-leading" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 14 14" fill="none"><path d="M7 1.8l4.5 2.6v5.2L7 12.2 2.5 9.6V4.4z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-list-row-text">
          <span class="ds-list-row-title">Modules</span>
          <span class="ds-list-row-supporting">0 available</span>
        </span>
      </button>
    </div>

    <div class="demo-pane">
      <p class="demo-pane-title">Sources — resting</p>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row">
        <span class="ds-list-row-text">
          <span class="ds-list-row-title">SprintEngine</span>
          <span class="ds-list-row-supporting">12 skills</span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-list-row-trailing">2m</span>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row ds-list-row--resting" aria-current="true">
        <span class="ds-list-row-text">
          <span class="ds-list-row-title">Matt Pocock</span>
          <span class="ds-list-row-supporting">41 skills</span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-list-row-trailing">14m</span>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row">
        <span class="ds-list-row-text">
          <span class="ds-list-row-title">browser-act</span>
          <span class="ds-list-row-supporting">103 skills</span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-list-row-trailing">1h</span>
      </button>
    </div>

    <div class="demo-pane">
      <p class="demo-pane-title">Cursor — a third channel, readable on the selected row</p>
      <!-- A list that walks with `aria-activedescendant` keeps one tab stop, so
           the row the keyboard is on is neither the row a person picked nor the
           element they are typing in. The cursor sits on the SELECTED row here,
           which is the case a hover fill cannot draw. -->
      <div role="listbox" aria-label="Skill sources" tabindex="0" aria-activedescendant="lr-cursor-light-2">
        <div role="option" id="lr-cursor-light-1" aria-selected="false" class="ds-list-row">
          <span class="ds-list-row-text">
            <span class="ds-list-row-title">anthropics/skills</span>
          </span>
        </div>
        <div role="option" id="lr-cursor-light-2" aria-selected="true" class="ds-list-row ds-list-row--selected">
          <span class="ds-list-row-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
          <span class="ds-list-row-text">
            <span class="ds-list-row-title">mattpocock/skills</span>
          </span>
        </div>
        <div role="option" id="lr-cursor-light-3" aria-selected="false" class="ds-list-row">
          <span class="ds-list-row-text">
            <span class="ds-list-row-title">pbakaus/impeccable</span>
          </span>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="demo-pane">
      <p class="demo-pane-title">Hover or tab a row to reveal its actions</p>
      <div class="ds-list-row-host" data-actions="2">
        <button type="button" class="ds-list-row">
          <span class="ds-list-row-text">
            <span class="ds-list-row-title">Engineering</span>
            <span class="ds-list-row-supporting"><span class="ds-list-row-id">MC-1931</span> · 17 skills</span>
          </span>
        </button>
        <span class="ds-list-row-actions">
          <button type="button" class="ds-list-row-action" aria-label="Reveal Engineering in folder">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 14 14" fill="none" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M1.8 3.6h3.4l1.1 1.4h5.9v5.4H1.8z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>
          </button>
          <button type="button" class="ds-list-row-action" aria-label="Remove Engineering">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 14 14" fill="none" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M3.25 3.25L10.75 10.75M10.75 3.25L3.25 10.75" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>
          </button>
        </span>
      </div>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row">
        <span class="ds-list-row-text">
          <span class="ds-list-row-title">Productivity</span>
          <span class="ds-list-row-supporting"><span class="ds-list-row-id">MC-1928</span> · 5 skills</span>
        </span>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row" disabled>
        <span class="ds-list-row-text">
          <span class="ds-list-row-title">Deprecated</span>
          <span class="ds-list-row-supporting">Unavailable while the source reindexes</span>
        </span>
      </button>
    </div>

    <div class="demo-pane">
      <p class="demo-pane-title">Attention — the row is the mark; gold outranks green</p>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row ds-list-row--needs-input">
        <span class="ds-list-row-flash" aria-hidden="true"></span>
        <span class="ds-list-row-text">
          <span class="ds-list-row-title">There are a couple of branches</span>
          <span class="ds-list-row-supporting">main · +114 −54</span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-list-row-trailing">needs input</span>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row ds-list-row--finished">
        <span class="ds-list-row-flash" aria-hidden="true"></span>

Liveness

Alive right now — unbounded work on a row that stays readable. Each chat keeps one of four patterns.

Reviewing the changeset orbit
Mapping the router ripple
Planning the migration think
Running the test suite snake

Just changed — one shot, in a status colour that already applies

3 errors

The pulse is decoration: the count beside it is what actually says three. The working mark carries a required label, because "working" is information and a purely visual liveness cue is invisible to a screen reader. With reduced motion every pattern holds the same still frame.

The marks that say something is happening, and the one that says something just changed.

Motion here carries information first: something is alive right now, or something just changed. It is also allowed a little character (ruling 2026-09-28): a working mark picks one of four patterns so a list of working chats does not tick in step, and a spawned agent is drawn as a small [agent glyph](../agent-glyph/component.md) that moves while it works. What motion never does is decorate something at rest. A mark that moves while nothing is happening teaches people to ignore movement.

| Mark | Means | Shipped as | |---|---|---| | Working mark | alive right now, for an unknown duration | ui/WorkingMark.tsx | | Agent glyph | this spawned agent is working, or how it ended | [agent-glyph](../agent-glyph/component.md) | | Change pulse | just changed, one shot | ui/ChangePulse.tsx | | Spinner | alive right now, for a bounded wait | [spinner](../spinner/component.md) | | Working edge | alive right now, on a surface whose content stays readable meanwhile | [working-edge](../working-edge/component.md) |

Working mark

A 3×3 grid of small square cells in accent.primary, 14px across, every cell resting dim. One of four patterns lights them, on a pure-CSS keyframe loop:

| Pattern | Movement | |---|---| | Orbit | a lit cell runs round the edge, trailing a fading tail; the centre holds still | | Ripple | a diagonal wave washes across, corner to corner | | Think | cells light in a shuffled order, like it is working something out | | Snake | a three-cell snake slithers round the edge; the centre holds still |

The pattern is picked from a seed, the id of the chat or agent that is working, so a chat keeps its pattern for as long as it works and a row of working chats spreads across all four. Use the mark where work is genuinely in flight and has no predictable end: an agent running, a job with no progress to report.

It is not a spinner substitute. A spinner says "wait, this will finish"; the mark says "this is ongoing", which is why it lives on a row that stays readable and interactive around it rather than over a blocked surface.

Change pulse

A one-shot tint-and-glow that eases back to rest when a watched number moves. It paints in the status colour that already applies — passed in as a tint — so it never introduces a new accent, and it never fires on first render, only on a change from a value that was already on screen.

Wrap the icon, not the number. The pulse is decoration; the real count stays on a sibling [badge](../badge/component.md) or in the control's accessible name, so nothing depends on having seen the animation.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Rest | no motion at all: the mark is absent, the pulse static | | Live | the mark's pattern cycles; the surface around it stays interactive | | Changed | one pulse, then rest — never a repeat, never a loop | | Reduced motion | every working mark holds one still frame, the four corners and the centre lit; the pulse does not play |

Reduced motion is handled in the stylesheet rather than in each component, so a consumer cannot forget it: the same class that animates is the class that carries the prefers-reduced-motion guard. The still frame is the same for all four patterns, so "working" reads one way to someone who has turned motion off. It is never a dot.

Every loop also holds still while the window is hidden or in the background, and a transcript row pauses its own when it scrolls out of view.

Accessibility

  • The working mark is role="img" with a required label — "Agent working" is information, and a purely visual liveness cue is invisible to a screen reader.
  • The change pulse is decorative only and takes no ARIA. Whatever changed is announced by the thing that actually changed — the badge count, the status line — not by the animation.
  • No mark may be the only carrier of its meaning. Someone with reduced motion, or not looking at that corner of the screen when it fired, must still be able to find out.

Usage

  • One liveness mark per row. A working mark *and* a spinner *and* a pulsing badge on the same row is three components saying one thing.
  • Seed the mark with the id of what is working, never with something that changes while it works, or the pattern will jump.
  • Never pulse on a value the person just typed. The pulse means "this changed underneath you"; replaying their own edit back at them is noise.
  • Motion is not emphasis. Something important but static gets ink, weight or a tone — never movement.
  • Never a status dot. State is a word, a glyph, a timer, a working mark or an agent glyph (ruling 2026-09-28).
components/liveness/component.css
/* Liveness — the working mark and the change pulse.
 *
 * Both animations live here rather than in the consuming component, so the
 * `prefers-reduced-motion` guard cannot be forgotten by a caller: the class
 * that animates is the class that carries the guard. */

/* ── working mark: alive right now, unbounded ─────────────────────────────── */

/* A 3×3 grid of cells resting dim; a pattern lights them. Each cell's delay
 * into its pattern's loop is written by the consumer (--ds-cell-delay), so the
 * four patterns share one set of cells. */
.ds-working-mark {
  display: inline-grid;
  flex: none;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 3px);
  grid-auto-rows: 3px;
  gap: var(--sem-space-3xs);
  place-content: center;
  width: 14px;
  height: 14px;
}

.ds-working-mark-cell {
  /* Softened, never round: a round cell would read as a dot. */
  border-radius: 0.8px;
  background: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  opacity: 0.16;
  animation-delay: var(--ds-cell-delay, 0s);
}

.ds-working-mark--orbit .ds-working-mark-cell {
  animation: ds-working-mark-orbit 1.2s linear infinite;
  animation-delay: var(--ds-cell-delay, 0s);
}
.ds-working-mark--ripple .ds-working-mark-cell {
  animation: ds-working-mark-ripple 1.3s var(--sem-motion-ease-standard) infinite;
  animation-delay: var(--ds-cell-delay, 0s);
}
.ds-working-mark--think .ds-working-mark-cell {
  animation: ds-working-mark-think 1.8s var(--sem-motion-ease-standard) infinite;
  animation-delay: var(--ds-cell-delay, 0s);
}
.ds-working-mark--snake .ds-working-mark-cell {
  animation: ds-working-mark-snake 1.6s linear infinite;
  animation-delay: var(--ds-cell-delay, 0s);
}
/* The edge patterns leave the centre cell at rest. */
.ds-working-mark .ds-working-mark-cell--still {
  animation: none;
}

@keyframes ds-working-mark-orbit {
  0% {
    opacity: 1;
  }
  12% {
    opacity: 0.75;
  }
  30% {
    opacity: 0.3;
  }
  45%,
  100% {
    opacity: 0.16;
  }
}

@keyframes ds-working-mark-ripple {
  0%,
  70%,
  100% {
    opacity: 0.16;
    transform: scale(0.7);
  }
  35% {
    opacity: 1;
    transform: scale(1);
  }
}

@keyframes ds-working-mark-think {
  0%,
  40%,
  100% {
    opacity: 0.16;
  }
  15% {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}

/* Head plus two tail cells: each edge cell is lit for three of eight steps. */
@keyframes ds-working-mark-snake {
  0%,
  37% {
    opacity: 1;
  }
  37.5%,
  100% {
    opacity: 0.16;
  }
}

/* ── change pulse: just changed, one shot ──────────────────────────────────── */

/* The tint is written by the consumer as --ds-pulse-tint and is always a status
 * colour that ALREADY applies to the thing being marked, so the pulse never
 * introduces an accent of its own. */
.ds-change-pulse {
  animation: ds-change-pulse var(--sem-motion-duration-pulse) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard) 1;
}

@keyframes ds-change-pulse {
  0% {
    color: var(--ds-pulse-tint, currentColor);
    transform: scale(1);
  }
  35% {
    color: var(--ds-pulse-tint, currentColor);
    transform: scale(1.12);
  }
  100% {
    transform: scale(1);
  }
}

/* One guard, every mark. Reduced motion keeps the INFORMATION — one still
 * frame, the four corners and the centre lit, still says "working" whichever
 * pattern was picked — and drops only the movement. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .ds-working-mark .ds-working-mark-cell {
    animation: none;
    opacity: 0.16;
    transform: none;
  }

  .ds-working-mark .ds-working-mark-cell:nth-child(odd) {
    opacity: 0.9;
  }

  .ds-change-pulse {
    animation: none;
  }
}
