<!-- The live confirm the triggers open. One instance, moved over the page and
     re-labelled per ask — one modal at a time is the contract, so one node is
     also the honest implementation. -->
<div class="ds-modal-scrim" id="live-scrim" hidden>
  <div class="ds-modal ds-modal--confirm" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="live-title" tabindex="-1">
    <div class="ds-modal-header">
      <h2 class="ds-modal-title" id="live-title">Delete workspace?</h2>
      <button type="button" class="ds-button ds-button--icon" aria-label="Close" data-cancel>
        <svg viewBox="0 0 14 14" fill="none" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M3.25 3.25L10.75 10.75M10.75 3.25L3.25 10.75" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>
      </button>
    </div>
    <div class="ds-modal-body" id="live-body">Its worktree and uncommitted changes are removed. This cannot be undone from here.</div>
    <div class="ds-modal-footer">
      <button type="button" class="ds-button ds-button--ghost" data-cancel>Cancel</button>
      <button type="button" class="ds-button ds-button--md" id="live-confirm">Delete</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
/* Reference behaviour for the contract in component.md. What must survive a
   framework rewrite: the focus trap, initial focus on the confirm button,
   focus restored to the opener, Escape / scrim-press / close all meaning
   cancel, and pointerdown on the scrim ITSELF — a drag that ends outside the
   shell must not dismiss. */

const scrim = document.getElementById('live-scrim')
const shell = scrim.querySelector('.ds-modal')
const titleOut = document.getElementById('live-title')
const bodyOut = document.getElementById('live-body')
const confirmButton = document.getElementById('live-confirm')

const ASKS = {
  danger: {
    title: 'Delete workspace?',
    body: 'Its worktree and uncommitted changes are removed. This cannot be undone from here.',
    confirm: 'Delete',
    buttonClass: 'ds-button ds-button--md ds-button--danger',
  },
  primary: {
    title: 'Archive automation?',
    body: 'It leaves the Automations rail. Its run history and branches stay.',
    confirm: 'Archive',
    buttonClass: 'ds-button ds-button--md ds-button--primary',
  },
}

let opener = null

const FOCUSABLE =
  'a[href], button:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]):not([type="hidden"]), select:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])'

function openModal(trigger) {
  const ask = ASKS[trigger.dataset.tone]
  titleOut.textContent = ask.title
  bodyOut.textContent = ask.body
  confirmButton.textContent = ask.confirm
  confirmButton.className = ask.buttonClass
  /* The overlay sits on the body; mirror the mode of the container that
     opened it so it is lit by that container, not by the page default. */
  const scope = trigger.closest('[data-mode]')
  if (scope) scrim.setAttribute('data-mode', scope.dataset.mode)
  opener = trigger
  scrim.hidden = false
  confirmButton.focus()
}

function closeModal() {
  scrim.hidden = true
  opener?.focus()
  opener = null
}

for (const trigger of document.querySelectorAll('[data-open-confirm]')) {
  trigger.addEventListener('click', () => openModal(trigger))
}
for (const cancel of scrim.querySelectorAll('[data-cancel]')) {
  cancel.addEventListener('click', closeModal)
}
confirmButton.addEventListener('click', closeModal)

/* Pointer-down on the scrim itself — not a click that merely ENDS there. */
scrim.addEventListener('pointerdown', (event) => {
  if (event.target === scrim) closeModal()
})

/* Escape cancels. In the full system a popover open inside the modal consumes
   Escape first (topmost surface only); this demo hosts none. */
document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  if (!scrim.hidden && event.key === 'Escape') {
    event.preventDefault()
    closeModal()
  }
})

/* The focus trap — the contract shipped Modal.tsx does not yet honour
   (MC-2109). Tab from the last control wraps to the first and Shift+Tab from
   the first wraps to the last; the scrimmed page is unreachable by keyboard. */
document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  if (scrim.hidden || event.key !== 'Tab') return
  const focusables = [...shell.querySelectorAll(FOCUSABLE)]
  if (focusables.length === 0) {
    event.preventDefault()
    shell.focus()
    return
  }
  const first = focusables[0]
  const last = focusables[focusables.length - 1]
  const active = document.activeElement
  if (event.shiftKey && (active === first || !shell.contains(active))) {
    event.preventDefault()
    last.focus()
  } else if (!event.shiftKey && (active === last || !shell.contains(active))) {
    event.preventDefault()
    first.focus()
  }
})
</script>
</body>
</html>

Pager

Light — a long source: first and last page always reachable, an elision between.

Showing 13–24 of 318 …

One page — the numbers are gone; the sentence stays, because the count is still news.

Showing 1–8 of 8

--inline — the stepper inside a band: n/m between two 26px chevrons, no sentence drawn and no foot padding. The sentence is still said, as the position's accessible name.

2/27

Dark — first page: previous is disabled rather than absent, so the strip never reflows.

Showing 1–12 of 318 …

--inline — the stepper inside a band: n/m between two 26px chevrons, no sentence drawn and no foot padding. The sentence is still said, as the position's accessible name.

1/27

The foot of a list that is walked one page at a time: the position said in words on the left, the page controls on the right.

Use a pager when a list is longer than a person will scroll and its order means something — a catalogue of 318 connectors kept in categories, a repository's skills kept in folders. Use progressive disclosure ("Show N more") only for a short tail inside one section. Use infinite scroll for a feed, where position does not matter and there is no last page.

A pager exists because the toggle it replaces cannot state a position. "Show 25 more" grows the page without ever saying how much is left, it forgets where you were the moment you leave, and three sections each expanded to a different depth is a list with no position at all.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Root | .ds-pager | yes — <nav> with an aria-label naming what is paged | | Range | .ds-pager-range | yes — the position in words, tabular, a polite live region | | Controls | .ds-pager-controls | no — absent when there is only one page | | Step | .ds-pager-step | yes (with controls) — previous, each page number, next | | Elision | .ds-pager-gap | no — … standing for skipped numbers, aria-hidden | | Icon | .ds-pager-icon | no — the chevrons, icon.size.xs, aria-hidden | | Position | .ds-pager-position | --inline only — n/m, tabular, carrying the sentence as its accessible name |

Steps sit size.control.sm (30px) tall and at least that wide, spaced by space.3xs, with space.md inline padding so a three-digit page still fits its box. The row is separated from the list above it by space.lg of top padding and nothing else — the list's own last row is the only edge it needs.

Variants

There is one pager. What changes is how much of it is there:

  • Paged — the range plus the controls.
  • Single page — the range alone. The count is still news ("Showing 1–8 of 8"); a strip of one number is not.
  • Empty — the range says what is missing ("Nothing matches “stripe”", "No plugins here") and there are no controls. An empty list still gets its sentence, because the alternative is a blank region that reads as broken.

…and one modifier, for a pager that is not the foot of anything:

  • --inline (2026-09-09) — the pager as a stepper inside a band: n/m in tabular-nums between two size.control.xs chevrons, sitting in a [toolbar](../toolbar/component.md) beside other controls. The diff window's file stepper is what it was drawn for — "2/27" between the hunk arrows and the view toggle.

Three things go, all for the same reason (the band has no width to spend on them): the numbered strip, the words sentence, and the foot padding. The chevrons drop to size.control.xs so the stepper sits level with the button --icon items beside it rather than standing a step taller.

What does not go is the rule that makes a pager a pager. The ends stay reachable, and the chevrons are *disabled* at them, never absent — removing them reflows the band under the pointer that is clicking them. And the sentence does not disappear: it moves to the position's accessible name, so a screen reader still hears "File 2 of 27" while the drawing shrinks to "2/27".

Use it only where a foot does not exist. A list with a bottom edge gets the full pager; n/m in a band is a compression, and compressions are paid for.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Rest | text.muted on a transparent ground | | Hover | bg.hover and an ink lift to text.primary | | Current page | bg.selected + text.primary + font.weight.medium, marked aria-current="page" | | Focus-visible | focus.ring | | Disabled | opacity: 0.5, cursor: not-allowed — previous on page 1, next on the last | | Inline position | .ds-pager-position at text.muted, tabular. Never the accent: "where am I" is a state display |

Usage

The current page is neutral. bg.selected plus an ink lift, exactly as a selected segment. An accent-filled page number is a reject on sight: the accent is the view's one primary action, and "which page am I on" is a state display.

The ends stay reachable. Always draw page 1 and the last page, plus a window around the current one, and elide the rest. The strip's width must not grow with the source — a 27-page catalogue and a 3-page one draw the same number of buttons. A single skipped page is drawn rather than elided: 1 … 3 is wider than 1 2 3 and hides more.

Previous and next are disabled, not absent. Removing them at the ends reflows the strip under the pointer that is clicking it.

One pager per region. It walks the whole region, groups included: a group that does not fit continues onto the next page under a heading that says so. Two pagers, or a pager per group, is a list with two positions.

Say the position in words. "Showing 13–24 of 318" is the whole point. Numbers alone tell you where you can go, not where you are. --inline is the one place the words are not *drawn*, and even there they are still said: the sentence becomes the position's accessible name rather than being dropped.

Paging replaces rows; it must not move focus. The clicked page button keeps focus, so the range sentence is a role="status" live region — that announcement is the only signal a screen-reader user gets that the list changed.

Accessibility

  • The root is <nav> with a required aria-label naming what is being paged ("Plugins in SprintEngine Studio"), so a page with several lists does not present several identical "pagination" landmarks.
  • Page numbers are <button>s; the current one carries aria-current="page" and every one carries an aria-label ("Page 3") so the number is not read as a bare digit.
  • Previous and next are aria-labelled; their chevrons are aria-hidden.
  • The elision is aria-hidden — it names no page.
  • The range is role="status" aria-live="polite", and it is the only live region in the pager. On --inline the position takes that role, and an aria-label carrying the full sentence — so the visible "2/27" and the announced "File 2 of 27" are one element, and there is still exactly one live region.
  • Tab order is the natural one: the strip is a row of ordinary buttons, not a roving-tabindex composite. A pager is reached rarely and left immediately, so a person tabbing to page 4 should not first have to discover that arrow keys drive it.

Shipped implementation

src/renderer/src/components/ui/Pager.tsx, exporting Pager (the row, with an inline prop) and pagerSteps (which numbers to draw, given the page and the count). What a page CONTAINS is not the primitive's business: the consumer's own model slices its groups and hands over page, pageCount and the range sentence. The Extensions catalogues' model is src/renderer/src/components/workspace/globalSurface/extensions/catalogue/cataloguePaging.ts.

components/pager/component.css
/* Pager — the foot of a list walked one page at a time
 * (src/renderer/src/components/ui/Pager.tsx).
 *
 * Two halves on one line: the position said in words on the left, the page
 * controls on the right. Nothing here is filled with the accent — the current
 * page is a neutral luminance step plus an ink lift, the same treatment a
 * selected segment gets, because "where I am" is a state display and the
 * accent budget belongs to the view's one primary action. */

.ds-pager {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--sem-space-lg);
  padding-top: var(--sem-space-lg);
}

/* The position, in words. A live region in the shipped implementation: paging
 * replaces the rows without moving focus, so this sentence is the only thing
 * that announces the change. */
.ds-pager-range {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
}

.ds-pager-controls {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-3xs);
}

.ds-pager-step {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
  min-width: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-md);
  border: 0;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition:
    background-color var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard),
    color var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

.ds-pager-step:hover:not(:disabled):not([aria-current='page']) {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

.ds-pager-step[aria-current='page'] {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
}

.ds-pager-step:focus-visible {
  outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
}

.ds-pager-step:disabled {
  opacity: 0.5;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}

/* The elision. Decorative — the numbers on either side already say which
 * pages are reachable — so it is aria-hidden in the markup. */
.ds-pager-gap {
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-xs);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
}

.ds-pager-icon {
  width: var(--sem-icon-size-xs);
  height: var(--sem-icon-size-xs);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .ds-pager-step {
    transition: none;
  }
}

/* ── Inline (2026-09-09) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * The pager as a STEPPER inside a band: `n/m` between two chevrons, sitting in
 * a toolbar beside other controls rather than under a list.
 *
 * The diff window's file stepper is what it was drawn for — "2/27" between the
 * hunk arrows and the view toggle — where the foot of a list does not exist and
 * there is no room for a sentence.
 *
 * Three things go, and each for the same reason (the band has no width to spend
 * on them): the numbered strip, the words sentence, and the foot padding. What
 * does NOT go is the rule that makes a pager a pager — the ends stay reachable
 * and the chevrons are DISABLED there, never absent, because removing them
 * reflows the band under the pointer that is clicking them.
 *
 * The sentence does not disappear either; it moves to the position's accessible
 * name, so the announcement is unchanged while the drawing shrinks to "2/27". */
.ds-pager--inline {
  display: inline-flex;
  justify-content: flex-start;
  gap: var(--sem-space-3xs);
  padding-top: 0;
}

/* Square chevrons at the band's own control step, so the stepper sits level
 * with the `button --icon` items beside it instead of standing a step taller. */
.ds-pager--inline .ds-pager-step {
  height: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
  min-width: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
  padding: 0;
}

/* The position itself. Tabular so the band does not twitch as the number grows
 * a digit, and muted because "where am I" is a state display — the same reason
 * the numbered strip never takes the accent. */
.ds-pager-position {
  flex: none;
  padding-inline: var(--sem-space-2xs);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
  white-space: nowrap;
}

Light — the full band: identity dot, title, count, scope, one action, one overflow.

Checklist

Panel content.

Flush — a search row follows, so the divider belongs under the search. One line per panel.

The list starts here.

Checklist

3/7
Panel content.

The one header contract for every panel: a single 34px band carrying the panel's name, its canonical count, an optional scope word, and at most two controls. Extracted from the shipped PanelHeader primitive (src/renderer/src/components/ui/PanelHeader.tsx); the panel-header rollout rolls this anatomy out to every panel that still draws its own header.

A panel gets exactly one of these. A header stacked on a toolbar is the two-bands-of-chrome defect the principles reject on sight — the controls belong in this band, and a status belongs to the thing that has it.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Header | .ds-panel-header | yes — a <header> band, bg.surface, one bottom hairline | | Identity dot | .ds-panel-header-identity | no — 6px, colored by the consumer's identity channel | | Title | .ds-panel-header-title | yes — an <h2>, font.size.body at font.weight.emphasis, text.primary, truncates | | Count | .ds-panel-header-count | no — the canonical count, mono-free, tabular, text.muted | | Scope | .ds-panel-header-scope | no — one word of context after a · separator | | Actions | .ds-panel-header-actions | no — the primary action and an overflow trigger, nothing else | | Progress | .ds-panel-header-progress | no — a 2px completion hairline overlaying the bottom border |

The band is 34px (size.control.md): space.sm block insets around a body-size title line. Inline insets are space.lg. Everything in the band centers on one baseline; nothing wraps.

The title truncates, the scope evaporates. The scope word gives up its space first and disappears entirely before the title loses a character — a panel that clips its own name to "Bac…" while a scope word sits whole beside it has the priority backwards. Pair the title with truncated-text so the full name is recoverable when it is actually cut off.

Variants

  • Default — bottom hairline at border.default. This is the panel's chrome edge.
  • --flush — no hairline. Use only when a search row follows immediately: one divider per panel, and it belongs under the search — that is the line that says "the list starts here" (see patterns/list-surface). A rule above the search as well boxes it into a strip of its own.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Rest | bg.surface, title at text.primary | | With progress | The 2px hairline sits on the bottom border, accent fill for done, status.warn segment after it for blocked | | Progress change | Width animates at motion.duration.normal, motion.ease.standard |

The header itself has no hover, selected, or disabled state — it is chrome, not a control. Its actions carry their own states.

Usage

One primary action, then overflow. The actions slot holds at most one labeled action and one overflow trigger. A second visible control means the first two are competing; move it into the overflow menu.

The count is the canonical count. Render it here or in the content, never both — two counts that could disagree are the defect the principles name.

The identity dot is identity, not status. It marks which tool owns the panel, using the consumer's identity color channel (--ds-panel-header-identity — the app supplies its per-tool value; there is no sem.* token for tool identity, deliberately). It never pulses, never changes tone, and the rest of the panel stays accent-neutral around it. Status belongs to rows and their status marks, not to the header — and a status is never a dot (owner ruling 2026-09-28), which is what keeps this one reading as identity.

The progress hairline is earned. Attach it only when the panel has a canonical completion metric (done of total). It is not decoration, not a loading bar, and not a second accent — it is the accent-as-hairline marking real progress, which the accent budget permits.

No status chips, no counts line, no subtitle sentence. The panel under the band already shows its own state. A scope word ("This project") is the ceiling; a sentence is a redesign signal.

Accessibility

  • The band renders as <header>; the title is a real <h2> so the panel lands in the document outline. Give it an id when a region's aria-labelledby points at it.
  • The identity dot is aria-hidden="true" — the title already names the panel; the dot only colors it.
  • The progress hairline carries role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, and an aria-label that states the metric ("3 of 7 steps done"). A 2px line is invisible to a screen reader without it.
  • Overflowed controls stay reachable: anything demoted to the overflow menu is still in the tab order once the menu opens.

Known drift

  • PanelHeader.tsx animates the progress fill over 200ms; the motion ramp has no such step. Canon is motion.duration.normal (180ms). Fold into the panel-header rollout.
components/panel-header/component.css
/* Panel header — the one header contract for every panel: a single 34px band
 * (size.control.md) carrying name, canonical count, optional scope, and at
 * most two controls. Extracted from the shipped PanelHeader primitive
 * (src/renderer/src/components/ui/PanelHeader.tsx); the panel-header rollout rolls this
 * anatomy out to every panel that still draws its own header.
 *
 * Family contract: one band of chrome per panel — a header stacked on a
 * toolbar is the second band the composition principles exist to prevent.
 * The header is chrome, not a control: it has no hover or selected state of
 * its own. */

.ds-panel-header {
  position: relative;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--sem-space-lg);
  box-sizing: border-box;
  min-height: var(--sem-size-control-md);
  padding: var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-lg);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-default);
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
}

/* One divider per panel, and when a search row follows it belongs under the
 * search — the line that says "the list starts here". This modifier hands
 * the hairline to that row instead of drawing two. */
.ds-panel-header--flush {
  border-bottom: 0;
}

/* Title cluster: dot, title, count, scope on one baseline. min-width lets
 * the title truncate instead of pushing the actions off the band. */
.ds-panel-header-lead {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
  min-width: 0;
}

/* 6px identity dot — which tool owns the panel, never a status. The color
 * comes through a consumer channel because tool identity deliberately has no
 * sem.* token; the fallback is the neutral status ink so an unwired demo
 * still renders honestly. Sized by the space.xs step. A disc is allowed here
 * only because it is identity: the product draws no status dots, so a small
 * disc is never how a state is said. */
.ds-panel-header-identity {
  flex: none;
  width: var(--sem-space-xs);
  height: var(--sem-space-xs);
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--ds-panel-header-identity, var(--sem-color-status-neutral));
}

/* The panel's name: body size at the emphasis weight, the strongest ink.
 * An <h2> in the markup, restated here so heading UA styles cannot leak. */
.ds-panel-header-title {
  margin: 0;
  min-width: 0;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-normal);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-default);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

.ds-panel-header-count {
  flex: none;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
}

/* The scope word shrinks far ahead of the title (flex-shrink 100): it gives
 * up its space first, and the title only starts truncating once the scope is
 * gone. A panel that clips its own name while a context word beside it stays
 * whole has the priority backwards. */
.ds-panel-header-scope {
  flex-shrink: 100;
  min-width: 0;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

.ds-panel-header-scope::before {
  content: '·';
  margin-inline: var(--sem-space-xs);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-disabled);
}

/* At most one primary action and one overflow trigger. A third control means
 * the first two are competing — move it into the overflow menu. */
.ds-panel-header-actions {
  flex: none;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-2xs);
}

/* ── Progress ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * A 2px completion hairline overlaying the bottom border — the accent as a
 * hairline marking real progress, which the accent budget permits. Attach
 * only when the panel has a canonical completion metric; it is not a
 * loading bar. Widths arrive as percentages through two custom properties. */
.ds-panel-header-progress {
  pointer-events: none;
  position: absolute;
  left: 0;
  right: 0;
  bottom: -1px;
  height: 2px;
}

.ds-panel-header-progress-fill {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  left: 0;
  width: var(--ds-panel-header-progress, 0%);
  background: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  transition: width var(--sem-motion-duration-normal) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

/* Optional second segment (blocked work) drawn after the accent fill. A
 * status hue as a hairline, not a chrome tint. */
.ds-panel-header-progress-warn {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  left: var(--ds-panel-header-progress, 0%);
  width: var(--ds-panel-header-progress-warn, 0%);
  background: var(--sem-color-status-warn);
  transition:
    width var(--sem-motion-duration-normal) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard),
    left var(--sem-motion-duration-normal) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .ds-panel-header-progress-fill,
  .ds-panel-header-progress-warn {
    transition: none;
  }
}

Popover

Light — click the trigger for the anchored surface; right-click the canvas for the pointer variant. Escape closes the topmost surface only; scrolling repositions, it does not dismiss.

The cursor-error variant — the one surface in the family with a caret, because the click that raised it left nothing on screen to anchor to. Collapsed to one line, and expanded to the full message with copy.

The anchored overlay engine. One surface, lifted to the end of <body> and positioned in fixed viewport coordinates, so it escapes every scroll container and stacking context on the page. Everything dropdown-shaped in the product — overflow menus, filter menus, select listboxes, pickers — composes this shell rather than owning its own portal, its own Escape handler, and its own outside-click logic. Extracted from the source product's Popover and PointerPopover primitives (src/renderer/src/components/ui/).

Use a tooltip instead when the content is a description and nothing in it is clickable — a surface that can swallow a click is a popover, and the two have different keyboard contracts. Use a modal when the task must block the page: a popover is light-dismiss by design and never scrims.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Trigger | — | the consumer's own control, carrying aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, and — only while open — aria-controls | | Surface | .ds-popover | yes — role="menu", "listbox", or "dialog", with a required aria-label and a stable id | | Content | — | host-owned; the shell carries chrome only and no padding of its own | | Scope body | .ds-popover-scope-body | a named content part — see below | | Scope heading | .ds-popover-scope-heading | scope body — font.size.meta at font.weight.emphasis | | Scope headline | .ds-popover-scope-headline | scope body — the second heading on a line with its inline action | | Scope list | .ds-popover-scope-list | scope body — mono identifiers at font.size.meta, one per line | | Scope list (missing) | .ds-popover-scope-list--missing | scope body — the ungranted set, one ink step quieter | | Scope rule | .ds-popover-scope-rule | scope body — the hairline between the two groups | | Scope note | .ds-popover-scope-note | scope body — one font.size.micro consequence line |

The shell decides the border, radius, background, shadow, layer, and entrance. It deliberately carries no padding: a menu list wants full-bleed rows with vertical inset, a dialog-role body wants an even inset, and neither should fight a default. Content padding belongs to the content.

Position is written by the consumer as viewport coordinates into the custom properties --ds-popover-top, --ds-popover-right, --ds-popover-bottom, and --ds-popover-left — set the one or two edges that anchor the surface and leave the rest auto. Anchor by the edge nearest the trigger (left for a start placement, right for end; bottom when flipped above) so the surface's measured size never enters the math on its anchored axis: the glued edge cannot drift by a surface-width when a measurement is momentarily stale. The consumer also mirrors the trigger's width into --ds-popover-trigger-width so width-coupled surfaces (a select's listbox) can set min-width: var(--ds-popover-trigger-width) without an inline width clobbering their own floor.

The scope body — a named content part

Content is host-owned everywhere else in this family. This one shape is named because it must be identical in three places: the Remote settings machine row (opened from a quiet link-button reading "6 scopes"), the inbound pair-request card, and the mobile companion. A surface whose job is to say what another machine may do on this one is the last one that should be drawn three times in three orders.

It hosts on the dialog role — it holds a heading, a rule and an action, none of which belong in a menu — and it brings its own inset, which is the Anatomy note's rule rather than an exception to it: the shell carries no padding, so content padding belongs to the content.

The order is the argument, and it is fixed:

`` <div class="ds-popover" role="dialog" aria-labelledby="…"> <div class="ds-popover-scope-body"> <div class="ds-popover-scope-heading" id="…">Granted scopes</div> ← what is held <ul class="ds-popover-scope-list">…</ul> ← mono, one per line <div class="ds-popover-scope-rule"></div> ← the hairline <div class="ds-popover-scope-headline"> ← what is not held… <span class="ds-popover-scope-heading">Not granted</span> …a link-button reading "Grant"… ← …and the one act that changes it </div> <ul class="ds-popover-scope-list ds-popover-scope-list--missing">…</ul> <div class="ds-popover-scope-note">It can't see chats here.</div> </div> </div> ``

  • Held first. The reader opened this to find out what is already true; a surface that led with what is missing would read as a prompt to grant rather than as an answer.
  • The action is inline with its heading, not under the list. "Grant" acts on the whole ungranted group, and parked at the bottom it reads as belonging to the last row. It is a [link button](../link-button/component.md) — one quiet verb inside a surface that is already an aside — never a filled button: this popover is not a view and has no primary action budget.
  • The consequence line is the reason the surface exists. "It can't see chats here" is what the reader actually came to find out; a bare pair of lists leaves them to derive it from two identifiers they may not know. One line, micro, text.muted, and only when something is actually missing — a note that is always there is decoration.
  • Never a danger tint on the missing list. One ink step, reinforced by a heading that says the same thing in words. A scope the person never granted is a fact, not a fault.
  • A second group is read-only. Where the same machine also has an outbound half with a different set, it goes under its own heading ("What you can do there") with no action beside it: this surface acts only on the grant *this* machine controls.
  • Identifiers stay a column here, not pills. The wide surface — the pairing code card — sets the same content as [scope pills](../scope-pill/component.md); a popover column is too narrow for a wrapped pill set to read as anything but ragged.

Variants

  • Placement — bottom-start (default), bottom-end, top-start, top-end. A placement is a preference, not a promise: the surface flips to the other vertical side when its preferred side has no room, and clamps 8px inside the viewport on both axes. The clamp bounds height as well as position: a surface taller than the viewport is capped to it and scrolls its content, so the last rows of a long menu are never off-screen. The gap between trigger and surface is 4px.
  • .ds-popover--pointer — coordinate-anchored instead of trigger-anchored: opens at a viewport point (a right-click, a text caret, a drop location) and clamps inside the viewport. It sits at z.menu, one layer above the trigger-anchored surface, because a context menu is summoned *over* whatever is already open — including an open popover. Same shell, same chrome; only the anchor and the layer differ. In the shipped kit this is PointerPopover (rich coordinate-anchored content) and the surface ContextMenu shares.
  • Material — raised (default) or glass. Raised is the ordinary surface. Glass is bg.surface-raised at glass.opacity over a backdrop-filter of glass.blur and glass.saturation, and it is opt-in per surface, never the family default: it exists for a card drawn deliberately over live app content that the reader should still see (the conversation peek over a running terminal; the composer's skill type-ahead over the transcript being read). Elevation and radius do not change with it — the popover family keeps shadow.popover and radius.overlay in both materials. Both shells carry it: the trigger-anchored surface (Popover, since 2026-09-08) and the pointer-anchored one (PointerPopover). See the toast spec for the blur ruling this opts into; nothing outside the kit may borrow the utility.
  • .ds-popover--cursor-error — the pointer-anchored surface carrying the *report* of a failed click rather than a menu: a missing file link, a rejected drop. It is the pointer-scoped member of the status.danger family (banner, inline-notice, toast) — the soft tone tint, one hairline, the shape-coded failed lifecycle glyph, never a saturated fill. Three things separate it from every other member of the family: it opens at the click that failed rather than at a trigger or a corner; it opens collapsed to one clipped line and expands to the full message on a click; and it auto-dismisses on a timer that pauses on hover, on focus, and for as long as it stays expanded — so the surface can never vanish out from under someone reading it. It announces itself as role="alert" / aria-live="assertive", which is what earns it the right to interrupt at all: it is reporting a failure, and the failure has no other home. In the shipped kit this is CursorErrorPopover (src/renderer/src/components/ui/CursorErrorPopover.tsx).

Its parts, all optional to the rest of the family: .ds-popover-cursor-error-body (the collapsed/expanded height clamp), .ds-popover-cursor-error-row (glyph, message, actions on one line), .ds-popover-cursor-error-message, .ds-popover-caret and .ds-popover-caret-seam (the --up / --down pair, aimed by --ds-popover-caret-left). The copy and dismiss affordances are the kit's icon buttons at the xs control step — the copy one is revealed on hover and on keyboard focus, never hover-only.

There is no arrow variant — with one ruled exception, below. A caret pointing at the trigger is decoration the 4px gap already does the work of, and it forces the surface to track the trigger horizontally instead of clamping freely.

The exception is the cursor-error surface, and it is about anchoring, not decoration. A trigger-anchored popover is *beside a thing the person can see*; a cursor-anchored error box has no visible anchor at all, because the click that raised it left nothing on screen. The caret is what ties the report back to the pixel that failed — it aims at the click even when the box is clamped sideways against the viewport, and the entrance scales from it so the surface visibly emanates from the click. Nothing else in the family may grow one: a caret on a surface whose anchor is already visible is the decoration this rule was written against.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Closed | Not in the document (or hidden) — out of view and out of the accessibility tree | | Open | Entrance: a 4px drop-and-fade at motion.duration.normal / motion.ease.standard — the one sanctioned popover entrance; removed under reduced motion | | Open, trigger scrolled | The surface repositions to track its trigger (scroll in the capture phase, and resize) — unlike a tooltip, which dismisses, because a popover holds state a scroll must not throw away | | Stacked | A popover opened from inside another stacks above it; each keeps its own surface |

Until the first measurement lands, the surface is kept invisible so the first paint never flashes at 0,0.

Usage

A trigger-anchored surface is anchored by the consumer's own control, not by this component: the shell is portaled to <body> and positioned from the coordinates the consumer writes into --ds-popover-*. So a caller "anchors" a popover by rendering its own trigger — a link button, a chip, a row's meta-line verb — carrying aria-haspopup, a live aria-expanded and, while open, the surface's aria-controls, and by handing the shell that trigger's rect. The shell's content is arbitrary: any children at all, at whatever role the consumer declares. Nothing about the scope body above needs a new shell.

Light dismiss, exactly three ways. Escape, a pointer-down outside, or the consumer closing it (picking an item, toggling the trigger). No scrim: the page stays visible and clickable-through-to — the outside click that dismisses also lands where it fell.

Escape closes the topmost surface only. Open popovers form a stack; an Escape consumed by the top one never reaches the one below, and never reaches a dialog hosting them. One press, one layer.

A pointer landing in a surface stacked above counts as inside. Every surface is portaled to <body>, so a popover opened from inside another is not a DOM descendant of it — a naive contains() check reads a click on the nested surface as an outside click and unmounts it before its own click lands, silently dropping the choice the user just made. This clause exists because that was a real defect.

The rule is the SHELL's, not the trigger-anchored variant's: it holds for the coordinate-anchored surface too (.ds-popover--pointer), which is the one that hosts rich content and therefore the one most likely to have a menu opened from inside it. A split button on a hover card's head line is exactly that shape — the card dismissed itself on the press that chose a menu row, and the row's click never landed. The stack is the source of truth for "what is open right now", so a press inside any member of it is never outside any other.

A surface opened from inside a menu-tier surface takes the menu tier. The layer is a property of what a surface was summoned *over*, not of how it was anchored: a trigger-anchored menu opened from a coordinate-anchored card sits at z.menu like the card, and at the default z.popover it would paint underneath the thing it was opened from. One z per surface, chosen by the shell from a named layer — a caller appending a second z utility leaves which one wins to stylesheet order.

The popup role is a contract, not a default. role="menu" for action lists, role="listbox" for selection, role="dialog" for rich content (a search field, a form). The trigger's aria-haspopup mirrors whichever the surface declares, so a screen reader hears what kind of surface Enter will open. Content then owes that role its keyboard behavior — a menu roves focus with arrows; the shell does not do this for you.

Do not rebuild the shell per host. Escape stacking, outside-press logic, focus restoration, and clip-escape are solved here once. A surface that owns its own copy of any of them will drift — the shipped codebase has bespoke popover chrome in notification and workspace surfaces, and every one answers these questions slightly differently.

Rebuilding it in a framework: what must survive the rewrite is the portal to <body>, the edge-nearest-trigger anchoring, the topmost-only Escape, the stacked-above outside-press guard, and focus returning to the trigger on close.

Accessibility

  • The surface carries its role and a required aria-label — a portaled surface has no surrounding context to borrow a name from.
  • The trigger carries aria-haspopup matching the popup role, aria-expanded for the open state, and aria-controls pointing at the surface's id only while it is open — a reference to a node that is not in the document is noise.
  • Closing returns focus to the trigger, so Escape never strands keyboard focus on <body>. Closing because the user clicked elsewhere skips the restore — focus follows the click.
  • Escape is handled on the document, before window-level listeners, so a hosting dialog keying its own Escape off defaultPrevented sees the popover consume it first regardless of mount order.
  • The entrance animation is removed under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

Known drift

CursorErrorPopover does not compose this shell (recorded 2026-09-08 with the entry above). It portals itself, measures and clamps itself, and keys its own Escape and outside-press — the four things the Usage section says are solved here once. Two consequences are already visible in the source:

  • Its Escape listener is registered on window in the capture phase and calls stopPropagation(), which is the opposite of the topmost-only rule. A surface opened over it does not get first refusal on the key; the error box takes it from underneath.
  • Its geometry constants — the cursor gap, the viewport inset, the collapsed and expanded height caps, the caret's corner margin — are private numbers rather than the shell's clamp. Two surfaces in the same family will drift apart on the first window that is short.
  • Its fill is mixed at runtime — color-mix(in oklab, bg.surface-raised 88%, tone.error) — where status.danger-soft is the token that already means "the soft tone tint for a danger surface". The CSS here spends the token; the mix is a fourth spelling of a value the ramp holds.
  • Its entrance and its expand both name their own curve and duration (140ms and 200ms on a literal cubic-bezier), where the motion ramp has one easing and three durations. motion.duration.normal + motion.ease.standard is the pair, and it is what this CSS composes.

Folding it into the shell means teaching the shell the caret and the collapsed/expanded height pair, which is the work this entry now names. What is not drift is the caret itself or the status.danger tone: both are ruled above.

The two entries that stood here before were spent by the overlay-geometry sweep and verified gone on 2026-09-02:

  • ~~Six shipped files hardcode the dark-only shadow 0 8px 24px -12px rgba(0,0,0,0.6), so light-mode overlays cast a dark-tuned shadow and --sem-shadow-popover goes unconsumed.~~ Resolved — the literal appears nowhere in the renderer, and the no overlay spells its own shadow seam holds it there.
  • ~~Popover.tsx writes rounded-[7px], which matches radius.overlay but bypasses the variable.~~ Resolved — it draws the radius through the variable.

Recording this rather than deleting the section: a spec that lists drift which was fixed two sweeps ago teaches a reader to expect a defect that is not there, and to distrust the rest of the entry. The drift log is a list to drain.

components/popover/component.css
/* Popover — the anchored overlay engine. One shell for everything
 * dropdown-shaped: overflow menus, filter menus, select listboxes, pickers.
 * Extracted from the source product's Popover / PointerPopover primitives
 * (src/renderer/src/components/ui/).
 *
 * The surface is lifted to the end of <body> and positioned in fixed viewport
 * coordinates, so it escapes every scroll container and stacking context on
 * the page. The consumer writes the one or two anchoring edges into
 * --ds-popover-top/right/bottom/left (the edge nearest the trigger, so a stale
 * measurement can never drift the glued edge) and mirrors the trigger's width
 * into --ds-popover-trigger-width for width-coupled listboxes.
 *
 * The shell owns chrome only — border, radius, background, shadow, layer,
 * entrance — and deliberately no padding: a menu wants full-bleed rows, a
 * dialog-role body wants an even inset, and neither should fight a default. */

.ds-popover {
  position: fixed;
  top: var(--ds-popover-top, auto);
  right: var(--ds-popover-right, auto);
  bottom: var(--ds-popover-bottom, auto);
  left: var(--ds-popover-left, auto);
  z-index: var(--sem-z-popover);
  box-sizing: border-box;
  /* The vertical half of the 8px viewport clamp: a surface taller than the
   * window is bounded to it and scrolls, never pinned to the top edge and
   * run off the bottom. */
  max-height: calc(100vh - 2 * var(--sem-space-sm));
  overflow-y: auto;
  border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-strong);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-overlay);
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface-raised);
  /* The token, not the shipped literal — six kit files hardcode a dark-only
   * shadow here; the token is the spec. */
  box-shadow: var(--sem-shadow-popover);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-default);
  /* The one sanctioned popover entrance: a 4px drop-and-fade composing the
   * token duration/ease pair. Not a fourth motion — this is the third of the
   * three the principles allow. */
  animation: ds-popover-enter var(--sem-motion-duration-normal) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

/* Closed is out of the document — or `hidden`, which must win over the
 * fixed-position display. */
.ds-popover[hidden] {
  display: none;
}

/* Coordinate-anchored: opens at a viewport point (right-click, caret, drop
 * location) instead of at a trigger. One layer up — a context menu is
 * summoned OVER whatever is already open, including an open popover. */
.ds-popover--pointer {
  z-index: var(--sem-z-menu);
}

/* Cursor-error: the pointer-anchored REPORT of a failed click. Same family,
 * different job — it carries a status.danger message rather than a menu, so it
 * takes the soft tone tint and the tone hairline in place of the raised
 * surface and the neutral edge. Everything else (portal, fixed coordinates,
 * viewport clamp, elevation, radius) is the shell's, unchanged.
 *
 * The one exception to "there is no arrow variant": the click that raised this
 * left nothing on screen to anchor to, so the caret is the anchor. */
.ds-popover--cursor-error {
  z-index: var(--sem-z-popover);
  /* The caret hangs past the surface edge, so this level cannot clip. */
  overflow: visible;
  border-color: var(--sem-color-status-danger);
  background: var(--sem-color-status-danger-soft);
  /* The entrance scales from the caret so the box visibly emanates from the
   * click; the pair is the sanctioned popover motion, not a fourth one. */
  transform-origin: var(--ds-popover-caret-left, 50%) var(--ds-popover-caret-origin, 100%);
  animation: ds-popover-cursor-error-enter var(--sem-motion-duration-normal)
    var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

/* Collapsed shows one clipped line; expanded grows to the message and scrolls.
 * The heights are layout measures — the reading limits of a transient report,
 * not steps on the control ramp. */
.ds-popover-cursor-error-body {
  max-height: 36px;
  overflow: hidden;
  transition: max-height var(--sem-motion-duration-normal) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

.ds-popover--cursor-error[data-expanded] .ds-popover-cursor-error-body {
  max-height: 360px;
  overflow-y: auto;
}

/* The message row: the shape-coded failed glyph at the leading edge, the text,
 * and the reveal actions. Tone by glyph plus tint, never by a coloured edge. */
.ds-popover-cursor-error-row {
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-start;
  gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
  padding: var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-md);
}

.ds-popover-cursor-error-message {
  min-width: 0;
  flex: 1;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-default);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

/* Expanded, the message is the full text of an error — an identifier, not
 * prose, so it reads in mono and keeps its own line breaks. */
.ds-popover--cursor-error[data-expanded] .ds-popover-cursor-error-message {
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  white-space: pre-wrap;
  overflow-wrap: break-word;
  overflow: visible;
  text-overflow: clip;
}

/* A 1px-calibrated triangle from a rotated square, so the fill and both outer
 * hairlines continue cleanly off the box edge. It is aimed at the click even
 * when the box is clamped sideways. */
.ds-popover-caret {
  position: absolute;
  left: var(--ds-popover-caret-left, 50%);
  width: 9px;
  height: 9px;
  pointer-events: none;
}

.ds-popover-caret::before {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-status-danger);
  background: var(--sem-color-status-danger-soft);
  transform: rotate(45deg);
}

/* Box above the click: the caret hangs below it, pointing down. */
.ds-popover-caret--down {
  bottom: -5px;
}

.ds-popover-caret--down::before {
  clip-path: polygon(100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%);
}

/* Box below the click: the caret sits above it, pointing up. */
.ds-popover-caret--up {
  top: -5px;
}

.ds-popover-caret--up::before {
  clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 0 100%);
}

/* Masks the 1px join where the rotated square meets the surface border. */
.ds-popover-caret-seam {
  position: absolute;
  left: var(--ds-popover-caret-left, 50%);
  width: 11px;
  height: 1px;
  background: var(--sem-color-status-danger-soft);
  pointer-events: none;
}

.ds-popover-caret-seam--down {
  bottom: 0;
}

.ds-popover-caret-seam--up {
  top: 0;
}

@keyframes ds-popover-cursor-error-enter {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: scale(0.96);
  }
  to {
    opacity: 1;
    transform: scale(1);
  }
}

@keyframes ds-popover-enter {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: translateY(-4px);
  }
  to {
    opacity: 1;
    transform: none;
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .ds-popover {
    animation: none;
  }
  .ds-popover-cursor-error-body {
    transition: none;
  }
}

/* ── Scope body ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * A named CONTENT part for the dialog-role surface: the answer to "what may
 * that machine do here?", opened from a quiet link-button on a row's meta line
 * ("6 scopes").
 *
 * It is documented as a part rather than left to each host because the shape
 * has to be identical in three places — the Remote settings row, the inbound
 * pair-request card, and the mobile companion — and a surface that says what
 * another machine is permitted to do is the last one that should be drawn
 * three times with three different orders. The shell still owns the chrome and
 * still carries no padding of its own; this part brings the inset with it,
 * which is the rule the Anatomy note states ("content padding belongs to the
 * content").
 *
 * The order is the argument: what is held, a rule, what is not held with the
 * one action that changes it, and a consequence in plain words. Held first,
 * because the reader came to find out what is already true. */
.ds-popover-scope-body {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
  padding: var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-lg);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
}

/* The heading over a list. `meta` at `font.weight.emphasis` — a step BELOW the
 * body text it introduces, which is what a label over a list is: the surface's
 * subject is the identifiers, not the words above them. */
.ds-popover-scope-heading {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

/* The second heading rides a line with its own action — "Not granted" beside
 * the link-button that grants. The action is inline with the heading rather
 * than under the list because it acts on the whole group; parked at the bottom
 * it would read as belonging to the last row. */
.ds-popover-scope-headline {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
}

/* The second group's heading is one step quieter than the first: the reader
 * came for what is held, and the ink order says so. */
.ds-popover-scope-headline .ds-popover-scope-heading {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
}

/* The identifiers, one per line, in mono at `meta`. A list rather than a set of
 * pills because a popover column is narrow and a wrapped pill set at this width
 * reads as ragged; the scope-pill component is for the wide surface (the
 * pairing code card), and this is the same content in a column. */
.ds-popover-scope-list {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--sem-space-3xs);
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
}

/* Not granted: one step of ink, and nothing else. Never a danger tint — a
 * scope the person never granted is a fact, not a fault — and never the only
 * carrier of the difference, which the heading above it states in words. */
.ds-popover-scope-list--missing {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
}

/* The hairline between the two groups. One rule, and it is what separates them:
 * a second heading alone would let the eye run the two lists together. */
.ds-popover-scope-rule {
  height: 1px;
  background: var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
}

/* The consequence, in the reader's own language — "It can't see chats or
 * terminals here." One line, `micro`, `text.muted`: it is the sentence that
 * explains why something they expected to see is missing, and it is the reason
 * this surface exists rather than a bare list. */
.ds-popover-scope-note {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
}
components/popover/component.html (demo)
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8" />
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
<title>Popover</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../../foundations/tokens.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../link-button/component.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="component.css" />
<style>
  body {
    margin: 0;
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  }
  .demo-stage {
    padding: var(--sem-space-3xl);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-app);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  }
  .demo-label {
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  }
  .demo-row {
    display: flex;
    align-items: flex-start;
    gap: var(--sem-space-lg);
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    margin-bottom: var(--sem-space-lg);
  }
  .demo-trigger {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
    height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
    padding: 0 var(--sem-space-lg);
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-default);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  .demo-trigger:hover {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  }
  .demo-trigger:focus-visible {
    outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
    outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
  }
  /* The pointer variant needs a place to right-click. A quiet canvas, nothing
     more — the surface it summons is the thing on display. */
  .demo-canvas {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    height: 120px;
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  }
  /* Menu content for the demo surfaces. Full-bleed rows with a vertical inset
     on the surface's content — the shell itself carries no padding. */
  .demo-menu {
    min-width: 180px;
    padding: var(--sem-space-2xs) 0;
  }
  .demo-item {
    display: flex;
    width: 100%;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: space-between;
    gap: var(--sem-space-lg);
    box-sizing: border-box;
    padding: var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-md);
    border: 0;
    background: transparent;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
    text-align: left;
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  .demo-item:hover,
  .demo-item:focus-visible {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    outline: none;
  }
  .demo-item kbd {
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-wide);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  }
  .demo-specimen {
    margin-bottom: var(--sem-space-lg);
  }
  /* Surfaces are authored parked so the anatomy is visible with scripts off —
     the catalog embeds this demo without JavaScript. The script lifts each
     exact node to the document body on load; nothing is cloned. */
  .ds-popover.demo-parked {
    position: static;
    animation: none;
  }
  /* The cursor-error specimens stay on the page rather than being lifted to
     the body: their anchor is a click that has already happened, so there is
     nothing to summon them from. Parked, and marked so the script skips them. */
  .demo-error-specimen {
    position: relative;
    max-width: 340px;
    margin-bottom: var(--sem-space-lg);
  }
  .demo-error-specimen .ds-popover {
    position: relative;
    inset: auto;
    animation: none;
  }
  /* The scope-body specimen is parked for the same reason the error one is:
     the catalog embeds this demo with scripts off, and the anatomy has to be
     readable there. Marked static so the lifting script skips it. */
  .demo-scope-specimen {
    position: relative;
    max-width: 280px;
    margin-bottom: var(--sem-space-lg);
  }
  .demo-scope-specimen .ds-popover {
    position: relative;
    inset: auto;
    animation: none;
  }
  .demo-error-actions {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-3xs);
    flex: none;
  }
  .demo-error-button {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    width: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
    height: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
    min-width: var(--sem-size-hit-target-min);
    min-height: var(--sem-size-hit-target-min);
    padding: 0;
    border: 0;
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: transparent;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  .demo-error-button:hover {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  }
  .demo-error-button:focus-visible {
    outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
    outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
  }
  .demo-error-button svg {
    width: var(--sem-icon-size-xs);
    height: var(--sem-icon-size-xs);
  }
  .demo-error-glyph {
    flex: none;
    width: var(--sem-icon-size-sm);
    height: var(--sem-icon-size-sm);
    color: var(--sem-color-status-danger);
  }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="demo-stage" data-mode="light">
  <p class="demo-label">Light — click the trigger for the anchored surface; right-click the canvas for the pointer variant. Escape closes the topmost surface only; scrolling repositions, it does not dismiss.</p>

  <div class="demo-specimen">
    <div class="ds-popover demo-parked" id="pop-light-menu" role="menu" aria-label="Skill actions">
      <div class="demo-menu">
        <button type="button" class="demo-item" role="menuitem">Open in editor</button>
        <button type="button" class="demo-item" role="menuitem">Reveal in folder</button>
        <button type="button" class="demo-item" role="menuitem">Sync source <kbd>⌘R</kbd></button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="demo-row">
    <button type="button" class="demo-trigger" data-popover-trigger="pop-light-menu" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">Skill actions</button>
  </div>


  <p class="demo-label">The cursor-error variant — the one surface in the family with a caret, because the click that raised it left nothing on screen to anchor to. Collapsed to one line, and expanded to the full message with copy.</p>
  <div class="demo-error-specimen">
    <div class="ds-popover ds-popover--cursor-error" data-demo-static role="alert" aria-live="assertive" style="--ds-popover-caret-left: 40px;">
      <span class="ds-popover-caret ds-popover-caret--down" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="ds-popover-caret-seam ds-popover-caret-seam--down" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <div class="ds-popover-cursor-error-body">
        <div class="ds-popover-cursor-error-row">
          <svg class="demo-error-glyph" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4"/><path d="M5.9 5.9l4.2 4.2M10.1 5.9l-4.2 4.2" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>
          <span class="ds-popover-cursor-error-message">Cannot open src/renderer/src/utils/openFileSurface.ts — the file is gone from this branch.</span>
          <span class="demo-error-actions"><button type="button" class="demo-error-button" aria-label="Copy error"><svg viewBox="0 0 14 14" fill="none" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="4.6" y="4.6" width="7" height="7" rx="1.4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3"/><path d="M9.4 2.4H3.8a1.4 1.4 0 0 0-1.4 1.4v5.6" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg></button></span>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="demo-error-specimen">
    <div class="ds-popover ds-popover--cursor-error" data-demo-static data-expanded role="alert" aria-live="assertive" style="--ds-popover-caret-left: 40px; --ds-popover-caret-origin: 0%;">
      <span class="ds-popover-caret ds-popover-caret--up" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="ds-popover-caret-seam ds-popover-caret-seam--up" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <div class="ds-popover-cursor-error-body">
        <div class="ds-popover-cursor-error-row">
          <svg class="demo-error-glyph" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4"/><path d="M5.9 5.9l4.2 4.2M10.1 5.9l-4.2 4.2" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>
          <span class="ds-popover-cursor-error-message">Cannot open src/renderer/src/utils/openFileSurface.ts
ENOENT: no such file or directory</span>
          <span class="demo-error-actions"><button type="button" class="demo-error-button" aria-label="Copy error"><svg viewBox="0 0 14 14" fill="none" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="4.6" y="4.6" width="7" height="7" rx="1.4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3"/><path d="M9.4 2.4H3.8a1.4 1.4 0 0 0-1.4 1.4v5.6" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg></button><button type="button" class="demo-error-button" aria-label="Dismiss"><svg viewBox="0 0 14 14" fill="none" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M3.25 3.25L10.75 10.75M10.75 3.25L3.25 10.75" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg></button></span>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="demo-label">The scope body — a named content part on the <code>dialog</code> role: what is held, a hairline, what is not held with the one action that changes it, and the consequence in plain words.</p>
  <div class="demo-scope-specimen">
    <div class="ds-popover" data-demo-static role="dialog" aria-labelledby="l-scope-h">
      <div class="ds-popover-scope-body">
        <div class="ds-popover-scope-heading" id="l-scope-h">Granted scopes</div>
        <ul class="ds-popover-scope-list">
          <li>workspace:read</li>
          <li>workspace:operate</li>
          <li>backlog:read</li>
          <li>backlog:operate</li>
        </ul>
        <div class="ds-popover-scope-rule"></div>
        <div class="ds-popover-scope-headline">
          <span class="ds-popover-scope-heading">Not granted</span>
          <button type="button" class="ds-link-button">Grant</button>
        </div>
        <ul class="ds-popover-scope-list ds-popover-scope-list--missing">
          <li>conversation:read</li>
          <li>conversation:operate</li>
        </ul>
        <div class="ds-popover-scope-note">It can't see chats here.</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="demo-canvas" data-context-for="pop-light-context">Right-click for the pointer variant</div>
  <div class="ds-popover ds-popover--pointer" id="pop-light-context" role="menu" aria-label="Canvas actions" hidden>
    <div class="demo-menu">
      <button type="button" class="demo-item" role="menuitem">New skill here</button>
      <button type="button" class="demo-item" role="menuitem">Paste</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="demo-stage" data-mode="dark">
  <p class="demo-label">Dark — the same shell, lit by the container it serves. The pointer variant is parked below to show it sits one layer above the anchored surface.</p>

  <div class="demo-specimen">
    <div class="ds-popover ds-popover--pointer demo-parked" id="pop-dark-context" role="menu" aria-label="Canvas actions">

  <div class="demo-row">
    <button type="button" class="demo-trigger" data-popover-trigger="pop-dark-menu" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">Skill actions</button>
  </div>
  <div class="ds-popover" id="pop-dark-menu" role="menu" aria-label="Skill actions" hidden>
    <div class="demo-menu">
      <button type="button" class="demo-item" role="menuitem">Open in editor</button>
      <button type="button" class="demo-item" role="menuitem">Reveal in folder</button>
      <button type="button" class="demo-item" role="menuitem">Sync source <kbd>⌘R</kbd></button>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="demo-canvas" data-context-for="pop-dark-context">Right-click for the pointer variant</div>
  <p class="demo-label">The cursor-error variant in dark — the soft tone tint and one tone hairline, tone carried by the glyph so it survives greyscale.</p>
  <div class="demo-error-specimen">
    <div class="ds-popover ds-popover--cursor-error" data-demo-static role="alert" aria-live="assertive" style="--ds-popover-caret-left: 40px;">
      <span class="ds-popover-caret ds-popover-caret--down" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="ds-popover-caret-seam ds-popover-caret-seam--down" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <div class="ds-popover-cursor-error-body">
        <div class="ds-popover-cursor-error-row">
          <svg class="demo-error-glyph" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4"/><path d="M5.9 5.9l4.2 4.2M10.1 5.9l-4.2 4.2" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>
          <span class="ds-popover-cursor-error-message">Nothing here accepts a dropped worktree.</span>
          <span class="demo-error-actions"><button type="button" class="demo-error-button" aria-label="Copy error"><svg viewBox="0 0 14 14" fill="none" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="4.6" y="4.6" width="7" height="7" rx="1.4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3"/><path d="M9.4 2.4H3.8a1.4 1.4 0 0 0-1.4 1.4v5.6" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg></button></span>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <p class="demo-label">The scope body — a named content part on the <code>dialog</code> role: what is held, a hairline, what is not held with the one action that changes it, and the consequence in plain words.</p>
  <div class="demo-scope-specimen">
    <div class="ds-popover" data-demo-static role="dialog" aria-labelledby="d-scope-h">
      <div class="ds-popover-scope-body">
        <div class="ds-popover-scope-heading" id="d-scope-h">Granted scopes</div>
        <ul class="ds-popover-scope-list">
          <li>workspace:read</li>
          <li>workspace:operate</li>
          <li>backlog:read</li>
          <li>backlog:operate</li>
        </ul>
        <div class="ds-popover-scope-rule"></div>
        <div class="ds-popover-scope-headline">
          <span class="ds-popover-scope-heading">Not granted</span>
          <button type="button" class="ds-link-button">Grant</button>
        </div>
        <ul class="ds-popover-scope-list ds-popover-scope-list--missing">
          <li>conversation:read</li>
          <li>conversation:operate</li>
        </ul>
        <div class="ds-popover-scope-note">It can't see chats here.</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
/* Reference behaviour for the contract in component.md. Rebuild it
   idiomatically in your framework — what must survive the rewrite is the
   portal to <body>, the edge-nearest-trigger anchoring, topmost-only Escape,
   the stacked-above outside-press guard, and focus returning to the trigger
   on close. */

const GAP = 4
const EDGE = 8

/* Lift every surface to the body — moved, never cloned — so each escapes its
   stage's stacking context, exactly as the component contract requires. */
for (const surface of document.querySelectorAll('.ds-popover:not([data-demo-static])')) {
  surface.classList.remove('demo-parked')
  surface.hidden = true
  document.body.appendChild(surface)
}
for (const specimen of document.querySelectorAll('.demo-specimen')) specimen.remove()

/* Open surfaces in stacking order: Escape pops the top; a pointer landing in
   a surface stacked above another counts as inside it. */
const stack = []

function mirrorMode(surface, scopeNode) {
  const scope = scopeNode.closest('[data-mode]')
  if (scope) surface.setAttribute('data-mode', scope.dataset.mode)
  else surface.removeAttribute('data-mode')
}

function close(surface, restoreFocus) {
  const index = stack.findIndex((entry) => entry.surface === surface)
  if (index < 0) return
  const [entry] = stack.splice(index, 1)
  surface.hidden = true
  for (const edge of ['top', 'right', 'bottom', 'left']) {
    surface.style.removeProperty('--ds-popover-' + edge)
  }
  if (entry.trigger) {
    entry.trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false')
    entry.trigger.removeAttribute('aria-controls')
    if (restoreFocus) entry.trigger.focus()
  }
}

function closeAll() {
  for (const entry of [...stack]) close(entry.surface, false)
}

/* Anchored: bottom-start preferred, anchored by the edge nearest the trigger.
   Flip above when there is no room below and more above; clamp inside the
   viewport on the cross axis. */
function placeAnchored(trigger, surface) {
  const anchor = trigger.getBoundingClientRect()
  const rect = surface.getBoundingClientRect()
  const spaceBelow = window.innerHeight - anchor.bottom - EDGE
  const spaceAbove = anchor.top - EDGE
  const flip = rect.height + GAP > spaceBelow && spaceAbove > spaceBelow
  surface.style.removeProperty('--ds-popover-top')
  surface.style.removeProperty('--ds-popover-bottom')
  if (flip) {
    surface.style.setProperty('--ds-popover-bottom', Math.round(window.innerHeight - anchor.top + GAP) + 'px')
  } else {
    surface.style.setProperty('--ds-popover-top', Math.round(anchor.bottom + GAP) + 'px')
  }
  const left = Math.max(EDGE, Math.min(anchor.left, window.innerWidth - rect.width - EDGE))
  surface.style.setProperty('--ds-popover-left', Math.round(left) + 'px')
  surface.style.setProperty('--ds-popover-trigger-width', Math.round(anchor.width) + 'px')
}

function openAnchored(trigger, surface) {
  mirrorMode(surface, trigger)
  surface.hidden = false
  placeAnchored(trigger, surface)
  trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')
  trigger.setAttribute('aria-controls', surface.id)
  stack.push({ surface, trigger, anchor: trigger })
  surface.querySelector('[role="menuitem"]')?.focus()
}

function openAtPoint(surface, x, y, scopeNode) {
  mirrorMode(surface, scopeNode)
  surface.hidden = false
  const rect = surface.getBoundingClientRect()
  const left = Math.max(EDGE, Math.min(x, window.innerWidth - rect.width - EDGE))
  const top = Math.max(EDGE, Math.min(y, window.innerHeight - rect.height - EDGE))
  surface.style.setProperty('--ds-popover-left', Math.round(left) + 'px')
  surface.style.setProperty('--ds-popover-top', Math.round(top) + 'px')
  stack.push({ surface, trigger: null, anchor: null })
  surface.querySelector('[role="menuitem"]')?.focus()
}

for (const trigger of document.querySelectorAll('[data-popover-trigger]')) {
  const surface = document.getElementById(trigger.dataset.popoverTrigger)
  trigger.addEventListener('click', () => {
    if (!surface.hidden) close(surface, true)
    else openAnchored(trigger, surface)
  })
}

for (const area of document.querySelectorAll('[data-context-for]')) {
  const surface = document.getElementById(area.dataset.contextFor)
  area.addEventListener('contextmenu', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault()
    closeAll()
    openAtPoint(surface, event.clientX, event.clientY, area)
  })
}

/* Escape closes the topmost surface only, restoring focus to its trigger. */
document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  if (event.key !== 'Escape' || stack.length === 0) return
  event.preventDefault()
  close(stack[stack.length - 1].surface, true)
})

/* Outside pointer-down closes — but a press landing in any surface stacked
   above counts as inside, so a nested surface's own click is never dropped. */
document.addEventListener('pointerdown', (event) => {
  for (let i = stack.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
    const { surface, trigger } = stack[i]
    if (surface.contains(event.target)) return
    if (trigger && trigger.contains(event.target)) return
    close(surface, false)
  }
})

/* Arrow-key roving inside the demo menus — the content's obligation to its
   declared role, not the shell's. */
document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  if (event.key !== 'ArrowDown' && event.key !== 'ArrowUp') return
  const surface = event.target.closest('.ds-popover')
  if (!surface) return
  const items = [...surface.querySelectorAll('[role="menuitem"]')]
  const index = items.indexOf(document.activeElement)
  if (index < 0) return
  event.preventDefault()
  const next = event.key === 'ArrowDown' ? (index + 1) % items.length : (index - 1 + items.length) % items.length
  items[next].focus()
})

/* Activating a menu item closes its surface and hands focus back. */
document.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
  const item = event.target.closest('[role="menuitem"]')
  const surface = item?.closest('.ds-popover')
  if (surface) close(surface, true)
})

/* Scroll and resize REPOSITION an anchored surface — unlike a tooltip, a
   popover holds state a scroll must not throw away. Capture phase, so nested
   containers reposition too. */
function repositionAll() {
  for (const entry of stack) {
    if (entry.anchor) placeAnchored(entry.anchor, entry.surface)
  }
}
window.addEventListener('scroll', repositionAll, true)
window.addEventListener('resize', repositionAll)
</script>
</body>
</html>

Provider row

Light — installed providers, one expanded, one with an update waiting, one absent and receded

Checked 2m ago
CL Claude Code 2.1.220 Ready — /Users/you/.local/bin/claude
GK Grok Build grok 0.2.114 (0c785038798) [stable] Unavailable — startup timed out after 15s
