One row for a *provider*: something the product talks to that can be present-or-absent, healthy-or-not, and configured per-instance. An agent CLI, a source-control forge, an MCP server, a capability module. Extracted from the source product's Agent CLIs lists.

It is not the general list row. Reach for list-row when the thing in the row is content the user made; reach for this when the row reports on something outside the product that the product depends on.

Two facts drive the whole anatomy, and they are separate: health (is it reachable) and enablement (do you want it on). A provider can be switched on and unreachable, or off and perfectly installed. Nothing here derives one from the other.

Anatomy

  • ds-provider-row — the group. It owns the row and its expansion, so a disclosure opens inside the row's own box rather than pushing a sibling panel into the list.
  • ds-provider-row__face — the resting row: space.lg of vertical padding, space.md at the sides, and no border. Five bordered bars in a list read as five panels; space and the hover fill do the separating. Where the list itself is a settings group or a catalogue page, the *list* takes one edge — the list card — and the rows inside it are still borderless, divided by the card's hairlines (the --in-card variant below).
  • ds-provider-row__mark — the brand mark's slot at icon.size.lg. The row sizes the slot and never picks the mark: a provider whose identity is a logo and one whose identity is a glyph must read at one weight.
  • ds-provider-row__health — the tone's status mark (status-dot: a shape-coded glyph, never a dot) at 10px, docked on the mark's TOP-LEFT corner on a small disc of the fill behind it, inside a 2px keyline in the same fill. The disc and keyline are structural, not decoration: without them the logo shows through the glyph's ring and the mark reads as a stain on it. Optional since 2026-09-10 — see "One status idiom" under Usage.
  • ds-provider-row__badge — the badge component's corner count, docked on the mark's TOP-RIGHT: how many things on this row are waiting for the person. The opposite corner from the health mark, so a row that somehow draws both reads as two marks rather than one smudge.
  • ds-provider-row__name + ds-provider-row__version — a baseline pair, name at font.size.body / font.weight.emphasis, version mono at font.size.micro. Neither grows, so they stay adjacent on a row with no trailing control.
  • ds-provider-row__state — exactly one line, at font.size.meta. ds-provider-row__id marks identifiers inside it.
  • ds-provider-row__trail — actions, then the disclosure chevron, then the switch. It owns its own clicks: flipping the switch must not also toggle the row.
  • ds-provider-row__detail — the expansion, indented to the name's left edge.
  • The section band above the list is the one chrome row: title left, freshness meta and the controls that act on the whole list right. Not part of this component, but a list of these rows without it has nowhere to put "when was this last checked" and the control that re-checks it.

Variants

  • Default — icon, name, state line. The floor: every provider row has all three.
  • Versioned — adds the mono version. Absent means nothing is rendered there. A row that says "unknown" where a version goes has spent a high-signal slot on the absence of information.
  • Switched (__switch present) — adds enablement. Only for a host with real enablement state to write to.
  • Disclosable (ds-provider-row--disclosable) — adds the chevron and the expansion.
  • Selected (ds-provider-row--selected) — Tier 1 selection for a list that drives a detail pane: a neutral fill, no left bar, no accent.
  • Badged (__badge present) — a count on the mark's corner. Often "1", and that is not a mistake: on a row the counter's job is *this one, here*, and the number is what makes it a pip rather than one more status colour.
  • Recessed (ds-provider-row--recessed) — the provider is not present on this machine. The mark drops to 60% and the name drops from text.primary to text.muted; nothing else changes. text.muted rather than the one step to text.default, which sat too close to the present rows to read as receded (owner ruling 2026-09-24), and rather than text.subtle, which falls under AA on the dark card. A glyph mark drawn in the text ink takes text.muted with it. Not a disabled state — every control keeps working, and the Install button such a row carries is the reason it is listed at all. That button is the --outline secondary, not the primary: an accent fill on every absent row pulls the eye straight back to the rows the list recedes (owner ruling 2026-09-24). The accent stays for the action on a present row (Update).
  • In a card (ds-provider-row--in-card) — the row inside the list card ([setting-row](../setting-row/component.md) → *The list card*, ruled 2026-09-15). The face drops its radius and takes the card's space.xl side inset; the health mark's disc and keyline and the corner count's ring follow the card's raised ground so neither halos. Everything else — the axes, the disclosure, the expansion's alignment to the name — is unchanged.
  • No tone variants of the row itself, deliberately. An unhealthy provider is reported by its health mark and its state line, not by tinting the row. A list where three of nine rows carry a wash has no resting state left.

States

  • Hover: bg.hover on the face, and the health mark's disc and keyline switch to the same fill so they do not halo. Rows separate by this fill — it is load-bearing, not feedback.
  • Selected: bg.selected, keyline follows again.
  • Expanded: the chevron rotates 180°; the face does not change fill. The row keeps its position, and the detail opens under it.
  • Health: good / warn / danger / neutral on the mark — a check disc, a ring with "!", a ring with "×", a ring with a bar — so the tones differ by shape, not only by colour. neutral is the honest tone where a host has no health probe (a marketplace listing) — it is not a fourth severity.
  • Unknown health is a real state and not the same as unhealthy. Where a probe failed rather than reported absence, say so on the state line and do not offer the action that assumes absence.
  • Reduced motion: the chevron's rotation is switched off. The state still reads from the angle, so nothing is lost.
  • No press-scale, no row-level motion. A list of nine rows that each spring on click is nine springs.

Usage

  • The state line is mandatory, and it is state. "Authenticated as <id> · Max subscription", "Not installed — no grok on PATH", "Unavailable — startup timed out after 15s". Never what the provider is or why you might want it — that is a caption, and it belongs to a marketplace detail panel if anywhere.
  • The health mark is never the only carrier of a state. It is aria-hidden and the words are what a screen reader gets, which is also what makes the row survive greyscale and colour-blindness.
  • One status idiom, and the list picks which one. The health mark and the corner count are both optional and a list uses one or the other — never both, and never either alongside a tinted pill saying the same thing.

Which one is decided by what the list is FOR, and the deciding question is what the rows differ by. The health mark earns its place where health genuinely varies down the column. Where it does not — an Agent CLIs list where nine of ten rows probe green — it is a status idiom spent on a fact nobody is scanning for, and it crowds out the mark that does have something to say. The owner arrived at exactly that list from an update notification and could not tell which CLI the notification was about (2026-09-10): ten health marks, all the same green, and the one thing they came for was not among them. The count replaced them. Since 2026-09-25 (owner ruling) Settings ▸ Agents draws that count beside the row's Update button, in the row's actions, rather than on the mark: it is still the row's one status idiom, placed next to the control that clears it (the badge entry, "In Settings").

  • A count says which, not how many. On a rail square it is a quantity; on a row it is a pointer. Give it the row's own name in its accessible label ("Codex — update available: 0.153.4") — a bare "1" docked on a logo is not a sentence.
  • Recede absence, do not grey it out. A provider the machine does not have belongs in the list — that is how it gets installed — but it should not hold the same weight as one that is there. Recede it and leave its controls working. A list that mixes the two puts the present ones first, in their usual order, and the receded ones after them in the same order, so the list reads as what is here and then what could be.
  • Do not render a switch a host cannot honour. A toggle wired to nothing is worse than no toggle: it reports a state the product does not have.
  • Do not render a disclosure over an empty panel. Where a provider has nothing to configure on this surface, the row ends at its state line.
  • Offer an action only when the state earns it. An Install button on a provider whose probe never completed is a fake affordance — that row's next action is to check again.
  • Keep the expansion the per-instance form that already exists. This is disclosure, not navigation: nothing about opening a row changes where the user is.
  • A settings group or a catalogue page of these rows takes the list card (ruled 2026-09-15); a rail, a shelf or an onboarding step does not. The section band sits outside the card with the count and the one control that acts on the whole list; the rows sit inside it in the --in-card form. Rows loose under a band on a settings page were the shape this replaced.

Accessibility

  • The chevron is a real <button> carrying aria-expanded and aria-controls on the panel it opens, plus an aria-label naming its provider ("Claude Code details") — a list of nine identical "details" is nine unusable controls.
  • Exactly one focusable control per disclosure. The face is a mouse target that calls the same handler; it is not a second tab stop and never a role="button" wrapper around a real button.
  • The switch is the switch component's contract: role="switch", aria-checked, Space toggles and Enter does not.
  • The health mark is aria-hidden; the state line is plain text in the reading order right after the name, so the row announces as name, version, state.
  • The corner count is the opposite: always named, never decorative, because nothing else on the row says what it counts. It is the badge component's count species, so it announces as a live region — the number moving while the reader is elsewhere is exactly what that is for.
  • Recessed is a contrast change and nothing else. It sets no aria-disabled, removes nothing from the tab order, and adds no state to the announcement — the state line already carries the fact in words. The receded name's text.muted clears AA on the row's ground and on its hover fill in the system's light and dark modes (at worst 4.7:1, light, hovered) — the same ink the state line has always worn there. It does not clear AA on bg.selected (3.9:1, light), so a row that is both selected and recessed keeps text.primary on its name; the mark still recedes.
  • Focus-visible is a 2px border.focus mark on the chevron and the switch independently — a ring on the chevron, an offset outline on the switch, whose checked fill is border.focus's own colour. The row itself never takes focus, so it never shows either.
  • The chevron pads out to size.hit-target-min around its icon.size.xs glyph. The glyph is what you see; the button is what you hit.
  • The face takes a hover fill only when it is disclosable. A fill on hover is this system's promise that the thing under the cursor is actionable, and a row whose only live control is a trailing button cannot keep it.
  • Contrast: name, state line, and mono identifiers all clear AA in both modes. The health mark is exempt because it is decorative by contract — but its disc and 2px keyline are what keep it perceptible at all against a brand mark, so they are not optional.
components/provider-row/component.css
/* Provider row — extracted from the source product's ProviderRow primitive
 * (src/renderer/src/components/ui/ProviderRow.tsx), the shared anatomy for the
 * agent CLIs list in Settings ▸ Agents and the onboarding essentials step. */

/* The row group holds the row and its expansion, so the disclosure opens INSIDE
 * the row's own box and the list below never shifts anything but its position. */
.ds-provider-row {
  display: block;
}

/* No border, on purpose. Five bordered bars in a list read as five panels; the
 * separating work is done by 12px of vertical padding and the hover fill. The
 * radius exists only so the fill has a shape — it never draws a box at rest. */
.ds-provider-row__face {
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-start;
  gap: var(--sem-space-lg);
  padding: var(--sem-space-lg) var(--sem-space-md);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
  transition: background-color var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

/* Hover fill only where the face is actionable. A fill on hover says "you can
 * act on me"; a row whose only live control is a trailing button must not make
 * that promise, or the whole row reads as a click target that does nothing. */
.ds-provider-row--disclosable > .ds-provider-row__face:hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
}

/* Tier 1 selection: a neutral fill, no left bar and no accent (see
 * patterns/selection.html). For a list whose row drives a detail pane. */
.ds-provider-row--selected > .ds-provider-row__face {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected);
}

/* A row whose disclosure is live takes the whole face as its mouse target. The
 * chevron is still the only focusable control for it. */
.ds-provider-row--disclosable > .ds-provider-row__face {
  cursor: pointer;
}

/* --in-card: the row inside a list card (setting-row's `.ds-setting-row-list`,
 * ruled 2026-09-15). The card clips its rows, so the face draws no radius — an
 * inset rounded fill inside a bordered card reads as a card in a card — and it
 * takes the card's 16px inset so the fill runs edge to edge like every other
 * card row. */
.ds-provider-row--in-card > .ds-provider-row__face {
  padding-left: var(--sem-space-xl);
  padding-right: var(--sem-space-xl);
  border-radius: 0;
}

/* The brand mark's box. The row sizes the slot and never picks the mark: a
 * provider whose identity is a logo and one whose identity is a glyph must read
 * at one weight. 1px down so the mark's optical centre lands on the name's
 * cap height rather than its baseline. */
.ds-provider-row__mark {
  position: relative;
  flex: none;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: var(--sem-icon-size-lg);
  height: var(--sem-icon-size-lg);
  margin-top: 1px; /* ds-lint-allow: optical nudge, not a spacing step */
}

.ds-provider-row__mark > svg,
.ds-provider-row__mark > img {
  width: var(--sem-icon-size-lg);
  height: var(--sem-icon-size-lg);
}

/* A provider this machine does not have. It recedes — the mark by opacity
 * because it is an image, the name to `text.muted`, the ink the state line
 * under it already wears — so a scan down the list lands on what IS here and
 * the absent rows sit behind them. `text.muted` and not the step between:
 * one ink step (`text.default`) was too close to `text.primary` to read as
 * receded at all (owner ruling 2026-09-24). `text.muted` is the lowest ink
 * that still clears AA on this ground and on the hover fill, in both modes
 * (5.3:1 and 4.7:1 light, 6.8:1 and 6.5:1 dark); `text.subtle` does not.
 *
 * It is NOT a disabled state: every control on the row keeps working, and the
 * Install button a recessed row carries is the whole reason it is listed. And
 * it is never the only carrier of the fact — the state line still says "Not
 * installed" in words. */
.ds-provider-row--recessed .ds-provider-row__mark {
  opacity: 0.6;
  /* A glyph mark drawn in `currentColor` recedes to the name's ink too; a
   * full-colour logo recedes by the opacity alone. */
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
}

.ds-provider-row--recessed .ds-provider-row__name {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
}

/* `text.muted` falls under AA on the selected fill, so a selected row keeps the
 * full ink on its name whether or not it is recessed. */
.ds-provider-row--recessed.ds-provider-row--selected .ds-provider-row__name {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

/* The count docked on the mark's TOP-RIGHT: the badge component's corner
 * species, on a list row rather than on a rail square. The opposite corner
 * from the health mark, so a surface that draws both reads as two marks rather
 * than one smudge — though a list should be drawing one or the other (see
 * component.md, "One status idiom").
 *
 * The badge brings its own geometry and its own keyline; all this slot does is
 * establish that the corner belongs to the mark. */
.ds-provider-row__badge {
  /* The keyline in the ground this list actually sits on. The badge component
   * rings itself in the app ground by default, which is a different colour
   * here — the same override the app rail makes for its canvas. */
  border-color: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
}

/* Health, docked on the mark's corner: the tone's status mark
 * (components/status-dot — the glyph, never a dot) at 10px, on a small disc
 * of whatever fill is behind the row, ringed by a 2px keyline in the same
 * fill. Without the disc the brand mark shows through the glyph's ring and it
 * reads as a stain on the logo; with a ground hard-coded to the resting
 * surface it halos the moment the row takes its hover fill, so all three
 * fills are named.
 *
 * It is decorative by contract — the state line says the state in words. */
.ds-provider-row__health {
  position: absolute;
  top: -4px; /* ds-lint-allow: the mark overhangs its 22px brand mark by its own keyline */
  left: -4px; /* ds-lint-allow: the mark overhangs its 22px brand mark by its own keyline */
  display: flex;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
}

/* One step under the inline glyph size: a corner mark is subordinate to the
 * 22px brand mark it sits on. The shape still reads at 10px — that is what
 * the glyph vocabulary is drawn for. */
.ds-provider-row__health > .ds-status-dot {
  width: 10px;
  height: 10px;
}

/* In a card the resting ground is the raised tone; a disc in the app
 * surface's colour would halo on it. */
.ds-provider-row--in-card .ds-provider-row__health {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface-raised);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--sem-color-bg-surface-raised);
}

.ds-provider-row--disclosable > .ds-provider-row__face:hover .ds-provider-row__health {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
}

.ds-provider-row--selected .ds-provider-row__health {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--sem-color-bg-selected);
}

.ds-provider-row__text {
  flex: 1;
  min-width: 0;
}

/* Name and version are a baseline PAIR. Neither grows, so they stay adjacent
 * instead of the version drifting to the far edge on a row that carries no
 * trailing control. */
.ds-provider-row__line {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
}

.ds-provider-row__name {
  min-width: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  white-space: nowrap;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

/* Real `--version` output is not always a semver — `grok 0.2.114 (0c785038798)
 * [stable]`, or a whole sentence from GNU bash. Flex shrink is proportional to
 * content, so the long one absorbs nearly all of it and the name survives; the
 * 45% cap is the backstop against a one-letter name beside a sentence. */
.ds-provider-row__version {
  min-width: 0;
  max-width: 45%;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  white-space: nowrap;
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
}

/* One line of state, in words. Never a caption: it says what is true now, not
 * what the provider is for. */
.ds-provider-row__state {
  display: block;
  margin-top: 1px; /* ds-lint-allow: optical line pairing, not a spacing step */
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-default);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
}

/* Identifiers inside the state line — a path, an account, a binary name — read
 * mono, one step down so the data does not out-shout the words around it. */
.ds-provider-row__id {
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
}

.ds-provider-row__trail {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  flex: none;
  gap: var(--sem-space-md);
  margin-top: var(--sem-space-3xs);
}

/* The chevron is drawn at icon.size.xs and the button pads out around it to
 * size.hit-target-min. Drawn size and target size are different numbers: a
 * 13px glyph in a 17px button is a 17px target, which is under the floor. */
.ds-provider-row__disclosure {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: var(--sem-size-hit-target-min);
  height: var(--sem-size-hit-target-min);
  padding: 0;
  border: none;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-chip);
  background: none;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  cursor: pointer;
}

.ds-provider-row__disclosure:hover {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
}

.ds-provider-row__disclosure:focus-visible {
  outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
}

/* The chevron rotates rather than being swapped for a second glyph, so the eye
 * tracks one object. It is the only thing here that moves, so it is the only
 * thing the reduced-motion guard switches off — the state still reads from the
 * angle. */
.ds-provider-row__chevron {
  width: var(--sem-icon-size-xs);
  height: var(--sem-icon-size-xs);
  transition: rotate var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

.ds-provider-row__disclosure[aria-expanded='true'] .ds-provider-row__chevron {
  rotate: 180deg;
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .ds-provider-row__face,
  .ds-provider-row__chevron {
    transition: none;
  }
}

/* The expansion starts on the name's left edge: the face's own inset plus the
 * mark plus the gap. Disclosure, not navigation — the row above it keeps its
 * position and nothing else in the list moves. */
.ds-provider-row__detail {
  padding-right: var(--sem-space-md);
  padding-bottom: var(--sem-space-lg);
  padding-left: calc(var(--sem-space-md) + var(--sem-icon-size-lg) + var(--sem-space-lg));
}

/* Same sum from the card's wider inset, so the detail still opens on the
 * name's edge. */
.ds-provider-row--in-card > .ds-provider-row__detail {
  padding-right: var(--sem-space-xl);
  padding-left: calc(var(--sem-space-xl) + var(--sem-icon-size-lg) + var(--sem-space-lg));
}
components/provider-row/component.html (demo)
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8" />
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
<title>Provider row</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../../foundations/tokens.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="component.css" />
<!-- The corner health mark is the status-dot component's glyph. -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../status-dot/component.css" />
<!-- The trailing enablement control is the `switch` component, unchanged. Linked
     so this file also stands alone in a browser; the catalog inlines every
     component's CSS itself and drops this head. -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../switch/component.css" />
<!-- The corner count on a mark is the badge component, unchanged. -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../badge/component.css" />
<!-- The list card the in-card rows sit in is setting-row's, unchanged. -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../setting-row/component.css" />
<style>
  body {
    margin: 0;
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  }
  .demo-stage {
    padding: var(--sem-space-3xl);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  }
  .demo-label {
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-lg);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  }
  /* The section band above the list: title left, freshness meta and the controls
     that act on the whole list right. One chrome row, not two. */
  .demo-band {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-2xs);
    padding: 0 var(--sem-space-md);
  }
  .demo-band h2 {
    margin: 0 auto 0 0;
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-title);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-tight);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  }
  .demo-band .meta {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  }
  .demo-icobtn {
    display: grid;
    place-items: center;
    width: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
    height: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
    padding: 0;
    border: none;
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: none;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  .demo-icobtn:hover {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  }
  .demo-icobtn:focus-visible {
    outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
    outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
  }
  /* Stand-in for the real brand marks, which come from the product's own icon
     set. Two-letter mono monograms on the icon plate so every demo row reads at
     the weight a logo would. */
  .demo-mono-mark {
    display: grid;
    place-items: center;
    width: var(--sem-icon-size-lg);
    height: var(--sem-icon-size-lg);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-active);
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
  }
  .demo-detail {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
  }
  .demo-ghost {
    height: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
    padding: 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-default);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: none;
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    cursor: pointer;
  }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="demo-stage" data-mode="light">
  <p class="demo-label">
    Light — installed providers, one expanded, one with an update waiting, one
    absent and receded
  </p>

  <div class="demo-band">
    <h2>Agent CLIs</h2>
    <span class="meta">Checked 2m ago</span>
    <button type="button" class="demo-icobtn" aria-label="Install a CLI from a folder">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16">
        <path d="M12 5.5V18.5M5.5 12H18.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" />
      </svg>
    </button>
    <button type="button" class="demo-icobtn" aria-label="Re-check every CLI now">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16">
        <path
          d="M13.25 7.25A5.25 5.25 0 0 0 4.05 4.1L2.75 5.5m0 0H6m-3.25 0V2.25M2.75 8.75a5.25 5.25 0 0 0 9.2 3.15l1.3-1.4m0 0H10m3.25 0v3.25"
          stroke="currentColor"
          stroke-width="1.35"
          stroke-linecap="round"
          stroke-linejoin="round"
        />
      </svg>
    </button>
  </div>

  <!-- Healthy, versioned, switched on, closed. -->
  <div class="ds-provider-row ds-provider-row--disclosable">
    <div class="ds-provider-row__face">
      <span class="ds-provider-row__mark">
        <span class="demo-mono-mark">CL</span>
        <span aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__health"><span class="ds-status-dot ds-status-dot--good"></span></span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__text">
        <span class="ds-provider-row__line">
          <span class="ds-provider-row__name">Claude Code</span>
          <span class="ds-provider-row__version">2.1.220</span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-provider-row__state">
          Authenticated as <span class="ds-provider-row__id">you@example.com</span> · Max subscription
        </span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__trail">
        <button
          type="button"
          class="ds-provider-row__disclosure"
          aria-expanded="false"
          aria-controls="detail-claude"
          aria-label="Claude Code details"
        >
          <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__chevron">
            <path d="M4.5 6.5L8 10L11.5 6.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" />
          </svg>
        </button>
        <button type="button" role="switch" aria-checked="true" aria-label="Claude Code enabled" class="ds-switch">
          <span aria-hidden="true" class="ds-switch-thumb"></span>
        </button>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Expanded: the chevron flipped, the detail on the name's left edge. -->
  <div class="ds-provider-row ds-provider-row--disclosable">
    <div class="ds-provider-row__face">
      <span class="ds-provider-row__mark">
        <span class="demo-mono-mark">CX</span>
        <span aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__health"><span class="ds-status-dot ds-status-dot--good"></span></span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__text">
        <span class="ds-provider-row__line">
          <span class="ds-provider-row__name">Codex</span>
          <span class="ds-provider-row__version">codex-cli 0.146.0</span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-provider-row__state">
          Ready — <span class="ds-provider-row__id">/opt/homebrew/bin/codex</span>
        </span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__trail">
        <button
          type="button"
          class="ds-provider-row__disclosure"
          aria-expanded="true"
          aria-controls="detail-codex"
          aria-label="Codex details"
        >
          <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__chevron">
            <path d="M4.5 6.5L8 10L11.5 6.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" />
          </svg>
        </button>
        <button type="button" role="switch" aria-checked="true" aria-label="Codex enabled" class="ds-switch">
          <span aria-hidden="true" class="ds-switch-thumb"></span>
        </button>
      </span>
    </div>
    <div class="ds-provider-row__detail" id="detail-codex">
      <p class="demo-detail">The per-instance form that already exists: command override, models, credentials.</p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Enabled and unhealthy: the two axes disagreeing, which is legal. -->
  <div class="ds-provider-row ds-provider-row--disclosable">
    <div class="ds-provider-row__face">
      <span class="ds-provider-row__mark">
        <span class="demo-mono-mark">GK</span>
        <span aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__health"><span class="ds-status-dot ds-status-dot--danger"></span></span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__text">
        <span class="ds-provider-row__line">
          <span class="ds-provider-row__name">Grok Build</span>
          <span class="ds-provider-row__version">grok 0.2.114 (0c785038798) [stable]</span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-provider-row__state">Unavailable — startup timed out after 15s</span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__trail">
        <button type="button" class="ds-provider-row__disclosure" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="detail-grok" aria-label="Grok Build details">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__chevron">
            <path d="M4.5 6.5L8 10L11.5 6.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" />
          </svg>
        </button>
        <button type="button" role="switch" aria-checked="true" aria-label="Grok Build enabled" class="ds-switch">
          <span aria-hidden="true" class="ds-switch-thumb"></span>
        </button>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- An update waiting: the corner count on the mark, and no health mark — this
       list has picked the count as its one status idiom. The number is 1
       because the count on a ROW says which, not how many. -->
  <div class="ds-provider-row ds-provider-row--disclosable">
    <div class="ds-provider-row__face">
      <span class="ds-provider-row__mark">
        <span class="demo-mono-mark">CX</span>
        <span
          role="status"
          aria-label="Codex — update available: 0.153.4"
          class="ds-badge-count ds-badge-count--accent ds-badge-count--corner ds-provider-row__badge"
          >1</span
        >
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__text">
        <span class="ds-provider-row__line">
          <span class="ds-provider-row__name">Codex</span>
          <span class="ds-provider-row__version">codex-cli 0.153.3</span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-provider-row__state">
          Ready — <span class="ds-provider-row__id">/opt/homebrew/bin/codex</span>
        </span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__trail">
        <button type="button" class="ds-provider-row__disclosure" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="detail-codex-update" aria-label="Codex details">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__chevron">
            <path d="M4.5 6.5L8 10L11.5 6.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" />
          </svg>
        </button>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Definitively absent: recessed a contrast step, no version at all, and the
       one action the state earns. The Install button is at full weight — the row
       recedes, its controls do not. -->
  <div class="ds-provider-row ds-provider-row--recessed">
    <div class="ds-provider-row__face">
      <span class="ds-provider-row__mark">
        <span class="demo-mono-mark">CU</span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__text">
        <span class="ds-provider-row__line">
          <span class="ds-provider-row__name">Cursor</span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-provider-row__state">
          Not installed — no <span class="ds-provider-row__id">cursor-agent</span> on PATH
        </span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__trail">
        <button type="button" class="demo-ghost">Install</button>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Probe failed, which is NOT absence: no Install offered. -->
  <div class="ds-provider-row">
    <div class="ds-provider-row__face">
      <span class="ds-provider-row__mark">
        <span class="demo-mono-mark">KM</span>
        <span aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__health"><span class="ds-status-dot ds-status-dot--warn"></span></span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__text">
        <span class="ds-provider-row__line">
          <span class="ds-provider-row__name">Kimi Code</span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-provider-row__state">Availability unknown — the check did not complete</span>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Selected: a marketplace listing whose row drives a detail pane. Neutral
       health, because this surface has no probe to report. -->
  <div class="ds-provider-row ds-provider-row--selected">
    <div class="ds-provider-row__face">
      <span class="ds-provider-row__mark">
        <span class="demo-mono-mark">OC</span>
        <span aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__health"><span class="ds-status-dot"></span></span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__text">
        <span class="ds-provider-row__line">
          <span class="ds-provider-row__name">OpenCode</span>
          <span class="ds-provider-row__version">Version 4</span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-provider-row__state">Community — published by SST</span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__trail">
        <button type="button" class="demo-ghost">Get</button>
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- In a card: the same rows as a settings group. The band stays outside;
       the list card (setting-row) is the group's one edge; the rows drop their
       radius and take the card's inset. -->
  <div class="demo-band" style="margin-top: var(--sem-space-3xl)">
    <h2>Version control</h2>
  </div>
  <ul class="ds-setting-row-list" aria-label="Version control">
    <li class="ds-provider-row ds-provider-row--in-card">
      <div class="ds-provider-row__face">
        <span class="ds-provider-row__mark">
          <span class="demo-mono-mark">git</span>
          <span aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__health"><span class="ds-status-dot ds-status-dot--good"></span></span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-provider-row__text">
          <span class="ds-provider-row__line">
            <span class="ds-provider-row__name">Git</span>
            <span class="ds-provider-row__version">2.47.1</span>
          </span>
          <span class="ds-provider-row__state">Available</span>
        </span>
      </div>
    </li>
    <li class="ds-provider-row ds-provider-row--in-card ds-provider-row--disclosable">
      <div class="ds-provider-row__face">
        <span class="ds-provider-row__mark">
          <span class="demo-mono-mark">gh</span>
          <span aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__health"><span class="ds-status-dot ds-status-dot--warn"></span></span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-provider-row__text">
          <span class="ds-provider-row__line">
            <span class="ds-provider-row__name">GitHub</span>
            <span class="ds-provider-row__version">2.62.0</span>
          </span>
          <span class="ds-provider-row__state">Not authenticated — <span class="ds-provider-row__id">gh auth login</span></span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-provider-row__trail">
          <button
            type="button"
            class="ds-provider-row__disclosure"
            aria-expanded="false"
            aria-controls="detail-github-card"
            aria-label="GitHub details"
          >
            <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__chevron">
              <path d="M4.5 6.5L8 10L11.5 6.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" />
            </svg>
          </button>
        </span>
      </div>
    </li>
  </ul>
</div>

<div class="demo-stage" data-mode="dark">
  <p class="demo-label">Dark — the same rows</p>

  <div class="demo-band">
    <h2>Agent CLIs</h2>
    <span class="meta">Checked 2m ago</span>
    <button type="button" class="demo-icobtn" aria-label="Re-check every CLI now">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16">
        <path
          d="M13.25 7.25A5.25 5.25 0 0 0 4.05 4.1L2.75 5.5m0 0H6m-3.25 0V2.25M2.75 8.75a5.25 5.25 0 0 0 9.2 3.15l1.3-1.4m0 0H10m3.25 0v3.25"
          stroke="currentColor"
          stroke-width="1.35"
          stroke-linecap="round"
          stroke-linejoin="round"
        />
      </svg>
    </button>
  </div>

  <div class="ds-provider-row ds-provider-row--disclosable">
    <div class="ds-provider-row__face">
      <span class="ds-provider-row__mark">
        <span class="demo-mono-mark">CL</span>
        <span aria-hidden="true" class="ds-provider-row__health"><span class="ds-status-dot ds-status-dot--good"></span></span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__text">
        <span class="ds-provider-row__line">
          <span class="ds-provider-row__name">Claude Code</span>
          <span class="ds-provider-row__version">2.1.220</span>
        </span>
        <span class="ds-provider-row__state">
          Ready — <span class="ds-provider-row__id">/Users/you/.local/bin/claude</span>
        </span>
      </span>
      <span class="ds-provider-row__trail">

Row button

Light

Dark

The list ROW as a control: full width, left-aligned, content height, and its layout in its children.

It is the button family's full-bleed member, and it exists because the family had no such member. [button](../button/component.md) answers *a thing you press* — inline-flex … justify-center on a size.control.* step with a label weight of its own. [list-row](../list-row/component.md) answers *a worklist row* — a title, a supporting line, a trailing meta, revealed actions, at most four elements at rest. Between them sits the row that is neither: a rail entry with three stacked lines, a listbox option, a settings rail tab, a skill file path with a size on the end, a "New …" affordance.

A sweep of the consuming product on 2026-09-08 found forty of those, each a raw <button>, and every one of them started by cancelling four things the button base had decided: the ramp height, the centring, the font-weight, and the gap. In a utility-class stack that cancellation is not reliable — two justify-* or two h-* on one element are resolved by stylesheet order — so this is not a convenience wrapper. It is the shape stated once so it cannot be half-stated forty times.

Which to reach for. If the row is the worklist row list-row describes, use that. If the row is an option, a rail entry, a tab or a create affordance — or if its content is a composition rather than a title and a supporting line — use this.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Row | .ds-row-button | yes — always a <button> | | Density | --nav / --bleed / --flush | no — the default is the inset row | | Variant | --dashed | no — the create affordance | | Contents | — | yes, and they are the CALLER's: a glyph slot, one or more lines, a trailing gutter |

The component states no height, no justify-content, no font weight and no gap between the lines. Those are the composition, and the composition differs per surface; what does not differ is the width, the ground, the selection treatment, the focus ring and the disabled canon, which is the whole of what is here.

Variants

  • Default — no modifier. border.default-free, transparent, radius.overlay, space.xs/space.sm inset. The inset row inside a padded rail.
  • --dashed — a 1px dashed border.default and text.muted ink. The "New …" affordance, which the [list surface anatomy](../../foundations/principles.md) puts first and full width at the very top of every rail. This is the only dashed edge in the system, and the condition is load-bearing: the row is a place for a thing that does not exist yet. A dashed edge anywhere else is decoration.

Density

Four steps, and each is a statement about what the row TOUCHES.

| Density | Radius | Ground | Focus ring | For | |---|---|---|---|---| | row (default) | radius.overlay | its own | outset | an inset row in a padded rail | | --nav | radius.overlay | its own | outset | the sidebar's rhythm — a size.control.sm floor so a one-line door row matches the controls above it | | --bleed | none | its own | inset | a full-bleed row in a list that reaches its container's edges | | --flush | none | none | inset | one of two targets inside a wrapper that owns the fill |

Two rules produce that table, and neither is a preference:

  • A full-bleed row draws no radius. An inset rounded fill inside a padded surface reads as a card nested in a card, and every other row list in the system fills to its own inset instead (see [menu](../menu/component.md), which makes the same call for the same reason).
  • A full-bleed row takes the ring INWARD. The row touches its container's edge, so an outset ring at focus.ring-offset is clipped by it. This is the carve-out principles.md already names for a control that clips its own overflow.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Rest | Transparent (or the dashed edge), text.default ink | | Hover | bg.hover ground, ink lifts to text.primary. --flush lifts the ink only — the wrapper paints the ground | | Selected | bg.selected fill, ink at text.primary, and a 2px inset accent.primary edge. Hover is not applied while selected | | Focus-visible | The shared ring; inset at --bleed and --flush | | Disabled | 45% opacity, not-allowed, hover suppressed | | Unavailable | aria-disabled rather than disabled, same look, tab stop kept — for a row whose tooltip explains why it is off |

Why hover is excluded from a selected row rather than repainted over it. bg.hover sits *below* bg.selected on the surface ramp. A selected row that also took the hover step would go *darker* under the pointer in light mode and *lighter* in dark — either way it reads as the row letting go of the choice. Repainting it (hover:bg-selected next to hover:bg-hover) is two declarations of one property at equal specificity, which is settled by stylesheet order; the fix is that a selected row never receives the hover step at all.

Usage

  • The create affordance is --dashed, full width, at the very top. Never below the scroll, and never a second full-width control stacked above the search field (principles.md → Composition, The list surface).
  • One --selected row on screen per pane. In a rail → list → detail layout the other two panes drop to the resting tier, which the consuming app reaches through its data-selection-pane cascade rather than a second modifier here.
  • Do not add a hover shadow, a scale, or a border that appears. A row that changes size under the pointer moves every row after it.

Accessibility

  • Selection announces as aria-current, not aria-pressed. A list row is navigation — "this is the one you are looking at" — where a toggle is a switch you threw. The app rail's squares deliberately read the other way (aria-pressed for a tool whose surface is floating), and one row of a drawer disagreeing with the row above it is the defect that distinction prevents.
  • A row inside a listbox takes role="option" and aria-selected; the component passes both through untouched rather than inferring them.
  • The row forwards its ref, its data-* attributes, tabIndex, role and onContextMenu, because a rail drives roving focus by querying for its own hook and a group decides for itself where the tab stop is. A row primitive that swallowed those is why forty of these stayed raw elements.
  • Anything the row reveals on hover must also appear on keyboard focus.

Shipped implementation

src/renderer/src/components/ui/RowButton.tsx, exporting RowButton with density, variant and selected.

components/row-button/component.css
/* Row button — the list ROW as a control. Extracted from the shipped
 * `RowButton` primitive (src/renderer/src/components/ui/RowButton.tsx).
 *
 * It is the button family's full-bleed member: everything the sized buttons
 * decide — height, centring, label weight — belongs to the row's children here,
 * and what the component owns is the width, the ground, the selection canon and
 * the focus ring. */

.ds-row-button {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
  width: 100%;
  padding: var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-sm);
  border: none;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-overlay);
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  text-align: left;
  cursor: pointer;
  /* No height and no `justify-content`: the children are the layout. */
  transition:
    background-color var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard),
    color var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard),
    border-color var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

/* No `transform` press. A full-width row that shrank under the pointer would
 * visibly detach from the rows above and below it; its press is the fill. */

.ds-row-button:hover:not(:disabled):not([aria-current='true']) {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

/* Selection is the neutral fill, the ink lift and the inset edge — the same
 * three the list-row entry rules, so a rail row and a worklist row cannot
 * disagree. Hover is EXCLUDED above rather than repainted here: bg.hover sits
 * below bg.selected, so a selected row under the pointer would dim. */
.ds-row-button[aria-current='true'] {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
}

.ds-row-button:focus-visible {
  outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
}

.ds-row-button:disabled {
  cursor: not-allowed;
  opacity: 0.45;
}

/* nav — the sidebar's navigation rhythm. A one-line door row matches the
 * controls above it; a two-line row still grows past the floor. */
.ds-row-button--nav {
  min-height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
  padding: var(--sem-space-2xs) var(--sem-space-sm);
}

/* bleed — a full-bleed row in a list that reaches its container's edges. No
 * radius (an inset rounded fill inside a padded surface reads as a card in a
 * card) and an INSET ring, because an outset one is clipped by the edge the row
 * touches. */
.ds-row-button--bleed {
  border-radius: 0;
}

.ds-row-button--bleed:focus-visible,
.ds-row-button--flush:focus-visible {
  outline-offset: calc(-1 * var(--sem-focus-ring-offset));
}

/* flush — one of two targets inside a wrapper that owns the fill and the
 * radius. It draws no ground in any state; a second one would be a box in a box. */
.ds-row-button--flush {
  border-radius: 0;
}

.ds-row-button--flush:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

/* dashed — the "New …" affordance at the head or foot of a rail: the first part
 * of the list-surface anatomy. The one dashed edge in the system, and it earns
 * it — the row is a PLACE for a thing that does not exist yet, and a solid edge
 * would make it look like the first item in the list. */
.ds-row-button--dashed {
  border: 1px dashed var(--sem-color-border-default);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
}

Scope pill

Light — the granted set, wrapping as a group of objects rather than as a sentence.

Granted scopes

  • workspace:read
  • workspace:operate
  • backlog:read
  • backlog:operate

Not granted

  • conversation:read
  • conversation:operate

A single pill inline, at rest. There is no other state.

conversation:operate

Dark — the same pills from the same tokens.

Granted scopes

  • workspace:read
  • workspace:operate
  • backlog:read
  • backlog:operate

Not granted

  • conversation:read
  • conversation:operate

A single pill inline, at rest. There is no other state.

conversation:operate

One machine-readable scope name in a pill: conversation:operate, workspace:read. It is the mark for a permission identifier wherever the product shows the person the actual strings — the pairing code's grant list, the popover that says what a paired machine may do here, the request a peer sent.

Set in mono, at font.size.micro, on radius.pill with a border.default hairline and a bg.surface ground. 22px tall, space.sm of inline padding. Display only, always.

Why neither existing mark could be it

Read [badge](../badge/component.md) and [micro-chip](../micro-chip/component.md) first; this entry exists because both were tried and both were wrong for the same underlying reason.

They are UI-face labels. This is code. A badge says "draft", "merged", "3". A micro chip says "Default". Those are words *about* the thing beside them, written in the reader's language, in the UI family, in sentence case. A scope pill's content is not a word about anything — it is the identifier, the same string that appears in the pairing request, in the audit line, and in the conversation:read a person will paste into a search box or an issue. Three consequences follow, and each of them is a rule one of those two components holds the other way:

| | badge | micro-chip | scope pill | |---|---|---|---| | Family | UI | UI | mono | | Tone | status.*-soft fills, a tone per state | none, permanently | none, permanently | | Shape | radius.pill | radius.chip (rectangular, explicitly) | radius.pill | | Content | a state word or a count | one fact, one or two words | an API identifier | | Tracking | — | tracking.wide | tracking.normal |

  • The family is not a style choice here. conversation:operate at 11px in the UI family is exactly where l / 1 / I and : / ; stop being distinguishable, and a person reading this list is deciding what another machine may do on this one. Mono is what makes the string checkable.
  • It can never take a tone, which rules out the badge family outright: the badge's whole vocabulary is status.*-soft fills that grade a state, and a scope has no state. It is held or it is not, and *that* is said by the heading above the set, not by a colour on the pill.
  • It is a pill, and micro-chip hands the rectangle back on purpose — that entry quotes badge's ruling that "radius.chip is the right token for a *rectangular* chip". A wrapped set of six colon-joined strings needs the round end to read as six objects rather than as one broken line; the rectangle at that density reads as a table with no rules.

The shortest form of the test: reach for a badge when the mark would change, for a micro chip when it would not, and for this when the mark is not a word at all.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Pill | .ds-scope-pill | yes — an inline <span> (or an <li> inside a set) holding exactly one scope name | | Set | .ds-scope-pill-set | no — the wrapping container, space.xs in both axes |

No glyph slot, no dismiss affordance, no count, no truncation. A pill holds one identifier and the whole of it: a scope shown as conversation:op… is a scope that does not exist.

Variants

  • Granted (no modifier). border.default, text.default, bg.surface. The default, because the common list is the list of what a machine *has*.
  • --missing. One step quieter on both axes — border.subtle and text.subtle — for a scope listed as *not* granted beside the ones that are. It is deliberately not a status.danger tint: a scope the person never granted is a fact, not a fault, and tinting it red would say the opposite of what the surface means. The difference is shape-coded by the heading the set sits under ("Granted scopes" / "Not granted"); the ink step alone is never the only carrier.
  • No tone variants, ever. See above. A scope pill that went green would be a second status idiom on a surface whose whole content is already a permission state.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Rest | The only state | | Hover / focus / pressed | None. It is not interactive and must not advertise a click it does not have | | Inside a hovered row | Unchanged — the row paints bg.hover behind it; the pill's own bg.surface ground is what keeps the identifier legible over it | | Disabled | Not a state this has. A pill in a disabled region dims with the region |

Usage

  • One scope per pill, and the pill never truncates. A set that does not fit wraps to another line. If the surface cannot afford the wrap, it is showing too many scopes and wants the popover's mono list instead.
  • Use a set, not a sentence. Comma-joining scopes into prose is what this replaces: the reader is counting and comparing, and prose defeats both.
  • The heading carries the meaning, the pill carries the name. "Granted scopes" over a set; "Not granted" over a --missing set. Never a pill that tries to say both, and never a mixed set where held and unheld sit together separated only by ink.
  • Never interactive. No onClick, no dismiss ✕, no filter behaviour. A scope a person can act on is a [check row](../check-row/component.md) — that is what the pairing dialog uses — or a [button](../button/component.md). The pill is what the choice looks like once it has been made.
  • Not a general-purpose mono chip. It is named for what it holds. A commit SHA, a branch name and a file path are not scopes; if one of those wants a mark, that is a new entry with its own argument, not this one widened.

Accessibility

  • Plain text in the document, read in the surface's reading order. It takes no role and no aria-label: the identifier is the content, and naming it would say the same string twice.
  • The set takes the accessible name, not the pill. A <ul class="ds-scope-pill-set"> with an aria-label ("Scopes in this code") is what tells a screen-reader user what the six strings underneath it are; without it they arrive as six unexplained identifiers.
  • --missing is never announced by its colour. The heading above the set is the only thing that says "not granted", and it is real text, so the quieter ink is reinforcement rather than information.
  • text.default on bg.surface clears AA at the 11px step, and the hairline gives the pill a non-text edge at 3:1. The --missing step keeps its hairline for the same reason: the mark survives greyscale because it never depended on a colour.
  • Never focusable, and it adds no tab stop to a surface that is already a popover or a card.

Shipped implementation

src/renderer/src/components/ui/ScopePill.tsx, exporting ScopePill and ScopePillSet through the kit barrel (ui/index.ts).

components/scope-pill/component.css
/* Scope pill — one machine-readable scope name, shown as a thing the reader can
 * count and compare rather than as prose.
 *
 * The pairing code's grant list is the surface it was drawn for: six names
 * like `conversation:operate` that the person is being asked to hand to another
 * machine. They are API strings, they are the strings that appear in the
 * request, in the audit line and in the popover that says what a machine may
 * do here — so they are set in mono and the pill's job is to make each one one
 * OBJECT, countable at a glance, wrapping as a set rather than as a sentence.
 *
 * Why it is neither of the two marks the system already has. `badge` and
 * `micro-chip` are UI-FACE labels: a word in the reader's language ("draft",
 * "merged", "Default"), sentence case, set in the UI family, sized to trail a
 * row's title. This is code — a colon-joined identifier the reader will search
 * for and quote — and a code string in the UI family at 11px is the one place
 * `l`, `1` and `I` stop being distinguishable. It also takes no tone and never
 * will (badge's whole vocabulary is tone), and it is a pill rather than the
 * rectangle micro-chip explicitly claims. Three differences, one cause: the
 * content is not a word about the thing, it IS the thing. */

.ds-scope-pill {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  /* Never shrinks: a wrapped SET of pills is the reading, and a pill that
     truncated its own identifier would be showing a scope that does not
     exist. The container wraps; the pill does not. */
  flex: none;
  /* 22px — the sub-control box step the button family already uses for its
     smallest square. Deliberately NOT a control step: the smallest of those is
     26px and it means "a person can press this", which this cannot be. A
     `min-height` rather than a `height`, so a pill in a zoomed or
     larger-text context grows with its line box instead of clipping it. */
  min-height: var(--sem-icon-size-lg);
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
  border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-default);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-pill);
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-regular);
  /* No `tracking-wide`: the UI-face marks open their letter-spacing to make a
     small word breathe, and opening a mono string's tracking un-does the one
     thing mono is for — the column grid that makes `:` and `_` findable. */
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-normal);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-default);
  white-space: nowrap;
}

/* The set. Pills wrap as a group and never as a paragraph: the gap is the same
 * in both axes so a two-row set reads as a grid of objects rather than as a
 * run-on line that happened to break. */
.ds-scope-pill-set {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}

/* Missing — a scope that is NOT granted, listed beside the ones that are. One
 * step of ink and one step of border, and nothing else: the difference between
 * held and not-held is a matter of fact, not of danger, and a `status.danger`
 * tint here would tell the reader that a scope they never granted is a
 * problem. Shape-coded too, by the heading it sits under, because a colour
 * step alone is not a state. */
.ds-scope-pill--missing {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
}

A titled region of a panel or pane: a one-line heading row — title, optional canonical count, at most one trailing control — over its content. Extracted from the source product's Section (src/renderer/src/components/ui/Section.tsx).

A section groups with space and a heading, which is the system's answer before any container: no card, no fill, no border box around the content. If the content genuinely needs containment, that is a different decision made for a stated reason — not this component growing chrome.

One such reason is on the record: a run of [setting-row](../setting-row/component.md)s takes a bordered card, because a settings page's groups are long enough that the gap between two groups and the gap between two rows become the same gap. The card belongs to that component, not to this one — the section still contributes only its title, which sits *outside* the card and keeps the typography specified here. principles.md, *Hairlines carry the structure*, ruling 2026-09-14.

A heading must separate something from something else. One section alone on a surface is not a group; render its content bare and let the surface's own name (the panel title, the list's accessible name) carry the label. The title is optional for exactly this case — a section with no title is just the padding contract.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Region | .ds-section | yes — a real <section> | | Header row | .ds-section-header | when titled — baseline-aligned, space.sm gap | | Heading cluster | .ds-section-heading | with the header — title + count, space.xs gap, shrinks first | | Title | .ds-section-title | with the header — an <h2>–<h4>, truncates | | Count | .ds-section-count | no — tabular-nums, text.muted | | Action | .ds-section-action | no — one trailing control | | Body | .ds-section-body | yes — the content, inset unless --flush |

The title is font.size.meta at font.weight.emphasis in text.primary — a weighted label, never uppercase letter-spaced chrome. Sentence case. The heading element's level (h2–h4) follows the document outline, not the type size: every section title renders identically whatever its level.

The header's padding (space.lg sides and top, space.xs below) and the body's inset (space.lg sides and bottom) share one left edge, so the title and its content sit on the same vertical line.

Variants

  • Default — body inset to the section's padding.
  • ds-section--flush — no body inset, for content that brings its own edge contract: a list whose rows own full-width hover fills, a table, a divider stack. The header keeps its padding either way.
  • ds-section--flush-header — the body inset drops and so does the header's, so the title, the count and a trailing control share the rows' left edge. Added 2026-09-02: --flush alone leaves the heading 12px inboard of rows that render flush to x=0, which reads as a misalignment rather than a hierarchy. Reach for it only when the body's rows genuinely have no inset of their own — a list of inbox-rows carries its own, and the header must stay inset to line up with it.

States

None. A section is structure, not a control — it has no hover, no selection, no disabled. Interactive states belong to the things inside it.

Usage

  • One trailing control, and a ceiling of one. A "New…" button, a filter glyph, an overflow menu — one of them. Two controls in a section header is the second chrome band forming; the second control belongs inside the content, behind the overflow, or nowhere.
  • The count is the canonical count, shown once. If the content below also numbers itself, one of the two goes — the same count in two places is two chances to disagree.
  • The count states fact, not activity: it does not pulse, tint, or turn into a badge. A count that needs attention semantics is a status, and statuses belong on the rows that have them.
  • Do not nest a titled section directly inside a titled section with no intervening content — that is two headings labelling one thing. Nested sections are legal when each genuinely separates groups; step the heading level (h3 → h4), never the type.
  • Sections stack with space between them, not rules. A divider between every section restates what the headings already say.

Accessibility

  • The region is a native <section>; give it aria-labelledby pointing at the title's id when the surface holds several, so the regions are navigable landmarks with names.
  • The title is a real heading element at the level the document outline requires — assistive tech navigates by outline, and a <div> styled as a heading is invisible to that.
  • The count is part of the section's announced name only when it matters; it is text, not an aria-label — screen readers read it in place.
  • The trailing action is a normally-focusable control in source order after the title, so Tab reads title-then-action, matching the visual order.

Known drift

Shipped Section.tsx matches this spec structurally (it is the source of it); its paddings are written as Tailwind steps (px-3, pt-3, pb-1.5) that land on the space scale's 12px and 6px but bypass the variables. Token canon: space.lg and space.xs.

components/section/component.css
/* Section — a titled region of a panel: heading row (title, canonical count,
 * at most one trailing control) over its content
 * (src/renderer/src/components/ui/Section.tsx).
 *
 * Structure, not a control: it groups with space and a heading — no card, no
 * fill, no border box, no divider between stacked sections. */

.ds-section {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
}

/* Baseline alignment, so the title, the count, and a text action share one
 * line whatever their sizes. */
.ds-section-header {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
  padding: var(--sem-space-lg) var(--sem-space-lg) var(--sem-space-xs);
}

.ds-section-heading {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
  min-width: 0;
}

/* A weighted label, never uppercase letter-spaced chrome. The element is
 * h2–h4 per the document outline; the rendering never changes with it. */
.ds-section-title {
  margin: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  white-space: nowrap;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

/* The canonical count, stated once. Fact, not activity: it never pulses,
 * tints, or becomes a badge. */
.ds-section-count {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
}

/* One trailing control — a ceiling, not a suggestion. */
.ds-section-action {
  flex: none;
}

/* Body shares the header's left edge, so title and content sit on one line. */
.ds-section-body {
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-lg) var(--sem-space-lg);
}

/* Flush body, for content that owns its own edges (full-bleed list rows, a
 * table). The header keeps its padding either way. */
.ds-section--flush .ds-section-body {
  padding: 0;
}

Segmented control

Light — arrow keys move the selection itself; the group is one tab stop. The last strip is --icon-only: the label is still there, as each segment's aria-label. Its other half, the tooltip, is the `tooltip` component in the consuming framework — never a native `title`, which this system does not put on a control.
